bukhari||1444: Hanzala said, on the authority of Tawus: "Two shields." And Al-Laith said: Ja'far narrated to me, from Ibn Hurmuz: I heard Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him) narrate from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Two shields."
bukhari||487: And that ‘Abdullah told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to alight beneath a huge tree short of Ar-Ruwaitha, on the right side of the road, facing the road, in a flat sandy place, until it opens out from a hillock a little short of the postal station of Ar-Ruwaitha by two miles. Its top had broken and bent over into its interior, while it stood on its trunk, and on its trunk there were many stumps.
bukhari||490: And that 'Abdullah bin 'Umar told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to alight in the valley which is at the lower part of Marr-az-Zahran, towards Medina, when he descended from As-Safrawat; he used to alight in the bottom of that valley, on the left side of the road as one goes to Mecca. There was no more than a stone's throw between the alighting place of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and the road.
bukhari||485: And that Abdullah bin Umar told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed at the place where the small mosque is, which is on this side of the mosque that is at Sharaf-ar-Rauha; and Abdullah used to know the place where the Prophet (ﷺ) had prayed, and he used to say: It is there, on your right, when you stand in the mosque to pray, and that mosque is on the edge of the road, on the right, as you go to Makkah; between it and the greater mosque there is a distance of a stone's throw or so.
bukhari||489: And that `Abdullah bin `Umar told him that Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alighted near some trees to the left of the road, in a watercourse below Harsha; that watercourse being adjacent to the foot of Harsha, between it and the road being about a bowshot's distance; and `Abdullah used to pray facing a tree which was the nearest of those trees to the road and was the tallest of them.
bukhari||488: And that 'Abdullah bin 'Umar told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) had prayed at the edge of a small valley beyond Al-'Arj, on the way to a hill, near that mosque, (where) there are two or three graves with a heap of stones over the graves, on the right side of the road, near the small trees of the road, among those small trees. 'Abdullah used to depart from Al-'Arj after the sun had passed the meridian at midday, and would pray the Zuhr prayer in that mosque.
bukhari||486: And that Ibn 'Umar used to pray facing the vein (ridge) that is at the departure point of Ar-Rawha', and that vein's end is at the edge of the road, short of the mosque that lies between it and the departure point, as you are going towards Mecca. A mosque had been built there, but 'Abdullah did not pray in that mosque; he used to leave it on his left and behind him, and pray in front of it, facing the vein itself. 'Abdullah used to set off from Ar-Rawha', and would not pray Zuhr until he reached that place, where he would pray Zuhr. And when returning from Mecca, if he passed by it an hour before dawn or in the last part of the night, he would stop and rest there until he prayed Fajr at that place.
bukhari||491: And that Abdullah bin Umar told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to stop at Dhi Tuwa and spend the night there till morning, and he would offer the Fajr prayer when he came to Mecca. The place where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray was on a rugged hillock, not in the mosque that was later built there, but lower than that, on a rugged hillock.
bukhari||492: And that 'Abdullah told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) faced the two openings of the mountain which lay between him and the tall mountain, towards the Ka'bah, and he placed the mosque which was built there to the left of the mosque at the edge of the hillock, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) place of prayer was below it, on the black hillock, leaving about ten cubits or so from the hillock; then one would pray facing the two openings of the mountain which lay between him and the Ka'bah.
bukhari||4910: Sulaiman bin Harb and Abu An-Nu'man said: Hammad bin Zaid narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: I was in a gathering which included 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Laila, whose companions used to hold him in great esteem. The topic of the later of the two term-periods (i.e., 'Idda) was mentioned, so I narrated the Hadith of Subai'a bint Al-Harith, on the authority of 'Abdullah bin 'Utba. Some of his companions then frowned at me disapprovingly. Muhammad said: I noticed this, so I said, "I would indeed be daring if I were to tell a lie about 'Abdullah bin 'Utba while he is still present in a part of Kufa." So he (i.e., 'Abdur-Rahman) felt ashamed and said, "But his uncle did not say that." So I met Abu 'Atiyya Malik bin 'Amir and asked him about it, and he began narrating to me the Hadith of Subai'a. I asked him, "Did you hear anything from 'Abdullah concerning this matter?" He replied, "We were with 'Abdullah when he said: 'Do you apply the stricter ruling to her case but do not apply the more lenient one? Indeed, the shorter Surah of An-Nisa' (i.e., Surat At-Talaq) was revealed after the longer one (i.e., Surat An-Nisa'), (and it states): "And for those who are pregnant, their term (of 'Idda) is until they deliver their burden."'"
muslim||116: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaibah, Muhammad bin al-Muthanna, and Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us - and their wordings are close to one another - Abu Bakr said: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah; the other two said: Muhammad bin Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Jamrah, who said: I used to interpret between Ibn Abbas and the people. A woman came to him asking about the nabidh (steeped drink) of the jar, and he said: The delegation of Abd al-Qais came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is the delegation," or "Who are the people?" They said: Rabi'ah. He said: "Welcome to the people," or "to the delegation, neither disgraced nor regretful." He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, we come to you from a distant land, and between us and you lies this tribe of the disbelievers of Mudar, and we are unable to come to you except in the sacred month, so command us with a decisive matter that we may inform those behind us of it, by which we may enter Paradise. He said: So he commanded them with four things and forbade them from four things. He said: He commanded them to believe in Allah alone, and said: "Do you know what belief in Allah is?" They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: "The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakah, the fasting of Ramadan, and that you give a fifth of the spoils of war." And he forbade them from ad-dubba' (gourd vessels), al-hantam (green jars), and al-muzaffat (pitch-coated vessels) - Shu'bah said: and sometimes he said an-naqir (hollowed-out wood vessels) - Shu'bah said: and sometimes he said al-muqayyar (pitch-coated vessels) - and he said: "Memorize it and inform those behind you of it." And Abu Bakr said in his narration: "those behind you," and al-muqayyar is not in his narration.
muslim||416: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, [saying]: Ibn Abi Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik - he [Qatadah] perhaps said: from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man from his (Anas's) people - who said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While I was at the House (the Ka'bah), between sleep and wakefulness, I heard someone saying: 'One of the three between the two men.' Then I was approached and taken away, and I was brought a golden basin containing water of Zamzam, and my chest was split open to such-and-such [point]." Qatadah said: "So I said to the one who was with me: 'What does he mean?' He said: 'To the lower part of his belly.'" [The Prophet continued]: "Then my heart was taken out and washed with the water of Zamzam, then it was put back in its place, then it was filled with faith and wisdom. Then I was brought a white animal, called al-Buraq, above a donkey and below a mule, whose stride reached as far as its eye could see. I was mounted upon it, and we set off until we reached the lowest heaven. Gabriel (peace be upon him) asked for the gate to be opened, and it was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' So it was opened for us, and it was said: 'Welcome to him, and what an excellent coming he has made.'" He said: "Then we came to Adam (peace be upon him)," and he continued the account with its story, and mentioned that in the second heaven he met Jesus and John (peace be upon them), and in the third Joseph, and in the fourth Idris, and in the fifth Aaron - Allah's blessings be upon them. He said: "Then we set off until we reached the sixth heaven, and I came to Moses (peace be upon him) and greeted him, and he said: 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.' When I passed by him, he wept, and it was called out to him: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'O Lord, this is a young man whom You sent after me, and more of his followers will enter Paradise than of my followers.'" He said: "Then we set off until we reached the seventh heaven, and I came to Abraham." And in the hadith it is said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) related that he saw four rivers, from whose source two rivers flow outward and two rivers flow within. I said: "O Gabriel, what are these rivers?" He said: "As for the two hidden rivers, they are two rivers in Paradise, and as for the two visible ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates." Then the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) was raised up for me, and I said: "O Gabriel, what is this?" He said: "This is the Frequented House; seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and when they leave it they never return to it again - that is their last time in it." Then I was brought two vessels, one containing wine and the other milk, and they were presented to me, and I chose the milk, and it was said: "You have chosen rightly; Allah will guide your nation to be upon the natural disposition (al-fitrah) through you." Then fifty prayers each day were made obligatory upon me. Then he continued the story to the end of the hadith.
muslim||475:
Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn Al-Jahdari and Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Al-Ghubari narrated to us, and the wording is that of Abu Kamil, who said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be distressed by that" - and Ibn 'Ubayd said: "and they will be inspired by that" - "so they will say: If only we could seek intercession with our Lord so that He might relieve us from this place of ours. So they will go to Adam (peace be upon him) and say: You are Adam, the father of mankind. Allah created you with His hand and breathed into you from His spirit, and commanded the angels and they prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord so that He may relieve us from this place of ours. He will say: I am not fit for that position, and he will mention the sin that he committed, and he will feel too ashamed before his Lord because of it. But go to Noah, the first messenger that Allah sent. So they will go to Noah (peace be upon him), and he will say: I am not fit for that position, and he will mention the sin that he committed, and he will feel too ashamed before his Lord because of it. But go to Abraham (peace be upon him), whom Allah took as an intimate friend. So they will go to Abraham (peace be upon him), and he will say: I am not fit for that position - and he will mention the sin that he committed, and he will feel too ashamed before his Lord because of it. But go to Moses (peace be upon him), to whom Allah spoke directly and gave him the Torah. So they will go to Moses (peace be upon him), and he will say: I am not fit for that position - and he will mention the sin that he committed, and he will feel too ashamed before his Lord because of it. But go to Jesus, the spirit of Allah and His word. So they will go to Jesus, the spirit of Allah and His word, and he will say: I am not fit for that position, but go to Muhammad (may peace be upon him), a servant whose past and future sins have been forgiven."

The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "So they will come to me, and I will ask permission from my Lord, and permission will be granted to me. When I see Him, I will fall down prostrating, and He will leave me thus for as long as He wishes. Then it will be said: O Muhammad, raise your head; speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with praise that my Lord will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, so I will bring them out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise. Then I will return and fall down prostrating, and He will leave me thus for as long as He wishes to leave me. Then it will be said: Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, so I will bring them out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise." He said: "I do not know whether it was the third or the fourth time - he said: So I will say: O my Lord, none remains in the Fire except those whom the Qur'an has confined" - meaning, for whom eternal dwelling has become binding. Ibn 'Ubayd said in his version: Qatadah said: meaning, for whom eternal dwelling has become binding.
muslim||411: Shaiban bin Farrukh narrated to us, Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas bin Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "I was brought al-Buraq, which is an animal white [in colour], tall, larger than a donkey but smaller than a mule, who would place his hoof at the furthest extent of his sight. So I mounted him until I came to Bait al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). I tied him to the ring to which the Prophets tie [their mounts]. Then I entered the mosque and prayed in it two rak'ahs, then went out, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Gabriel said: 'You have chosen the natural inclination (al-Fitrah).' Then he ascended with us to heaven, and Gabriel sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Adam, and he welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then he ascended with us to the second heaven, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with the two cousins, Jesus son of Mary and John son of Zachariah, peace be upon them both, and they welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then he ascended with me to the third heaven, and Gabriel sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad, may peace be upon him.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Joseph, peace be upon him, and he had been given half of [all] beauty. He welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then he ascended with us to the fourth heaven, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Idris, and he welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Allah, Mighty and Sublime, said: 'And We raised him to a lofty station' (19:57). Then he ascended with us to the fifth heaven, and Gabriel sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Aaron, peace be upon him, and he welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then he ascended with us to the sixth heaven, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Moses, peace be upon him, and he welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then he ascended to the seventh heaven, and Gabriel sought that it be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad, may peace be upon him.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Abraham, peace be upon him, leaning his back against al-Bait al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House), into which seventy thousand angels enter every day, never to return to it again. Then he took me to Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary), and its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and its fruit was like large water-jars. When it was overcome by what overcame it from the command of Allah, it changed, and none among the creation of Allah is able to describe it due to its beauty. So Allah revealed to me what He revealed, and He made obligatory upon me fifty prayers every day and night. Then I descended to Moses, peace be upon him, and he said: 'What has your Lord made obligatory upon your ummah?' I said: 'Fifty prayers.' He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your ummah will not be able to bear that. Indeed, I tried the Children of Israel and tested them.' So I returned to my Lord and said: 'O Lord, make it lighter for my ummah.' So He removed five from me. I returned to Moses and said: 'He has removed five from me.' He said: 'Indeed your ummah will not be able to bear that; return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction.' So I kept going back and forth between my Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, and Moses, peace be upon him, until He said: 'O Muhammad, they are five prayers every day and night, for each prayer ten [rewards], so that makes fifty prayers [in reward]. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, it is recorded for him as one good deed, and if he does it, it is recorded for him as ten. And whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is recorded against him, but if he does it, it is recorded as one evil deed.' Then I descended until I reached Moses, peace be upon him, and informed him, and he said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction.'" The Messenger of Allah, may peace be upon him, said: "So I said: 'I have returned to my Lord until I feel ashamed before Him.'"
muslim||532: Uthman b. Abu Shaiba al-Absi narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, will say: O Adam! And he will say: Here I am at Your service, and at Your beck and call, and all good is in Your hands. He will say: Bring forth the delegation of Hell-fire. He (Adam) will say: What is the delegation of Hell-fire? He will say: Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. He (the Prophet) said: That is when the small child will become gray-haired, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as if drunk, though they are not drunk, but the punishment of Allah is severe." He (the narrator) said: This was very hard on them, so they said: O Messenger of Allah, which of us will be that man? He said: "Rejoice, for indeed of Ya'juj and Ma'juj there will be a thousand, and of you there will be one man." He then said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." So we praised Allah and glorified Him. Then he said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." So we praised Allah and glorified Him. Then he said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Your likeness among the nations is like the likeness of a white hair on the skin of a black bull, or like a spot on the foreleg of a donkey."
muslim||451:
Zuhair b. Harb narrated to me: Ya'qub b. Ibrahim narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ata' b. Yazid al-Laythi, that Abu Hurairah informed him: that some people said to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him): O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: Do you have any doubt about seeing the moon on a night when it is full? They said: No, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Do you have any doubt about seeing the sun when there is no cloud over it? They said: No, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Then you shall see Him in like manner. Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection and say: Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it. So he who used to worship the sun will follow the sun, and he who used to worship the moon will follow the moon, and he who used to worship the false gods will follow the false gods. This Ummah will then remain, with its hypocrites among it. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will come to them in a form other than the form which they know, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from you. This is our place until our Lord comes to us; when our Lord comes to us, we shall recognize Him. Then Allah, Exalted, will come to them in the form which they know, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: You are our Lord, and they will follow Him. Then a bridge will be laid across the middle of Hell, and I and my Ummah will be the first to cross it. No one will speak on that day except the Messengers, and the plea of the Messengers on that day will be: O Allah, save, save! In Hell there are hooks like the thorns of the sa'dan plant - have you seen the sa'dan? They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: They are like the thorns of the sa'dan, except that no one knows how huge they are except Allah. They will snatch people according to their deeds; some of them will be [saved but scarred] remaining because of their deeds, and some will be cut to pieces and fall down [into Hell] but will [later] be saved. When Allah has finished judging between His servants, and wishes to bring out of Hell, by His mercy, whomever He wishes, He will command the angels to bring out of the Fire whoever did not associate anything with Allah, of those whom Allah wished to show mercy, of those who used to say: There is no god but Allah. The angels will recognize them in the Fire by the mark of prostration; the Fire consumes every part of the son of Adam except the mark of prostration, for Allah has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration. So they will be brought out of the Fire, having been burnt to charcoal, and the water of life will be poured upon them, and they will sprout as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood. Then Allah will finish judging between His servants, and there will remain one man facing Hell, who will be the last of the people of Paradise to enter it. He will say: O my Lord, turn my face away from the Fire, for its smell has poisoned me and its flame has burned me. He will keep supplicating Allah as long as Allah wills that he should supplicate. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say: If I do that for you, will you then ask for something else? He will say: I shall not ask You for anything else. And he will give his Lord whatever pledges and covenants Allah wills. So Allah will turn his face away from the Fire. When he turns toward Paradise and sees it, he will remain silent for as long as Allah wills him to remain silent, then he will say: O my Lord, bring me nearer to the gate of Paradise. Allah will say to him: Did you not give your pledges and covenants that you would not ask Me for anything other than what I gave you? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are! He will say: O my Lord, and he will keep supplicating Allah until He says to him: If I grant you that, will you then ask for something else? He will say: No, by Your might. So he will give his Lord whatever pledges and covenants Allah wills, and He will bring him nearer to the gate of Paradise. When he stands at the gate of Paradise, it will open wide before him, and he will see what is in it of blessings and joy, and he will remain silent for as long as Allah wills him to remain silent. Then he will say: O my Lord, let me enter Paradise. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say to him: Did you not give your pledges and covenants that you would not ask for anything other than what you were given? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are! He will say: O my Lord, let me not be the most wretched of Your creatures. He will keep supplicating Allah until Allah, Blessed and Exalted, laughs at him, and when Allah laughs at him, He will say: Enter Paradise. When he enters it, Allah will say to him: Wish for something. He will ask his Lord and wish, until Allah reminds him of this and that, until when his wishes are exhausted, Allah, Exalted, will say: That is for you, and the like of it besides.

'Ata' b. Yazid said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri was with Abu Hurairah and did not contradict any part of his account, until when Abu Hurairah narrated that Allah said to that man: "and the like of it besides," Abu Sa'id said: "and ten times as much besides," O Abu Hurairah. Abu Hurairah said: I only remembered his saying, "That is for you, and the like of it besides." Abu Sa'id said: I bear witness that I remembered from the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) his saying, "That is for you, and ten times as much besides." Abu Hurairah said: And that man will be the last of the people of Paradise to enter it.
muslim||480:
Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah and Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Numair narrated to us - and they agreed in the wording of the hadith, except that one of them added a word here and there beyond the other - they said: Muhammad bin Bishr narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurairah, who said:

"One day meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the forearm was raised up to him, for it was something he liked. He took a bite from it, then said: 'I am the leader of the people on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why that is? Allah will gather the first and the last of mankind on the Day of Resurrection on a single plain, so that the caller can be heard by all of them and the eye can see all of them, and the sun will draw near, and the people will be overcome by such distress and anguish as they cannot bear or endure. Some people will say to others: Do you not see the condition you are in? Do you not see what has befallen you? Should you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord? So some people will say to others: Go to Adam. So they will come to Adam and say: O Adam, you are the father of mankind; Allah created you with His own hand and breathed into you of His spirit, and commanded the angels and they prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the condition we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Adam will say: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. He forbade me from the tree, and I disobeyed Him. Myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Noah. So they will come to Noah and say: O Noah, you are the first of the Messengers sent to the earth, and Allah named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the condition we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? He will say to them: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. I had a supplication which I made against my people. Myself, myself! Go to Abraham, peace be upon him. So they will come to Abraham and say: You are the Prophet of Allah and His close friend among the people of the earth. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the condition we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Abraham will say to them: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again - and he will mention his lies. Myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Moses. So they will come to Moses, peace be upon him, and say: O Moses, you are the Messenger of Allah; Allah favored you with His messages and with speaking to you directly over the people. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the condition we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Moses, peace be upon him, will say to them: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. I killed a person whom I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself! Go to Jesus, peace be upon him. So they will come to Jesus and say: O Jesus, you are the Messenger of Allah, and you spoke to the people while still in the cradle, and a word from Him which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the condition we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? Jesus, peace be upon him, will say to them: My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again - and he will not mention any sin. Myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Muhammad (ﷺ). So they will come to me and say: O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, and Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the condition we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us? So I will set out and come beneath the Throne, and fall down prostrate before my Lord. Then Allah will open to me and inspire me with praises and glorification of Him such as He has not opened to anyone before me. Then it will be said: O Muhammad, raise your head; ask and you shall be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I will raise my head and say: O my Lord, my nation, my nation! Then it will be said: O Muhammad, admit those of your nation who are not to be judged through the right gate among the gates of Paradise, and they will share the other gates with the rest of mankind. By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaves of one of the doors of Paradise is like the distance between Makkah and Hajar, or like the distance between Makkah and Busra."
muslim||479:
Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zaid narrated to us, Ma'bad ibn Hilal al-'Anazi narrated to us. And it was also narrated to us by Sa'id ibn Mansur - and it is his wording - Hammad ibn Zaid narrated to us, Ma'bad ibn Hilal al-'Anazi narrated to us, he said: We set out to visit Anas ibn Malik, and we sought Thabit's intercession [to gain access to him]. When we reached him, he was performing the Duha prayer. Thabit asked permission for us, and we entered upon him, and he seated Thabit with him on his couch. He said to him: O Abu Hamzah, your brothers from the people of Basrah are asking you to narrate to them the hadith of intercession. He said: Muhammad (may peace be upon him) narrated to us, he said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will surge together, some toward others, and they will come to Adam and say to him: Intercede for your progeny. He will say: I am not fit for this, but go to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), for he is the intimate friend of Allah. So they will come to Ibrahim, and he will say: I am not fit for this, but go to Musa (peace be upon him), for he is the one to whom Allah spoke directly. So Musa will be brought, and he will say: I am not fit for this, but go to 'Isa (peace be upon him), for he is the spirit of Allah and His word. So 'Isa will be brought, and he will say: I am not fit for this, but go to Muhammad (may peace be upon him). So I will be brought, and I will say: I am fit for this. So I will go and ask permission of my Lord, and permission will be granted to me. I will stand before Him and praise Him with praises which I am not able to do now, which Allah will inspire in me. Then I will fall down prostrating before Him, and it will be said to me: O Muhammad, raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; ask, you will be given; intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will say: My Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah. Then it will be said: Go, and whoever has in his heart the weight of a wheat grain or a barley grain of faith, bring him out of it. So I will go and do that. Then I will return to my Lord and praise Him with those praises, then I will fall down prostrating before Him. It will be said to me: O Muhammad, raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; ask, you will be given; intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will say: My Ummah, my Ummah. It will be said to me: Go, and whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith, bring him out of it. So I will go and do that. Then I will return again to my Lord and praise Him with those praises, then I will fall down prostrating before Him. It will be said to me: O Muhammad, raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; ask, you will be given; intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will say: O my Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah. It will be said to me: Go, and whoever has in his heart something even less, even less, even less than the weight of a mustard seed of faith, bring him out of the Fire. So I will go and do that."

This is the hadith of Anas which he narrated to us. Then we left him, and when we were at the back of the graveyard, we said: Let us turn aside to al-Hasan and greet him, as he was hiding in the house of Abu Khalifah. He said: So we entered upon him and greeted him, and we said: O Abu Sa'id, we have come from your brother Abu Hamzah, and we have never heard anything like the hadith he narrated to us about intercession. He said: Go on. So we narrated the hadith to him, and he said: Go on. We said: He did not add anything more for us? He said: He narrated it to us twenty years ago when he was in full possession of his faculties. He has left out something - I do not know whether the old man forgot it or disliked to narrate it to you lest you rely on it [alone]. We said to him: Narrate it to us. So he laughed and said: Man was created of haste [Qur'an 21:37]. I have only mentioned this to you because I intended to narrate it to you. Then I will return to my Lord a fourth time and praise Him with those praises, then I will fall down prostrating before Him. It will be said to me: O Muhammad, raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; ask, you will be given; intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will say: O my Lord, grant me permission concerning whoever said "There is no god but Allah." He will say: That is not for you - or He said: That is not up to you - but by My might, My majesty, My greatness, and My supremacy, I shall bring out whoever said "There is no god but Allah."

He said: I bear witness concerning al-Hasan that he narrated this to us, that he heard it from Anas ibn Malik - I think he said - twenty years before, when he was in full possession of his faculties.
muslim||454: And Suwayd bin Sa'eed narrated to me, he said: Hafs bin Maysarah narrated to me, from Zayd bin Aslam, from Ata' bin Yasar, from Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri, that some people in the time of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: Yes. He said: Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun at noon, when it is clear without a cloud? And do you have any difficulty in seeing the moon on a full moon night, when it is clear without a cloud? They said: No, O Messenger of Allah. He said: You will have no more difficulty in seeing Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, than you have in seeing one of them. When the Day of Resurrection comes, an announcer will announce: Let every people follow what they used to worship. So there will not remain anyone who used to worship anything besides Allah, Glory be to Him, such as idols and stone images, but they will fall into the Fire, until none remains but those who used to worship Allah, whether righteous or sinful, and the remnant of the People of the Book. Then the Jews will be called, and it will be said to them: What did you used to worship? They will say: We used to worship Ezra, the son of Allah. It will be said: You have lied; Allah never took a consort or a son. What do you want now? They will say: We are thirsty, our Lord, give us drink. They will be directed with a sign: Will you not go there? So they will be gathered to the Fire, which will appear like a mirage, crushing itself upon itself, and they will fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said to them: What did you used to worship? They will say: We used to worship the Messiah, the son of Allah. It will be said to them: You have lied; Allah never took a consort or a son. It will be said to them: What do you want? They will say: We are thirsty, our Lord, give us drink. He said: They will be directed with a sign: Will you not go there? So they will be gathered to Hell, which will appear like a mirage, crushing itself upon itself, and they will fall into the Fire, until none remains but those who used to worship Allah the Exalted, whether righteous or sinful. Then the Lord of the Worlds, Glory be to Him and Exalted, will come to them in a form other than the one in which they had seen Him. He will say: What are you waiting for? Let every people follow what they used to worship. They will say: Our Lord, we separated from the people in the world when we were in the greatest need of them, and we did not accompany them. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from you; we do not associate anything with Allah - twice or three times - until some of them will almost turn away. He will say: Is there a sign between you and Him by which you would recognize Him? They will say: Yes. Then the shin will be uncovered, and none will remain who used to prostrate to Allah of his own accord, but Allah will permit him to prostrate; and none will remain who used to prostrate out of fear and hypocrisy, but Allah will make his back one single (rigid) piece, so that every time he intends to prostrate, he falls on his back. Then they will raise their heads, and He will have changed into the form in which they had seen Him the first time. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: You are our Lord. Then the bridge will be laid across Hell, and intercession will be permitted, and they will say: O Allah, save us, save us. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the bridge? He said: It is slippery and treacherous, upon which there are hooks and barbs and thorns like the thorny plant found in Najd called As-Sa'dan. The believers will pass over it like the twinkling of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like birds, and like the finest horses and riding camels. Some will be saved unharmed, some will be lacerated but released, and some will be thrown down into the Fire of Hell. Until, when the believers are delivered from the Fire - by Him in Whose hand is my soul, none of you would plead more earnestly with Allah for obtaining justice than the believers will plead with Allah on the Day of Resurrection for their brothers who are in the Fire. They will say: Our Lord, they used to fast with us, and pray, and perform pilgrimage. It will be said to them: Bring out those whom you recognize. So their forms will be forbidden to the Fire, and they will bring out a great many people whom the Fire had seized up to the middle of their shins and up to their knees. Then they will say: Our Lord, none remains in it of those whom You commanded us to bring out. He will say: Go back, and whoever you find in whose heart there is the weight of a dinar of good, bring him out. So they will bring out a great many people. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have left none in it of those whom You commanded us. Then He will say: Go back, and whoever you find in whose heart there is the weight of half a dinar of good, bring him out. So they will bring out a great many people. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have left none in it of those whom You commanded us. Then He will say: Go back, and whoever you find in whose heart there is the weight of a mote of good, bring him out. So they will bring out a great many people. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have left no good in it. And Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri used to say: If you do not believe me regarding this hadith, then read, if you wish: "Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward" (Surat An-Nisa, 4:40). Then Allah, Mighty and Sublime, will say: The angels have interceded, and the Prophets have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and none remains except the Most Merciful of the merciful. He will then take a handful from the Fire and bring out from it a people who never did any good, who have been turned into charcoal, and He will cast them into a river at the entrances of Paradise called the River of Life. They will emerge from it as a seed emerges from the silt carried by a flood. Do you not see how it comes out beside a stone or beside a tree, and what is towards the sun comes out yellowish and greenish, while what is towards the shade comes out white? They said: O Messenger of Allah, it is as if you had been a shepherd in the desert! He said: They will emerge like pearls, with seals around their necks, and the people of Paradise will recognize them: These are the freed slaves of Allah, whom Allah has admitted into Paradise without any deed they had done or any good they had put forward. Then He will say: Enter Paradise, and whatever you see is yours. They will say: Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given anyone else among the worlds. He will say: You have with Me something even better than this. They will say: Our Lord, what could be better than this? He will say: My pleasure - I shall never be angry with you after this, ever.
muslim||2441: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Arara narrated to us, one of them adding a word here and there over the other, saying: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: On the Day of Hunayn, Hawazin, Ghatafan, and others came forward with their offspring and their livestock, while with the Prophet (may peace be upon him) that day were ten thousand men, along with the Freed Ones (al-Tula'a). They turned away from him until he remained alone. He said: That day he called out twice, without mixing anything else with them. He said: He turned to his right and said, "O company of the Ansar!" They said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah! Rejoice, we are with you." He said: Then he turned to his left and said, "O company of the Ansar!" They said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah! Rejoice, we are with you." He said: He was riding a white mule, so he dismounted and said, "I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger." Then the polytheists were routed, and the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) obtained abundant spoils of war. He distributed them among the Muhajirun and the Freed Ones, but did not give the Ansar anything. The Ansar said, "When hardship comes, we are called upon, but the spoils are given to others besides us." This reached him, so he gathered them in a tent and said, "O company of the Ansar, what is this talk that has reached me about you?" They remained silent. He said, "O company of the Ansar, are you not content that the people should take away the worldly goods while you take away Muhammad, bringing him into your homes?" They said, "Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah, we are content." He said: Then he said, "If the people were to take a valley, and the Ansar were to take a mountain pass, I would take the mountain pass of the Ansar." Hisham said: I said, "O Abu Hamza, were you present for that?" He said, "And how could I have been absent from it?"
muslim||2290: Suwaid bin Sa'eed narrated to me, Hafs - that is, Ibn Maisarah al-Sanani - narrated to us, from Zaid bin Aslam, that Abu Salih Dhakwan informed him, that he heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due on it, but when the Day of Resurrection comes, plates of fire will be beaten out for him; then they will be heated in the fire of Hell, and his side, his forehead and his back will be branded with them. Every time they cool, they will be repeated for him during a day whose length will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is pronounced among (Allah's) servants, and he sees his fate, either to Paradise or to Hell." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about camels?" He said: "Nor is there an owner of camels who does not pay what is due on them - and part of what is due on them is milking them on the day they come to water - but when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will be thrown down in a smooth plain, and they will come upon him in the greatest numbers they have ever had, not missing a single young one among them; they will trample him with their hooves and bite him with their mouths. Every time the first of them passes over him, the last of them will be brought back to him, during a day whose length will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is pronounced among (Allah's) servants, and he sees his fate, either to Paradise or to Hell." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about cattle and sheep?" He said: "Nor is there an owner of cattle or sheep who does not pay what is due on them, but when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will be thrown down in a smooth plain, none of them missing, none with twisted horns, nor hornless, nor broken-horned; they will gore him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. Every time the first of them passes over him, the last of them will be brought back to him, during a day whose length will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is pronounced among (Allah's) servants, and he sees his fate, either to Paradise or to Hell." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about horses?" He said: "Horses are of three types: for one man they are a burden, for another they are a shelter, and for another they are a reward. As for the one for whom they are a burden, that is a man who ties them up for show, out of pride, and to fight against the people of Islam - they are a burden for him. As for the one for whom they are a shelter, that is a man who ties them up in the way of Allah, and then does not forget the right of Allah concerning their backs and their necks - they are a shelter for him. As for the one for whom they are a reward, that is a man who ties them up in the way of Allah for the people of Islam, in a meadow or a garden; whatever they eat from that meadow or garden, good deeds will be recorded for him equal to the number of what they ate, and good deeds will be recorded for him equal to the number of their droppings and urine; and if they break loose from their tether and gallop across a hillock or two, Allah will record for him good deeds equal to the number of their tracks and droppings; and if their owner passes them by a river and they drink from it, though he did not intend to water them, Allah will record for him good deeds equal to the number of what they drank." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about donkeys?" He said: "Nothing has been revealed to me concerning donkeys except this single comprehensive verse: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.'" (Surah al-Zalzalah, 99:7-8)
muslim||2149: Dawud b. Rushaid narrated to us, Ismail b. Ulayyah narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abdullah b. Abi Mulaikah who said: I was sitting beside Ibn Umar, while we were waiting for the funeral procession of Umm Aban bint Uthman, and with him was Amr b. Uthman. Then Ibn Abbas came, led by a guide, and I think he had informed him of Ibn Umar's location. So he came and sat beside me, and I was between the two of them. Then there was a sound from the house, and Ibn Umar said - as if he were suggesting to Amr that he should get up and forbid them - "I heard the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) say: 'The dead person is indeed punished because of the weeping of his family.'" He said: Abdullah stated it without qualification. Then Ibn Abbas said: We were with the Commander of the Faithful, Umar b. al-Khattab, until when we were at al-Bayda, he suddenly noticed a man who had stopped in the shade of a tree. He said to me: Go and find out for me who that man is. So I went, and it turned out to be Suhaib. I returned to him and said: You commanded me to find out for you who that was, and it is Suhaib. He said: Tell him to catch up with us. I said: His family is with him. He said: Even if his family is with him. And perhaps Ayyub said: "Tell him to catch up with us." When we arrived, it was not long before the Commander of the Faithful was struck (assassinated). Suhaib came, saying: "O my brother! O my companion!" Umar said: Do you not know, or have you not heard - Ayyub said, or he said: "Have you not known, or have you not heard, that the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: 'The dead person is indeed punished because of some of the weeping of his family'?" He said: As for Abdullah, he stated it without qualification, but as for Umar, he said "some of." So I got up and went in to Aisha and told her what Ibn Umar had said. She said: "No, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) never said that the dead person is punished because of anyone's weeping." But he said: "Indeed, Allah increases the punishment of the disbeliever because of his family's weeping." And indeed, it is Allah who causes laughter and weeping, and "no soul bearing burden shall bear the burden of another." Ayyub said: Ibn Abi Mulaikah said: Al-Qasim b. Muhammad narrated to me, saying: When Aisha was informed of what Umar and Ibn Umar had said, she said: "You are indeed narrating to me from two who were neither liars nor accused of lying, but hearing can be mistaken."
muslim||3336: Hammad bin Isma'il bin Ulayyah narrated to us, Ismail's father narrated to us, from Wuhaib, from Yahya bin Abi Ishaq, that he narrated from Abu Sa'id, the freed slave of al-Mahri: that hardship and difficulty struck them in Medina, and that he came to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and said to him: I have a large family, and hardship has struck us, so I intended to move my family to some fertile area (ar-Rif). Abu Sa'id said: Do not do that, stay in Medina, for we went out with the Prophet of Allah (may peace be upon him)—I think he said—until we arrived at Usfan, where he stayed for several nights. The people said: By Allah, we are not accomplishing anything here, and our families are left alone behind us, and we cannot feel secure about them. This reached the Prophet (may peace be upon him), and he said: "What is this news that has reached me from you? I do not know how"—he said—"By the One by whom I swear, or by the One in Whose hand is my soul, I had resolved," or "if you wish"—I do not know which of the two he said—"to order that my she-camel be saddled, and then I would not undo any of its knots until I reach Medina." And he said: "O Allah, Ibrahim made Mecca sacred and made it a sanctuary, and I make Medina sacred, a sanctuary, between its two mountain passes: that no blood be shed therein, and no weapon be carried therein for fighting, and no tree be cut down therein except for fodder. O Allah, bless us in our city. O Allah, bless us in our sa' (measure). O Allah, bless us in our mudd (measure). O Allah, bless us in our sa'. O Allah, bless us in our mudd. O Allah, bless us in our city. O Allah, make with the blessing two blessings." And, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, there is no mountain pass or narrow path in Medina but that two angels are guarding it until you come to it." Then he said to the people: "Move on," so we moved on and made our way to Medina. And by the One by whom we swear, or by whom one swears—the doubt is from Hammad—we had not yet set down our baggage when we entered Medina, when the tribe of Banu Abdullah bin Ghatafan raided us, and nothing had provoked them before that.
muslim||4428: Muhammad b. al-Muthanna narrated to me: Abd al-A'la narrated to me: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadra, from Abu Sa'id, that a man from Aslam called Ma'iz b. Malik came to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) and said: I have committed an indecency, so carry out the punishment upon me. The Prophet (may peace be upon him) turned him away several times. He said: Then he (the Prophet) asked his people, and they said: We do not know anything wrong with him, except that he has done something which he thinks he cannot get out of except by having the prescribed punishment carried out on him. He said: So he (Ma'iz) went back to the Prophet (may peace be upon him), and he commanded us to stone him. He said: So we took him to Baqi' al-Gharqad. He said: We neither bound him nor dug a pit for him. He said: We threw at him bones, clods of earth, and pieces of pottery. He said: He fled, so we ran after him until he came to the open ground of the Harra, where he stood firm for us, and we threw at him the rocks of the Harra, that is, stones, until he became still. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) stood up in the afternoon delivering a sermon, and he said: "Is it that whenever we go out on an expedition in the way of Allah, a man remains behind with our families, having a bleating like the bleating of a billy-goat? It is upon me that I shall not have brought to me any man who does that, but I will make an example of him." He said: He neither asked forgiveness for him nor cursed him.
muslim||3692:
Harun bin Sa'id Al-Aili narrated to us, Abdullah bin Wahb narrated to us, Sulaiman (meaning Ibn Bilal) informed me, Yahya informed me, Ubaid bin Hunain informed me that he heard Abdullah bin Abbas narrating: I remained for a year wanting to ask Umar bin Al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not ask him out of awe of him, until he went out for Hajj and I went out with him. When he returned, and we were on part of the road, he turned aside to the arak trees to relieve himself. I waited for him until he finished, then I walked with him, and I said: "O Commander of the Believers, who are the two who conspired against the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) among his wives?" He said: "That was Hafsah and Aishah." I said to him: "By Allah, I had wanted to ask you about this for a year, but I could not out of awe of you." He said: "Do not do that. Whatever you think I have knowledge of, ask me about it, and if I know it I will tell you."

He (Ibn Abbas) said: And Umar said: "By Allah, during the time of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) we did not count women as having any importance, until Allah Most High revealed concerning them what He revealed, and allotted to them what He allotted." He said: "While I was engaged in a matter I was considering, my wife said to me: 'If only you would do such and such.' I said to her: 'What is it to you and what business is it of yours to interfere in a matter I intend to do?' She said to me: 'How strange you are, O son of Al-Khattab! You do not want to be answered back, yet your daughter answers back the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) until he remains angry for the whole day.'"

Umar said: "So I took my cloak and went out at once until I entered upon Hafsah, and I said to her: 'O my daughter, do you answer back the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) until he remains angry for the whole day?' Hafsah said: 'By Allah, we do answer him back.' I said: 'Know that I warn you of the punishment of Allah and the anger of His Messenger. O my daughter, do not let this one deceive you who is pleased with her own beauty and the love the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) has for her' - meaning Aishah."

"Then I went out until I entered upon Umm Salamah, because of my kinship with her, and I spoke to her. Umm Salamah said to me: 'How strange you are, O son of Al-Khattab! You have intruded into everything, until you now wish to intrude between the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) and his wives.' He said: She rebuked me so sharply that it took away some of what I was feeling, and I left her."

"I had a companion from among the Ansar; when I was absent he would bring me news, and when he was absent I would bring him news. We were at that time fearful of a king among the kings of Ghassan, of whom it was mentioned to us that he intended to march against us, so our hearts were filled with concern about him. My companion from the Ansar came knocking at the door and said: 'Open, open!' I said: 'Has the Ghassani come?' He said: 'Something more serious than that - the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) has separated from his wives.' I said: 'May the nose of Hafsah and Aishah be rubbed in the dust!' Then I took my garment and went out until I came, and there was the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) in an upper chamber of his, which was reached by a ladder, and a black servant of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) was at the top of the stairs. I said: 'This is Umar,' and I was given permission."

Umar said: "So I related to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) this account, and when I reached the account of Umm Salamah, the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) smiled. He was lying on a mat with nothing between him and it, and under his head was a leather pillow stuffed with palm fibre, and at his feet was a pile of tanning bark, and at his head were hanging hides. I saw the mark of the mat on the side of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and I wept."

He said: "What makes you weep?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, Khosrau and Caesar live in such luxury, while you are the Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "Are you not pleased that theirs should be this world and yours the Hereafter?"
muslim||4506: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, Shu'bah told us. And Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' told me - and the wording is his - Ghundar told us, Shu'bah told us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl who said: I heard Suwayd ibn Ghafalah say: I went out, along with Zayd ibn Suhan and Salman ibn Rabi'ah, as fighters (in a military expedition), and I found a whip, so I picked it up. They said to me: "Leave it." I said: "No, but I will make it known publicly; if its owner comes (I will give it to him), otherwise I will make use of it." He said: I refused to yield to them (on this). When we returned from our expedition, it was decreed for me that I performed the pilgrimage, so I came to Medina and met Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and I told him about the matter of the whip and what they had said. He said: I found a purse containing one hundred dinars in the time of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), so I brought it to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and he said: "Announce it publicly for a year." He said: So I announced it publicly, but I found no one who recognized it. Then I came to him again, and he said: "Announce it publicly for a year." So I announced it publicly, but I found no one who recognized it. Then I came to him again, and he said: "Announce it publicly for a year." So I announced it publicly, but I found no one who recognized it. He said: "Keep in mind its number, its container, and its tie-string; then if its owner comes (give it to him), otherwise make use of it." So I made use of it. I met him (Ubayy) after that in Mecca, and he said: I do not know whether it was three years or one year.
muslim||4431:
Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani narrated to me, Yahya ibn Ya'la - who is Ibn al-Harith al-Muharibi - narrated to us, from Ghaylan - who is Ibn Jami' al-Muharibi - from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: "Ma'iz ibn Malik came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: O Messenger of Allah, purify me. He said: Woe to you, go back and ask Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him. He said: So he went back a short distance, then came again and said: O Messenger of Allah, purify me. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: Woe to you, go back and ask Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him. He said: So he went back a short distance, then came again and said: O Messenger of Allah, purify me. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said the same thing, until when it was the fourth time, the Messenger of Allah said to him: Of what shall I purify you? He said: Of fornication. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asked: Is he mad? He was told that he was not mad. He said: Has he drunk wine? A man got up and smelled his breath but did not find the smell of wine on him. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: Have you committed fornication? He said: Yes. So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned. The people were divided into two groups concerning him: one group said: He has perished, his sin has overwhelmed him; and another group said: There is no repentance better than the repentance of Ma'iz, for he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and put his hand in his hand, then said: Kill me with stones. He said: They remained thus for two or three days, then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came while they were sitting, and he gave the greeting of peace, then sat down, and said: Ask forgiveness for Ma'iz ibn Malik. He said: They said: May Allah forgive Ma'iz ibn Malik. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: He has repented a repentance which, if it were divided among a nation, would suffice them all.

He said: Then a woman from Ghamid, of the tribe of Azd, came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, purify me. He said: Woe to you, go back and ask Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him. She said: I see that you want to send me back as you sent back Ma'iz ibn Malik. He said: What is that? She said: She is pregnant from fornication. He said: Is it you? She said: Yes. He said to her: Not until you have given birth to what is in your womb. He said: So a man from among the Ansar took charge of her until she gave birth. He said: Then he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: The woman from Ghamid has given birth. He said: Then we shall not stone her and leave her child small with no one to nurse him. A man from among the Ansar stood up and said: His nursing is upon me, O Prophet of Allah. He said: So he had her stoned."
muslim||3691: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Umar bin Yunus al-Hanafi told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, from Simak Abu Zumail, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin al-Khattab told me, he said: "When the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque and found the people striking the ground with pebbles, saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has divorced his wives.' That was before they were commanded to observe the veil (hijab). Umar said: I said, 'I shall certainly find out about this today.' He said: So I went in to Aishah and said, 'O daughter of Abu Bakr, has it come to this, that you would trouble the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?' She said, 'What business is it of mine and yours, O son of al-Khattab? Attend to your own affairs.' He said: So I went in to Hafsah bint Umar and said to her, 'O Hafsah, has it come to this, that you would trouble the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)? By Allah, you know well that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) does not love you, and were it not for me, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would have divorced you.' She wept most bitterly. I said to her, 'Where is the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?' She said, 'He is in his storeroom in the loft (mashrubah).' So I entered, and there I found Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), sitting on the threshold of the loft, with his legs dangling over a hollowed-out piece of wood, which was a trunk that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would climb up and down on. I called out, 'O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' Rabah looked up at the room, then looked at me, and said nothing. Then I said, 'O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' Rabah looked up at the room, then looked at me, and said nothing. Then I raised my voice and said, 'O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), for I think that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) thinks I have come because of Hafsah. By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered me to strike her neck, I would strike her neck.' I raised my voice, and he gestured to me to come up. So I went in to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he was lying on a mat. I sat down, and he drew his lower garment closer around himself - he had nothing else on - and the mat had left marks on his side. I looked around with my eyes at the storeroom of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and there I found a handful of barley, about a sa' in quantity, and a similar amount of acacia leaves (used for tanning) in a corner of the room, and a hide hanging up. My eyes filled with tears. He said: 'What makes you weep, O son of al-Khattab?' I said, 'O Prophet of Allah, why should I not weep, when this mat has left marks on your side, and this is your storeroom in which I see only what I see, while that Caesar and that Khosrau live amid fruits and rivers, and you are the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and His chosen one, and this is your storeroom?' He said, 'O son of al-Khattab, are you not satisfied that we should have the Hereafter and they should have this world?' I said, 'Yes indeed.'" He said: "And I went in to him when I entered, and I could see anger in his face. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, why should the matter of the women distress you? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, and Gabriel, and Michael, and I and Abu Bakr, and the believers are with you.' Rarely did I speak - and I praise Allah for it - a word, but I hoped that Allah would confirm the truth of what I said." And this verse came down, the verse of choice (āyat al-takhyīr): "Perhaps his Lord, if he divorced you, would substitute for him wives better than you" [Surah at-Tahrim 66:5], and "If you two (wives) cooperate against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel, and the righteous among the believers, and the angels are also his supporters" [Surah at-Tahrim 66:4]. Aishah bint Abu Bakr and Hafsah used to cooperate against the rest of the wives of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced them?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I entered the mosque, and the Muslims were striking the ground with pebbles, saying, "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has divorced his wives." Shall I go down and tell them that you have not divorced them?' He said, 'Yes, if you wish.' So I kept talking to him until the anger left his face, until he smiled, and he had one of the most beautiful smiles among people. Then the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came down, and I came down. I came down clinging to the trunk, while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came down as though he were walking on the ground, not touching it with his hand. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, you were in the loft for twenty-nine days.' He said, 'The month can be twenty-nine days.' I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice, 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has not divorced his wives.'" And this verse came down: "And when there comes to them information about [public] security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, those seeking to derive correct conclusions would have known about it [from them]" [Surah an-Nisa 4:83]. And it was I who had derived that matter, and Allah, Exalted and Glorious, revealed the verse of choice.
muslim||3695:
Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Hanzali and Muhammad bin Abi 'Umar narrated this hadith to us with very similar wording. Ibn Abi 'Umar said: "Abdur-Razzaq narrated to us," while Ishaq said: "Abdur-Razzaq informed us"; he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Az-Zuhri, from 'Ubaidullah bin 'Abdullah bin Abi Thawr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said:

I had long wished to ask 'Umar about the two women among the wives of the Prophet (may peace be upon him) about whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "If you two (wives) turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts are indeed so inclined" (Surah At-Tahrim, 66:4), until 'Umar went for Hajj, and I went for Hajj with him. When we were on part of the road, 'Umar turned aside, and I turned aside with him carrying a water-vessel. He relieved himself, then came to me, and I poured water on his hands and he performed ablution. I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, who were the two women among the wives of the Prophet (may peace be upon him) to whom Allah, Mighty and Sublime, said: 'If you two (wives) turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts are indeed so inclined'?" 'Umar said: "I am astonished at you, O Ibn 'Abbas." (Az-Zuhri said: By Allah, he disliked what he had asked him about, but he did not conceal it from him.) He said: "They are Hafsah and 'Aishah." Then he began to relate the story. He said:

We, the tribe of Quraish, were a people who dominated our women, but when we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women. My house was among the Banu Umayyah bin Zaid in the 'Awali (upper part of Madinah). One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to answer me back. I was displeased that she answered me back, and she said: "Why are you displeased that I answer you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet (may peace be upon him) answer him back, and one of them may keep away from him for the whole day until night." This alarmed me, so I went and entered upon Hafsah and said: "Do you answer back the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him)?" She said: "Yes." I said: "Does one of you keep away from him for a whole day until night?" She said: "Yes." I said: "Whoever among you does that has certainly failed and lost. Does any of you feel secure that Allah will not become angry with her because of the anger of His Messenger (may peace be upon him), and then she would be ruined? Do not answer back the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), nor ask him for anything, but ask me for whatever you need. And do not let it deceive you that your co-wife is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) than you" - meaning 'Aishah.

He said: I had a neighbor from among the Ansar, and we used to take turns going down to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him); he would go down one day and I would go down another day. He would bring me news of revelation and other matters, and I would bring him the same. We used to talk about how the Ghassan were shoeing their horses to attack us. My companion went down (to the Prophet), then came to me in the evening and knocked on my door and called me. I went out to him, and he said: "A great matter has happened." I said: "What is it? Has Ghassan come?" He said: "No, it is greater and more serious than that: the Prophet (may peace be upon him) has divorced his wives." I said: "Hafsah has failed and lost. I had thought this would happen." When I had prayed the dawn prayer, I put on my clothes, then went down and entered upon Hafsah, and she was weeping. I said: "Has the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) divorced you all?" She said: "I do not know. He is there, secluded in this upper room." I went to a black slave-boy of his and said: "Seek permission for 'Umar." He went in, then came out to me and said: "I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent." So I went and reached the pulpit and sat down. There was a group sitting near it, some of them weeping. I sat for a while, then what I was feeling overwhelmed me, and I went again to the slave-boy and said: "Seek permission for 'Umar." He went in, then came out to me and said: "I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent." So I turned to leave, and then the slave-boy called me and said: "Enter, for he has given you permission." I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and found him reclining on a mat of palm-fiber which had left marks on his side. I said: "Have you divorced your wives, O Messenger of Allah?" He raised his head to me and said: "No." I said: "Allah is Greater! If you had seen us, O Messenger of Allah - we, the tribe of Quraish, were a people who dominated our women, but when we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women. I became angry with my wife one day, and she began to answer me back, and I was displeased that she answered me back. She said: 'Why are you displeased that I answer you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet (may peace be upon him) answer him back, and one of them may keep away from him for the whole day until night.' I said: 'Whoever among them does that has certainly failed and lost. Does any of them feel secure that Allah will not become angry with her because of the anger of His Messenger (may peace be upon him), and then she would be ruined?'" The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) smiled. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon Hafsah and said: 'Do not let it deceive you that your co-wife is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) than you.'" He smiled again. I said: "May I sit with you comfortably, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So I sat down, and I raised my head in the room, and by Allah, I saw nothing in it that caught the eye except three hides. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to grant abundance to your Ummah, for He has granted abundance to the Persians and the Romans, though they do not worship Allah." He sat up straight and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of Al-Khattab? Those are a people to whom their good things have been given in advance in the life of this world." I said: "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." He had sworn not to enter upon them for a month, due to the intensity of his displeasure with them, until Allah, Mighty and Sublime, rebuked him (for this oath).
muslim||4580: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Hujayn informed us, Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn az-Zubayr, from 'Aishah, that she informed him that Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), sent word to Abu Bakr as-Siddiq asking him for her inheritance from the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), from what Allah had granted him as spoils in Medina, and Fadak, and what remained of the khumus (fifth) of Khaybar. Abu Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: 'We are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity.' The family of Muhammad (may peace be upon him) only eat from this wealth. And by Allah, I will not change anything of the charity of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) from the state it was in during the time of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and I will certainly deal with it as the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) dealt with it." So Abu Bakr refused to give Fatimah anything. Fatimah was displeased with Abu Bakr because of this, so she avoided him and did not speak to him until she died. She lived six months after the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him). When she died, her husband 'Ali ibn Abi Talib buried her at night and did not inform Abu Bakr of it, and 'Ali led the funeral prayer over her. During Fatimah's lifetime, 'Ali had a certain standing among the people, but when she died, the people's faces turned away from him, so 'Ali sought reconciliation with Abu Bakr and to give him his pledge of allegiance, for he had not given the pledge during those months. He sent word to Abu Bakr saying: "Come to us, and let no one come with you," out of dislike for the presence of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: "By Allah, do not go in to them alone." Abu Bakr said: "What could they possibly do to me? By Allah, I will indeed go to them." So Abu Bakr went in to them. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib recited the shahadah (testimony of faith), then said: "We know, O Abu Bakr, your excellence and what Allah has given you, and we do not begrudge you any good that Allah has brought to you. But you acted alone in this matter, while we thought we had a right due to our kinship with the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him)." He continued speaking to Abu Bakr until Abu Bakr's eyes overflowed with tears. When Abu Bakr spoke, he said: "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, the kinship of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) is dearer to me to maintain than my own kinship. As for what occurred between me and you concerning this wealth, I did not fall short of the truth in it, and I did not leave anything that I saw the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) do concerning it except that I did it." 'Ali said to Abu Bakr: "Your appointment is this afternoon for the pledge of allegiance."
