So when Abu Bakr had prayed the noon prayer, he ascended the pulpit and recited the shahadah, and mentioned the matter of 'Ali and his delay in giving the pledge, and the excuse he had offered for it, then he sought forgiveness. Then 'Ali ibn Abi Talib recited the shahadah, and he extolled the right of Abu Bakr and said that what had made him act as he did was not out of envy of Abu Bakr, nor a denial of that which Allah had favored him with, "but we thought we had a share in this matter, and it was decided without consulting us, and we were displeased about it in ourselves." The Muslims were pleased with this and said: "You have done well." And the Muslims drew close to 'Ali when he returned to what was right and proper.
muslim||4582: Ibn Numair narrated to us: Ya'qub bin Ibrahim narrated to us: My father narrated to us. Another chain: Zuhair bin Harb and Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Hulwani narrated to us, they said: Ya'qub, who is Ibn Ibrahim, narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Urwah bin Az-Zubair informed me that A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), informed him that Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), asked Abu Bakr, after the death of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), to give her her inheritance from what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had left of what Allah had bestowed upon him as spoils. Abu Bakr said to her: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "We are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity." She (A'ishah) said: Fatimah lived for six months after the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and Fatimah used to ask Abu Bakr for her share of what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had left from Khaibar, Fadak, and his charitable land in Madinah, but Abu Bakr refused to give her that, and said: I will not leave anything that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to do, but that I will do it, for I fear that if I neglect any part of his command, I will go astray. As for his charitable land in Madinah, Umar gave it to Ali and Abbas, and Ali took full control of it. As for Khaibar and Fadak, Umar kept them and said: These two are the charity of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), which were for his needs that arose and his contingencies, and their affairs are to be managed by whoever is in charge of authority. She (A'ishah) said: And so they have remained thus until today.
muslim||5616: Al-Hakam bin Musa Abu Salih narrated to us, Shu'ayb, meaning Ibn Ishaq, narrated to us, Hisham bin 'Urwah informed me, 'Urwah bin al-Zubayr and Fatimah bint al-Mundhir bin al-Zubayr narrated to me, that they both said: Asma bint Abi Bakr set out when she emigrated while she was pregnant with 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr. She arrived at Quba, and there she gave birth to 'Abdullah at Quba. Then, when she had given birth, she went out to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) so that he might chew something and put it in the baby's mouth (tahnik). The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) took him from her and placed him in his lap, then called for a date. He (the narrator) said: 'A'ishah said: We stayed a while searching for one before we found it. He chewed it and then spat it into the baby's mouth, so the first thing that entered his stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him). Then Asma said: Then he wiped him and prayed for him (invoked a blessing upon him), and named him 'Abdullah. Later, when he was seven or eight years old, he came to give the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), al-Zubayr having ordered him to do so. The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) smiled when he saw him coming towards him, and then accepted his pledge.
muslim||4588:
Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, [saying]: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar, [who said]: Simak al-Hanafi narrated to me, [who said]: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, saying: When it was the day of Badr... [continuing the chain] And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us - and the wording is his - Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us, Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, Abu Zumayl - who is Simak al-Hanafi - narrated to me, Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, saying:

"When it was the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the polytheists, and they numbered one thousand, while his companions numbered three hundred and nineteen men. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands and began to call upon his Lord: 'O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me. O Allah, grant me what You have promised me. O Allah, if You destroy this band of the people of Islam, You will not be worshipped on earth.' He continued calling upon his Lord, stretching out his hands, facing the qiblah, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak, and put it back on his shoulders, then embraced him from behind and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, your imploring of your Lord is enough for you; He will surely fulfill for you what He has promised you.' Then Allah, Mighty and Sublime, revealed: 'When you sought help of your Lord, and He answered you, "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."' [Quran 8:9] So Allah reinforced him with the angels."

Abu Zumayl said: Ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: "While a man from the Muslims was that day pursuing a man from the polytheists ahead of him, he suddenly heard the crack of a whip above him, and the voice of a horseman saying: 'Forward, Hayzum!' He looked at the polytheist ahead of him, and he fell down on his back. He looked at him, and found that his nose had been struck and his face slashed as if by a whip-stroke, and it had all turned green. The Ansari man came and related that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'You have spoken the truth; that was from the reinforcement of the third heaven.' They killed seventy that day and took seventy captive."

Abu Zumayl said: Ibn Abbas said: "When they had taken the captives, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and Umar: 'What do you think about these captives?' Abu Bakr said: 'O Prophet of Allah, they are cousins and kinsmen; I think you should take ransom from them, which would be a strength for us against the disbelievers, and perhaps Allah will guide them to Islam.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What do you think, O son of al-Khattab?' I said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I do not hold the view that Abu Bakr holds. Rather, I think you should hand them over to us so that we may strike off their necks - hand over Aqil to Ali so that he may strike off his neck, and hand over so-and-so, a relative of Umar, to me so that I may strike off his neck. For these are the leaders of disbelief and its chiefs.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) preferred what Abu Bakr had said, and did not prefer what I had said. The next day, when I came, I found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr sitting and weeping. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me why you and your companion are weeping. If I find cause to weep, I will weep, and if I do not find cause to weep, I will weep out of sympathy for your weeping.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I am weeping because of what your companions presented to me regarding taking ransom. Indeed, their punishment was shown to me, as near to me as this tree' - a tree near the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ). Then Allah, Mighty and Sublime, revealed: 'It is not for a prophet to have captives until he inflicts a massacre upon [his enemy] in the land...' up to His saying: 'so eat of what you have taken as spoils of war, [as being] lawful and good...' [Quran 8:67-69] So Allah made the spoils of war lawful for them."
muslim||5315: Hajjaj bin Ash-Sha'ir told me: Ad-Dahhak bin Makhlad told me, from a note he presented to me and then read to me, saying: Hanzalah bin Abi Sufyan informed us, Sa'id bin Mina' told us, saying: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: When the trench was being dug, I saw signs of hunger on the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so I turned back to my wife and said to her: Do you have anything? I have seen severe hunger on the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). She brought out for me a leather bag containing a sa' of barley, and we had a small domestic lamb. He said: So I slaughtered it, and she ground the barley, finishing when I finished. I then cut the meat up and put it in its cooking pot, then I went off to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). She said: Do not disgrace me before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and those with him. He said: So I came to him and spoke to him privately, saying: O Messenger of Allah, we have slaughtered a small lamb of ours, and a sa' of barley we had has been ground; so come, you and a group with you. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) then called out and said: O people of the trench, Jabir has prepared a feast for you, so come along. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: Do not take your pot off (the fire), and do not bake your dough, until I come. So I came, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came ahead of the people, until I came to my wife. She said: May you be disgraced, may you be disgraced! I said: I have done what you told me. So I brought out our dough to him, and he spat into it and blessed it. Then he went to our pot, and he spat into it and blessed it. Then he said: Call a woman to bake with you, and ladle out from your pot, and do not take it off (the fire). And they were a thousand men. I swear by Allah, they ate until they left it and turned away, while our pot was still bubbling just as it was, and our dough - or as he said, Ad-Dahhak said: - was still being baked just as it was.
muslim||2950:
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim together narrated to us, from Hatim - Abu Bakr said: Hatim ibn Isma'il al-Madani narrated to us - from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said:

We entered upon Jabir ibn Abdullah, and he asked about the people (present) until he reached me. I said: "I am Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Husayn." He reached out his hand toward my head and undid my top button, then undid my lower button, then placed his palm between my chest - I was at that time a young boy - and said: "Welcome, son of my brother! Ask whatever you wish." So I asked him, while he was blind, and the time of prayer came, and he stood up wrapped in a woven cloth. Whenever he placed it on his shoulder, its ends would fall back to him because of its smallness, while his mantle was beside him on the clothes rack. He led us in prayer.

I said: "Tell me about the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)." He gestured with his hand, counting nine, and said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) remained for nine years without performing Hajj. Then in the tenth year it was announced to the people that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would perform Hajj. So a great number of people came to Madinah, all seeking to follow the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and to do as he did. We set out with him until we reached Dhul-Hulayfah. There Asma bint Umays gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, and she sent word to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) asking what she should do. He said: 'Perform ghusl, bind yourself with a cloth, and enter into ihram.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) then prayed in the mosque, then mounted al-Qaswa, and when his camel stood up with him at al-Bayda, I looked as far as I could see, before him, riders and walkers, and to his right the same, and to his left the same, and behind him the same. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was among us, and the Qur'an was being revealed to him, and he knew its interpretation, and whatever he did, we did. He raised his voice in Tawhid: 'Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak.' And the people raised their voices with the [phrases] they used to raise, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) did not object to any of it, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) kept to his Ttalbiyah."

Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "We intended nothing but Hajj, not knowing about Umrah, until we came with him to the House. He touched the corner (of the Ka'bah), then ran three rounds and walked four. Then he went to the Station of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and recited: 'And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer' (2:125). He placed the Station between himself and the House." My father used to say - and I do not know of him mentioning it except from the Prophet (peace be upon him) - that he recited in the two rak'ahs: "Say, He is Allah, the One" and "Say, O disbelievers." Then he returned to the corner and touched it, then went out of the gate to al-Safa. When he drew near to al-Safa he recited: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the rites of Allah" (2:158), [saying] "I begin with what Allah began with." So he began with al-Safa and climbed it until he could see the House. He faced the Qiblah and declared Allah's oneness and magnified Him, and said: "There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable. There is no god but Allah alone, who fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone." Then he supplicated in between that, saying the same thing three times. Then he descended to al-Marwah, and when his feet reached the bottom of the valley he ran, and when he ascended he walked, until he came to al-Marwah, where he did as he had done at al-Safa.

When his last circuit ended at al-Marwah, he said: "If I had known beforehand what I know now, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals, and I would have made this an Umrah. So whoever among you has not brought a sacrificial animal, let him exit ihram and make it an Umrah." Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'sham stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for this year only, or forever?" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) interlaced his fingers together and said: "Umrah has entered into Hajj," twice, "no, rather forever, forever."

Ali came from Yemen with the sacrificial camels of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and found Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, among those who had exited ihram, wearing dyed clothes and having applied kohl. He objected to this, and she said: "My father commanded me to do this." Ali used to say in Iraq: "I went to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), objecting on account of Fatimah for what she had done, seeking a ruling from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) regarding what she had reported from him. I informed him that I had objected to her." He said: "She spoke the truth, she spoke the truth. What did you say when you undertook the Hajj?" He said: "I said: 'O Allah, I intend what Your Messenger intends.'" He said: "Then I have the sacrificial animals with me, so do not exit ihram." Jabir said: "The total number of sacrificial animals that Ali brought from Yemen and that the Prophet (peace be upon him) brought was one hundred."

He said: "So all the people exited ihram and cut their hair, except the Prophet (peace be upon him) and those who had sacrificial animals with them. When the Day of Tarwiyah came, they set out for Mina and entered into ihram for Hajj. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) rode and led the prayers there - Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr - then waited a little until the sun rose. He ordered a tent of hair cloth to be pitched for him at Namirah.

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) then proceeded, and Quraysh had no doubt that he would halt at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, as Quraysh used to do in the time of Jahiliyyah. But the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went on until he came to Arafah, where he found that the tent had been pitched for him at Namirah, and he stayed there. When the sun had passed its zenith, he ordered al-Qaswa to be brought and saddled for him. He came to the bottom of the valley and addressed the people, saying:

'Verily your blood and your property are sacred to you, just as this day of yours and this month of yours and this land of yours are sacred. Behold, everything pertaining to the affairs of Jahiliyyah is abolished under my feet. The blood-vengeance claims of Jahiliyyah are abolished, and the first claim I abolish among our blood-claims is that of the son of Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith, who was being suckled among the Banu Sa'd and was killed by Hudhayl. And the usury of Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first usury I abolish is our own usury, that of Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib; it is all abolished. So fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them as a trust from Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful to you by the word of Allah. You have a right over them, that they not allow anyone whom you dislike to tread your bed. But if they do that, then beat them with a beating that is not severe. And they have a right over you, that you provide for them and clothe them fittingly. I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray - the Book of Allah. You will be asked about me, so what will you say?' They said: 'We bear witness that you have conveyed the message, fulfilled your trust, and given sincere counsel.' He then raised his index finger toward the sky and pointed it at the people, saying: 'O Allah, bear witness. O Allah, bear witness,' three times.

Then he gave the call to prayer, then the call to commence, and he prayed Zuhr. Then he gave the call to commence again and prayed Asr, and he prayed nothing between them. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) rode until he came to the standing-place, and he positioned the flank of his camel al-Qaswa toward the rocks, with the path of the walkers in front of him, and faced the Qiblah. He remained standing there until the sun set and the yellow glow had somewhat faded, until the disk had disappeared. He seated Usamah behind him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) moved on, having tightened the rein of al-Qaswa so that its head nearly touched the front of his saddle, and he was saying with his right hand: 'O people, calmness, calmness.' Whenever he came to a hill among the hills, he would loosen the rein a little until it climbed up, until he came to Muzdalifah. There he prayed Maghrib and Isha with a single call to prayer and two calls to commence, and he did not glorify Allah [with any voluntary prayer] between them. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) lay down until dawn broke, and he prayed Fajr when the dawn became clear, with a call to prayer and a call to commence.

Then he rode al-Qaswa until he came to al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and he faced the Qiblah, supplicating Him, magnifying Him, declaring His oneness and His uniqueness. He remained standing there until it became very bright, and he moved on before the sun rose. He seated al-Fadl ibn Abbas behind him, who was a man with beautiful hair, fair, and handsome. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) moved on, some women passed by riding swiftly, and al-Fadl began looking at them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) placed his hand on al-Fadl's face, and al-Fadl turned his face to the other side to look, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) moved his hand to the other side onto al-Fadl's face, turning his face away from that side as well when he looked, until he came to the bottom of Muhassir, where he quickened the pace a little. Then he took the middle road which leads out to the largest Jamrah, until he came to the Jamrah that is by the tree, and he threw seven pebbles at it, saying "Allahu Akbar" with each pebble, pebbles of the size for flicking, throwing from the bottom of the valley.

Then he went to the place of sacrifice and slaughtered sixty-three [camels] with his own hand. Then he gave [the rest] to Ali, who slaughtered what remained, and he shared with him in his sacrificial offering. Then he ordered that a piece from every camel be taken and put in a pot, and it was cooked, and the two of them ate from its meat and drank from its broth.

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) rode and went to the House and performed Tawaf, and prayed Zuhr at Makkah. Then he went to the Banu Abdul-Muttalib, who were drawing water at Zamzam, and said: 'Draw water, O Banu Abdul-Muttalib! Were it not that people might overpower you regarding your right to provide water, I would draw water with you.' So they handed him a bucket, and he drank from it."
muslim||4622:
Shayban bin Farrukh narrated to us, Sulayman bin al-Mughirah narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Abdullah bin Rabah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: "Delegations came to Mu'awiyah, and that was during Ramadan. Some of us used to prepare food for one another, and Abu Hurairah was among those who frequently invited us to his lodging. So I said: 'Should I not prepare food and invite them to my lodging?' So I ordered that food be prepared, then I met Abu Hurairah in the evening and said: 'The invitation is at my place tonight.' He said: I said: 'Yes.' So I invited them, and Abu Hurairah said: 'Shall I not inform you of a hadith from your own accounts, O company of the Ansar?' Then he mentioned the conquest of Makkah, and said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) advanced until he arrived at Makkah. He sent al-Zubair in command of one flank, and sent Khalid in command of the other flank, and sent Abu Ubaidah in charge of those on foot without armor. They took the bottom of the valley, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with the main army column. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) looked and saw me. Abu Hurairah said: I said: 'Here I am, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'None should come to me except an Ansari.'"

Others besides Shayban added: He said: "Call out to me the Ansar." He said: So they surrounded him, while the Quraysh had gathered a rabble of their lowly followers and dependents, and they said: "We will put these forward; if they achieve something we will be with them, and if they are struck down, we will give what is asked of us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you see the rabble of Quraysh and their followers?" Then he said, with one of his hands over the other: "[Advance] until you meet me at al-Safa." He said: So we set off, and none of us wished to kill anyone but that he killed him, and none of them turned anything against us. He said: Then Abu Sufyan came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the green pastures of Quraysh have been laid open; there is no Quraysh after today." Then he [the Prophet] said: "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe." The Ansar said among themselves: "As for the man, he has been overtaken by a desire for his hometown and tenderness towards his kinsfolk." Abu Hurairah said: Then the revelation came - and when the revelation came, it was not hidden from us; when it came, no one would raise his eyes to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until the revelation was concluded. When the revelation ended, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O company of the Ansar!" They said: "Here we are, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Did you say: 'As for the man, he has been overtaken by a desire for his hometown'?" They said: "That was indeed said." He said: "No indeed! I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger. I emigrated to Allah and to you; my life is your life and my death is your death." So they came forward to him weeping, saying: "By Allah, we said what we said only out of protectiveness for Allah and His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah and His Messenger believe you and accept your excuse."

He said: Then the people went to the house of Abu Sufyan, and the people closed their doors. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) advanced until he came to the Stone and touched it, then he circled the House. He said: Then he came upon an idol beside the House which they used to worship. He said: In the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a bow, and he was holding it by its curved tip. When he came to the idol, he began to jab it in its eye, saying: "The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished." When he finished his circumambulation, he went to al-Safa and climbed upon it until he could see the House, and he raised his hands, and began to praise Allah and to pray with whatever he wished to pray for.
muslim||5129:
Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn 'Ufair Abu 'Uthman al-Misri informed us, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, 'Ali ibn Husain ibn 'Ali informed me, that Husain ibn 'Ali informed him, that 'Ali said: "I had an old she-camel that was my share from the spoils of the Battle of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) had given me another old she-camel from the khumus (fifth share) that day. When I wanted to consummate my marriage with Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), I made an arrangement with a goldsmith from Banu Qainuqa' to go with me so that we might bring back some idhkhir (a type of sweet-smelling grass) which I intended to sell to goldsmiths, and with the proceeds I would provide for my wedding feast. While I was gathering equipment for my two she-camels - saddles, sacks, and ropes - my two she-camels being tethered beside the room of a man from among the Ansar, and having gathered what I had gathered, I found that their humps had been cut off, their flanks had been slit open, and portions of their livers had been taken. I could not hold back my tears when I saw that sight befallen them. I said: 'Who did this?' They said: 'Hamzah ibn 'Abdul-Muttalib did it. He is in this house drinking with a group of the Ansar. A singing girl sang to him and his companions, saying in her song: 'O Hamzah, what about those fat she-camels?' So Hamzah got up with his sword and cut off their humps and slit open their flanks and took portions from their livers.'"

'Ali said: "So I went off until I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and Zaid ibn Harithah was with him. The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) recognized in my face what had befallen me, so the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: 'What is the matter with you?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have never seen anything like today - Hamzah attacked my two she-camels, cutting off their humps and slitting open their flanks, and there he is now in a house with a drinking party.'"

He said: "So the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) called for his cloak and put it on, then set off walking, and I followed him along with Zaid ibn Harithah, until he came to the door behind which Hamzah was. He asked permission to enter, and they granted him permission. There they were, a drinking party. The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) began to rebuke Hamzah for what he had done. Hamzah's eyes were red. Hamzah looked at the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), then raised his gaze to look at his knees, then raised his gaze further and looked at his navel, then raised his gaze further and looked at his face. Hamzah said: 'Are you anything but slaves of my father?' The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) realized that he was intoxicated, so the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) withdrew, stepping backward, and went out, and we went out with him."
muslim||4607:
Ishaq bin Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Ibn Abi 'Umar, Muhammad bin Rafi', and 'Abd bin Humaid narrated to us - and the wording is that of Ibn Rafi' - Ibn Rafi' and Ibn Abi 'Umar said: "Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us," while the other two said: "Abd ar-Razzaq informed us": Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Ubaidullah bin 'Abdullah bin 'Utbah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that Abu Sufyan told him directly, mouth to mouth, saying: I set out during the truce that was between me and the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him). He said: While I was in Syria, a letter was brought from the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) to Heraclius, that is, the great one of the Byzantines. He said: Dihyah al-Kalbi had brought it and delivered it to the governor of Busra, who delivered it to Heraclius. Heraclius said: "Is there anyone here from the people of this man who claims to be a prophet?" They said: "Yes." He said: So I was called along with a group of Quraysh, and we entered upon Heraclius, and he seated us before him. He said: "Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?" Abu Sufyan said: I said, "I am," so they seated me before him and seated my companions behind me. Then he called for his interpreter and said to him: "Tell them that I am going to question this man about the one who claims to be a prophet, and if he lies to me, contradict him."

Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, were it not for the fear that lying would be attributed to me, I would have lied. Then he said to his interpreter: "Ask him how is his lineage among you?" I said: "He is of noble lineage among us." He said: "Was any of his forefathers a king?" I said: "No." He said: "Did you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" I said: "No." He said: "Do the noble people follow him, or the weak ones?" I said: "Rather the weak ones." He said: "Are they increasing or decreasing?" I said: "No, rather they are increasing." He said: "Does anyone among them turn back from his religion after having entered it, out of dislike for it?" I said: "No." He said: "Have you fought him?" I said: "Yes." He said: "How was your fighting with him?" I said: "The war between us and him goes back and forth; he inflicts losses on us and we inflict losses on him." He said: "Does he betray trust?" I said: "No, and we are currently in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it." He (Abu Sufyan) said: By Allah, I found no opportunity to insert anything into my speech except this one word.

He said: "Has anyone said this saying before him?" I said: "No." He said to his interpreter: "Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you claimed that he is of noble lineage among you - and thus messengers are sent from among the noble lineages of their people. I asked you whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you claimed not; so I said, had one of his forefathers been a king, I would have said he is a man seeking the kingdom of his forefathers. I asked you about his followers, whether they are the weak or the noble, and you said the weak - and they are the followers of the messengers. I asked you whether you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said, and you claimed not; so I knew that he would not have abstained from lying about people only to go and lie about Allah. I asked you whether anyone turns back from his religion after entering it, out of dislike for it, and you claimed not - and such is faith when it mixes with the joy of hearts. I asked you whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you claimed they are increasing - and such is faith until it is complete. I asked you whether you fought him, and you claimed that you did fight him, and that the war between you goes back and forth, he inflicting losses on you and you inflicting losses on him - and thus the messengers are tested, then the final outcome is theirs. I asked you whether he betrays trust, and you claimed that he does not betray trust - and thus the messengers do not betray trust. I asked you whether anyone said this saying before him, and you claimed not; so I said, had anyone said this saying before him, I would have said he is a man following a saying that was said before him."

He said: Then he said: "What does he command you to do?" I said: "He commands us to pray, to give zakat, to maintain ties of kinship, and to be chaste." He said: "If what you say about him is true, then he is indeed a prophet. I already knew that he was going to appear, but I did not think he would be from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would love to meet him, and if I were with him, I would wash his feet, and his dominion will indeed reach what is beneath my feet."

He said: Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) and read it, and it was:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great one of the Byzantines. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. Now then, I invite you with the call of Islam. Submit and you will be safe, submit and Allah will give you your reward twice over; but if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the peasantry (the common people). And O People of the Book, come to a common word between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and that we associate no partners with Him, and that none of us take others as lords besides Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims (submitters to Allah)."

He said: When he finished reading the letter, voices were raised around him and there was much clamor, and he ordered us to be taken out, so we were taken out. He said: I said to my companions when we went out: "The matter of Ibn Abi Kabshah (i.e., Muhammad) has become significant - indeed the king of the Byzantines fears him!" He said: And I continued to be certain of the matter of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), that he would prevail, until Allah caused Islam to enter into me.
muslim||941: Aisha said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grew heavy (with illness), Bilal came to inform him of the time for prayer, and he said: Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man, and whenever he stands in your place, he will not be able to make the people hear; if only you would command Umar (instead). He said: Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. She said: I then said to Hafsah: Say to him: Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man, and whenever he stands in your place, he will not be able to make the people hear; if only you would command Umar (instead). She said this to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: You are indeed the companions of Yusuf (i.e., you keep insisting). Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. She said: So they commanded Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. She said: When he had entered into the prayer, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) felt some lightness (relief) in himself, so he got up, being supported between two men, his feet dragging along the ground. She said: When he entered the mosque, Abu Bakr heard his movement and started to withdraw, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured to him to remain in his place. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then came and sat down on the left side of Abu Bakr. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led the people in prayer sitting, while Abu Bakr stood; Abu Bakr followed the prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the people followed the prayer of Abu Bakr.
muslim||1004: Qutaybah bin Sa'eed, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq bin Ibrahim all narrated to us, from Jarir - Abu Bakr said: Jarir bin Abdul Hamid narrated to us - from Musa bin Abi 'Aishah, from Sa'eed bin Jubair, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Sublime: "Do not move your tongue with it" (Surah Al-Qiyamah, verse 16), he said: When Gabriel would descend to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with the revelation, he would move his tongue and his lips along with it, and it would be difficult for him, and this could be recognized from him. So Allah, Most High, revealed: "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it" (Surah Al-Qiyamah, verse 16) - meaning, to hasten in grasping it - "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation" (Surah Al-Qiyamah, verse 17) - meaning, it is upon Us to gather it in your breast and its recitation, so that you will recite it - "So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation" (Surah Al-Qiyamah, verse 18), he said: meaning, when We have revealed it, then listen to it - "Indeed, upon Us is its explanation" (Surah Al-Qiyamah, verse 19), meaning, it is upon Us to make it clear through your tongue. So whenever Gabriel came to him, he would listen attentively, and when he had gone, he would recite it just as Allah had promised him.
muslim||1080: Yahya b. Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi'. And Isa b. Hammad al-Misri narrated to me: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid b. Abi Habib, he said: And Harun b. Abdullah narrated to me: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak b. Uthman narrated to us, he said: And al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Yahya, who is al-Qattan, narrated to us, from Ibn Ajlan. And Harun b. Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah b. Zayd narrated to me, he said: And Yahya b. Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il, meaning Ibn Ja'far, narrated to us: Muhammad, who is Ibn Amr, informed me, he said: And Hannad b. al-Sari narrated to me: Abdah narrated to us, from Muhammad b. Ishaq - all of these, from Ibrahim b. Abdullah b. Hunayn, from his father, from Ali - except al-Dahhak and Ibn Ajlan, for they both added: from Ibn Abbas, from Ali, from the Prophet (may peace be upon him) - all of them said: "He forbade me from reciting the Qur'an while I am bowing (in rak'ah)," and they did not mention in their narration the prohibition of it during prostration, as al-Zuhri, Zayd b. Aslam, al-Walid b. Kathir, and Dawud b. Qays mentioned.
muslim||6151: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Hujain bin al-Muthanna told us, 'Abd al-'Aziz bin 'Abdullah bin Abi Salamah told us, from 'Abdullah bin al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurairah, who said: "While a Jewish man was displaying merchandise of his, he was offered something for it which he disliked, or was not satisfied with - 'Abd al-'Aziz was uncertain [about the wording] - and he said: 'No, by the One who chose Musa (peace be upon him) above mankind.' A man from the Ansar heard him and struck him on the face, saying: 'You say: By the One who chose Musa (peace be upon him) above mankind, while the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) is among us?' So the Jewish man went to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: 'O Abu al-Qasim, I have a covenant and a pact [of protection], and so-and-so struck me on the face.' The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'Why did you strike his face?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he said: By the One who chose Musa (peace be upon him) above mankind, while you are among us?' The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) became angry, so that the anger could be seen on his face, then he said: 'Do not give preference among the prophets of Allah, for the Trumpet will be blown, and everyone in the heavens and everyone on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown a second time, and I will be the first to be resurrected, or among the first to be resurrected, and there will be Musa (peace be upon him), holding on to the Throne. I do not know whether he was accounted for his swoon on the Day of the Mount, or whether he was resurrected before me. And I do not say that anyone is better than Yunus bin Matta (peace be upon him).'"
muslim||904: Sa'id b. Mansur, Qutaiba b. Sa'id, Abu Kamil al-Jahdari - and the wording is Abu Kamil's - and Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Malik al-Umawi narrated to us; they said: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Qatada, from Yunus b. Jubair, from Hittan b. 'Abdullah ar-Raqashi, who said: I prayed a prayer with Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and when it was time for the sitting, a man from the group said: "The prayer has been established with righteousness and zakat?" When Abu Musa had finished the prayer and given the salutation, he turned and said: "Which of you said such-and-such words?" The people remained silent. Then he said again: "Which of you said such-and-such words?" The people remained silent. He said: "Perhaps you, Hittan, said it?" He said: "I did not say it, and indeed I feared that you would rebuke me for it." Then a man from the group said: "I said it, and I intended nothing by it but good." Abu Musa said: "Do you not know how you should speak in your prayer? The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) delivered a sermon to us, and made clear to us our way, and taught us our prayer. He said: 'When you pray, straighten your rows, then let one of you lead you. When he says the takbir, say the takbir; and when he recites: "not of those who have earned Your anger, nor of those who have gone astray" (Surat al-Fatiha, verse 7), say: Amin, and Allah will answer you. When he says the takbir and bows, say the takbir and bow, for the imam bows before you and rises before you.'" The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "That compensates for that." "And when he says: 'Allah hears the one who praises Him,' say: 'O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs praise' - Allah will hear you, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said through the tongue of His Prophet (may peace be upon him): 'Allah hears the one who praises Him.' And when he says the takbir and prostrates, say the takbir and prostrate, for the imam prostrates before you and rises before you." The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "That compensates for that." "And when it is time for the sitting, let the first words of each of you be: 'At-tahiyyatu at-tayyibatu, as-salawatu lillah, as-salamu 'alaika ayyuha an-nabiyyu wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh, as-salamu 'alaina wa 'ala 'ibadillahi as-salihin, ashhadu an la ilaha illallah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh.'"
muslim||6381: Qais bin 'Ubad said: I was in Medina among some people, among whom were some of the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), when a man came whose face bore the mark of humility. Some of the people said: This is a man from the people of Paradise, this is a man from the people of Paradise. He prayed two rak'ahs, performing them briefly, then went out, and I followed him. He entered his house and I entered as well, and we talked. When he became at ease, I said to him: When you entered earlier, a man said such and such. He said: Glory be to Allah, no one should say what he does not know. I will tell you why that was: I saw a dream during the time of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and I related it to him. I saw myself in a garden - he mentioned its spaciousness, its herbage, and its greenness - and in the middle of the garden was an iron pillar, its base in the earth and its top in the sky, and at its top was a handhold. It was said to me: Climb it. I said to him: I cannot. Then a servant came to me - Ibn 'Awn said: al-minsaf means the servant - and he said, taking hold of my garment from behind - he described that he lifted him from behind with his hand - so I climbed until I was at the top of the pillar, and I grasped the handhold. It was said to me: Hold fast. Then I woke up, and it was indeed in my hand. I related it to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said: That garden is Islam, that pillar is the pillar of Islam, and that handhold is the firm handhold, and you will remain upon Islam until you die. He said: And the man was 'Abdullah bin Salam.
muslim||6362: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Ar'arah as-Sami and Muhammad bin Hatim narrated to me - and their accounts were close in the sequence of the hadith, and the wording is that of Ibn Hatim - they said: 'Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi narrated to us, al-Muthanna bin Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Jamrah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When news of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) mission reached Abu Dharr in Mecca, he said to his brother: 'Ride to this valley and find out for me about this man who claims that news comes to him from heaven. Listen to what he says, then come back to me.' So the other set off until he arrived at Mecca and heard what he was saying, then he returned to Abu Dharr and said: 'I saw him commanding noble character, and speech that is not poetry.' Abu Dharr said: 'You have not satisfied what I wanted.' So he provisioned himself and carried a waterskin containing water until he arrived at Mecca. He went to the mosque and sought the Prophet (peace be upon him), though he did not know him, and he disliked asking about him. He remained until nightfall overtook him, so he lay down. 'Ali saw him and realized that he was a stranger, and when he saw him he followed him. Neither of them asked the other anything until morning came. Then he carried his waterskin and provisions to the mosque, and he spent that day without seeing the Prophet (peace be upon him) until evening came, so he returned to his sleeping place. 'Ali passed by him and said: 'Has it not yet come time for the man to know his lodging?' So he made him get up and took him along with him, and neither of them asked the other anything. When the third day came, the same thing happened, and 'Ali made him get up to stay with him. Then he said to him: 'Will you not tell me what brought you to this town?' He said: 'If you give me a pledge and a covenant that you will guide me rightly, I will do so.' He did so, and then he told him. 'Ali said: 'It is indeed true, and he is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). When morning comes, follow me, for if I see anything I fear for you, I will stop as if I am relieving myself; if I continue on, then follow me until you enter where I enter.' He did so, and set off following him, until he entered upon the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he entered with him. He heard what he said, and he accepted Islam on the spot. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Return to your people and inform them, until my command comes to you.' He said: 'By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will surely proclaim it loudly among them.' So he went out until he came to the mosque, and he called out at the top of his voice: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' The people rose up and struck him until they had knocked him down. Al-'Abbas came and bent over him, saying: 'Woe to you! Do you not know that he is from Ghifar, and that the route of your traders to Syria passes through their territory?' So he rescued him from them. Then the next day he returned and did the same thing, and they rose up against him and struck him. Al-'Abbas bent over him and rescued him."
muslim||6383: Qutaybah bin Sa'eed and Ishaq bin Ibrahim narrated to us, and the wording is that of Qutaybah: Jarir narrated to us, from Al-A'mash, from Sulaiman bin Mushir, from Kharashah bin Al-Hurr, who said: "I was sitting in a circle in the mosque of Madinah, and in it was an old man of goodly appearance, who was Abdullah bin Salam. He began narrating to them a fine account. When he stood up, the people said: 'Whoever would like to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this one.' I said: 'By Allah, I will surely follow him and find out where his house is.' So I followed him, and he went on until he nearly left Madinah, then he entered his house. I asked permission to enter upon him, and he permitted me, and said: 'What do you need, son of my brother?' I said to him: 'I heard the people, when you stood up, say: Whoever would like to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this one, so I was pleased to be with you.' He said: 'Allah knows best who are the people of Paradise, and I will tell you why they said that: While I was sleeping, a man came to me and said to me: Get up. He took my hand, and I set off with him. Then I saw broad paths to my left. I set out to take one of them, but he said to me: Do not take it, for it is the path of the people of the left. Then there were broad, clear paths to my right, and he said to me: Take this way. Then he brought me to a mountain and said to me: Climb up. Whenever I tried to climb, I would fall on my backside. I did that several times. Then he took me on until he brought me to a pillar, its top in the sky and its bottom in the earth, with a ring at its top, and he said to me: Climb to the top of this. I said: How can I climb this when its top is in the sky? He took my hand and thrust me upward, and I found myself clinging to the ring. Then he struck the pillar and it fell, but I remained clinging to the ring until morning came. Then I went to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and related it to him, and he said: As for the paths you saw on your left, they are the paths of the people of the left. As for the paths you saw on your right, they are the paths of the people of the right. As for the mountain, it is the abode of the martyrs, and you will never attain it. As for the pillar, it is the pillar of Islam. As for the ring, it is the handhold of Islam, and you will continue to cling to it until you die.'"
muslim||6406:
Abdullah bin Barrad Abu Amir al-Ash'ari and Abu Kuraib Muhammad bin al-'Ala' - and the wording is that of Abu Amir - narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said:

"When the Prophet (may peace be upon him) finished with Hunain, he sent Abu Amir with an army to Awtas. He met Duraid bin as-Simmah, and Duraid was killed, and Allah routed his companions." Abu Musa said: "He sent me along with Abu Amir." He said: "Abu Amir was struck in his knee - a man from Banu Jusham shot him with an arrow and it lodged firmly in his knee. I came up to him and said: 'O uncle, who shot you?' Abu Amir pointed to Abu Musa and said: 'That one is my killer, you see him, that is the one who shot me.'"

Abu Musa said: "So I made for him and went after him, and I caught up with him. When he saw me he turned away fleeing, so I followed him and began saying to him: 'Have you no shame? Are you not an Arab? Will you not stand firm?' So he stopped, and I met him, and he and I exchanged two blows, and I struck him with the sword and killed him.

Then I returned to Abu Amir and said: 'Allah has killed your enemy.' He said: 'Pull out this arrow.' So I pulled it out, and water spurted from it. He said: 'O son of my brother, go to the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) and convey my greetings to him, and tell him: Abu Amir says to you, ask forgiveness for me.'"

He said: "Abu Amir appointed me over the people, and he remained for a short while, then he died. When I returned to the Prophet (may peace be upon him), I entered upon him while he was in a room, on a bed woven with palm-fiber cords, with a mattress over it, and the cords of the bed had left marks on the back and sides of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him). I informed him of our news and the news of Abu Amir, and I told him what he had said: 'Tell him to ask forgiveness for me.'"

So the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) called for water, performed ablution with it, then raised his hands and said: "O Allah, forgive Ubaid Abu Amir," until I saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said: "O Allah, make him on the Day of Resurrection above many of Your creation," or "above many of the people."

I said: "And for me too, O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness." So the Prophet (may peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, forgive Abdullah bin Qais his sin, and admit him on the Day of Resurrection to a noble entrance."

Abu Burdah said: "One of the two [prayers] was for Abu Amir, and the other was for Abu Musa."
muslim||6395:
Abdul Malik bin Shu'aib bin Al-Laith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, Khalid bin Yazid narrated to me, Sa'eed bin Abi Hilal narrated to me, from 'Umarah bin Ghaziyyah, from Muhammad bin Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah bin Abdur-Rahman, from Aishah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Satirize the Quraysh, for that is harder on them than being pelted with arrows." So he sent for Ibn Rawahah and said: "Satirize them." So he satirized them, but it did not satisfy him. Then he sent for Ka'b bin Malik, then he sent for Hassan bin Thabit. When he entered upon him, Hassan said: "It is time for you to send for this lion who strikes with its tail." Then he stuck out his tongue and began moving it, and said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will tear them apart with my tongue as one tears apart a piece of leather." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not be hasty, for Abu Bakr is the most knowledgeable of Quraysh regarding their genealogies, and I have lineage among them, so let him clarify my lineage for you." So Hassan went to him, then came back and said: "O Messenger of Allah, he has clarified your lineage for me, and by the One Who sent you with the truth, I will pull you out from among them just as a hair is pulled out from dough."

Aishah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Hassan: "The Holy Spirit will continue to support you as long as you defend Allah and His Messenger."

And she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Hassan satirized them, and thus healed and was healed."

Hassan said: "You satirized Muhammad, so I answered on his behalf, and with Allah lies the reward for that":

"You satirized Muhammad, the righteous, the pious, the Messenger of Allah, whose characteristic is faithfulness.
Indeed my father, his father, and my honor are a shield for the honor of Muhammad against you.
May I be bereaved of my little daughter if you do not see them
Raising the dust from the two sides of Kada,
Racing alongside the reins, ascending,
Upon their shoulders the thirsty spearheads.
Our steeds remain drenched with sweat,
The women striking them with their veils.
If you turn away from us, we shall make the 'Umrah,
And the conquest will come, and the veil will be lifted.
And if not, then be patient for a day of striking
In which Allah will grant honor to whom He wills.
And Allah has said: I have sent a servant
Who speaks the truth, in which there is no concealment.
And Allah has said: I have prepared an army,
They are the Ansar, whose habit is confrontation.
For us, every day from Ma'add,
There is abuse, or fighting, or satire.
So whoever among you satirizes the Messenger of Allah,
And whoever praises him and supports him, are not equal.
And Gabriel, the messenger of Allah, is among us,
And the Holy Spirit, who has no equal."
muslim||6163:
Amr bin Muhammad An-Naqid, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Hanzali, Ubaidullah bin Sa'id, and Muhammad bin Abi 'Umar Al-Makki all narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah - and the wording is that of Ibn Abi 'Umar - Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah narrated to us, Amr bin Dinar narrated to us, from Sa'id bin Jubair who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: Nawf Al-Bikali claims that Musa (peace be upon him), the companion of the Children of Israel, is not the same Musa who was the companion of Al-Khidr (peace be upon him). Ibn 'Abbas said: The enemy of Allah has lied. I heard Ubayy bin Ka'b say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) say: "Musa (peace be upon him) stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel, and he was asked: 'Who among the people is most knowledgeable?' He said: 'I am the most knowledgeable.' Allah reproached him for this, since he did not attribute the knowledge back to Him. So Allah revealed to him: 'There is a servant of Mine at the junction of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you.' Musa said: 'O Lord, how can I meet him?' It was said to him: 'Carry a fish in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, he will be there.' So he set off, and his young companion, Yusha' bin Nun, went with him. Musa (peace be upon him) carried a fish in a basket, and he and his young companion walked until they reached the rock. Musa (peace be upon him) and his companion lay down to sleep, and the fish thrashed about in the basket until it slipped out of the basket and fell into the sea. Allah held back the flow of water from it, so it became like an arch, and it was a tunnel for the fish, and it was a wonder for Musa and his young companion. They continued walking for the rest of that day and night, and Musa's companion forgot to tell him. When morning came, Musa (peace be upon him) said to his young companion: 'Bring us our morning meal; we have certainly suffered fatigue from this journey of ours.' He did not feel fatigue until he had passed beyond the place he had been commanded to reach. His companion said: 'Do you remember when we took shelter at the rock? I forgot the fish there, and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan, and it took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner.' Musa said: 'That is what we were seeking.' So they turned back, retracing their footsteps. He said: they were retracing their steps until they reached the rock, and there they saw a man covered with a garment. Musa greeted him with salam, and Al-Khidr said to him: 'How does one greet with salam in this land?' He said: 'I am Musa.' Al-Khidr said: 'Musa of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'Yes.' Al-Khidr said: 'You have knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which Allah has taught you that I do not know, and I have knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which He has taught me that you do not know.' Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: 'May I follow you so that you may teach me something of the right guidance which you have been taught?' He said: 'You will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience about something over which you have no comprehensive knowledge?' Musa said: 'You will find me patient, if Allah wills, and I will not disobey any order of yours.' Al-Khidr said to him: 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself make mention of it to you.' Musa said: 'Agreed.' So Al-Khidr and Musa set off, walking along the seashore, and a ship passed by them. They spoke to the crew so that they would carry them aboard. They recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without any fare. Al-Khidr then went to one of the planks of the ship and pulled it out. Musa said to him: 'These people carried us without charging any fare, and you went and made a hole in their ship so as to drown its passengers! You have indeed done a grave thing.' Al-Khidr said: 'Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?' Musa said: 'Do not take me to task for what I forgot, and do not be hard upon me for my error.' Then they disembarked from the ship, and while they were walking along the shore, they came upon a boy playing with other boys. Al-Khidr took hold of his head and pulled it off with his hand, killing him. Musa said: 'Have you killed a pure soul who had killed no one? You have indeed done a horrible thing.' Al-Khidr said: 'Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?' Musa said: 'This is worse than the first.' Musa said: 'If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me in your company. You have found in me sufficient excuse.' They continued until they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, but they refused to entertain them as guests. There they found a wall about to collapse, and Al-Khidr set it upright.' Al-Khidr gestured with his hand like this and set it upright. Musa said to him: 'These are people we came to, and they did not entertain us as guests nor feed us. Had you wished, you could have taken payment for this.' Al-Khidr said: 'This is the parting between me and you. I will now inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.'"

The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "May Allah have mercy on Musa. I wish he had been patient so that more of their story could have been narrated to us."

The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) also said: "The first of these actions by Musa was due to forgetfulness."

He said: A sparrow came and landed on the edge of the ship, then dipped its beak into the sea, and Al-Khidr said to him: "My knowledge and your knowledge have not decreased the knowledge of Allah except as much as this sparrow has decreased the sea."

Sa'id bin Jubair said: And he [Ibn Abbas] used to recite: "And there was ahead of them a king who seized every good ship by force," and he used to recite: "As for the boy, he was a disbeliever."
muslim||6572: Abdullah bin Abdur Rahman bin Bahram Ad-Darimi narrated to us, Marwan - meaning ibn Muhammad Ad-Dimashqi - narrated to us, Sa'id bin Abdul Aziz narrated to us, from Rabi'ah bin Yazid, from Abu Idris Al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding what he reported from Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, that He said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not commit injustice against one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except one whom I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except one whom I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except one whom I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, you would never be able to reach Me in order to harm Me, nor would you ever be able to reach Me in order to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and the human among you and the jinn among you, were all as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not add anything to My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and the human among you and the jinn among you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man, that would not decrease anything from My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and the human among you and the jinn among you, were to stand in one place and ask of Me, and I gave everyone what he asked for, that would not decrease what I have, except as much as a needle decreases the ocean if it is dipped into it. O My servants, it is but your deeds that I record for you, and then I recompense you for them, so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself." Sa'id said: Abu Idris Al-Khawlani, when he narrated this hadith, would kneel down on his knees.
muslim||6739: Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Hanzali narrated to us, Uthman bin Umar narrated to us, Azrah bin Thabit narrated to us, from Yahya bin Uqayl, from Yahya bin Ya'mar, from Abu Al-Aswad Ad-Dili who said: Imran bin Husain said to me: "Tell me, what people do today and strive hard at - is it something that has been decreed for them and has already passed upon them from a decree that preceded, or is it in what they are to encounter from what their Prophet brought them and by which the proof has been established against them?" I said: "Rather, it is something that has been decreed for them and has already passed upon them." He said: "Would that not then be injustice?" He said: I was struck with intense alarm at that, and I said: "Everything is the creation of Allah and the possession of His hand, so He is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned." He said to me: "May Allah have mercy on you. I only intended by what I asked you to test your understanding. Two men from Muzainah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell us, what people do today and strive hard at - is it something that has been decreed for them and has already passed upon them from a decree that preceded, or is it in what they are to encounter from what their Prophet brought them and by which the proof has been established against them?' He said: 'No, rather it is something that has been decreed for them and has already passed upon them, and the confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Sublime: "By the soul and He who perfected it, and inspired it with discernment of its wickedness and its righteousness."'"
muslim||6509: Zuhair bin Harb narrated to us, Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, Jarir bin Hazim informed us, Muhammad bin Sirin narrated to us, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "None spoke in the cradle except three: Jesus son of Mary, the companion of Juraij, and Juraij was a worshipper who took up a hermitage and dwelt in it. His mother came to him while he was praying, and she said: 'O Juraij!' He said: 'O Lord, my mother or my prayer?' and he continued with his prayer, so she left. The next day she came to him while he was praying, and she said: 'O Juraij!' He said: 'O Lord, my mother or my prayer?' and he continued with his prayer, so she left. The next day she came to him while he was praying, and she said: 'O Juraij!' He said: 'O Lord, my mother or my prayer?' and he continued with his prayer. So she said: 'O Allah, do not let him die until he has looked upon the faces of prostitutes.' The Children of Israel then spoke of Juraij and his worship, and there was a harlot renowned for her beauty who said: 'If you wish, I will tempt him for you.' She presented herself to him but he paid no attention to her. So she went to a shepherd who used to take shelter near his hermitage, and she allowed him to have relations with her, and he had intercourse with her, and she conceived. When she gave birth, she said: 'This child is from Juraij.' They went to him and brought him down and demolished his hermitage, and began to beat him. He said: 'What is the matter with you?' They said: 'You fornicated with this harlot and she has borne a child from you.' He said: 'Where is the child?' So they brought the child to him. He said: 'Let me pray.' So he prayed, and when he finished, he went to the child and poked him in the stomach, and said: 'O boy, who is your father?' The child said: 'So-and-so, the shepherd.' So they turned to Juraij, kissing him and touching him for blessing, and they said: 'We will build your hermitage for you out of gold.' He said: 'No, rebuild it with clay as it was.' So they did. And [as for] the child who nursed from his mother, a man passed by riding a fine mount with fine trappings, and his mother said: 'O Allah, make my son like this man.' So the child left the breast and turned to look at him, and said: 'O Allah, do not make me like him.' Then he turned back to the breast and resumed nursing." He [Abu Hurairah] said: "It is as if I can see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) demonstrating his nursing with his forefinger in his mouth, sucking it." He said: "And they passed by a slave-girl while they were beating her, saying: 'You committed fornication, you stole,' while she was saying: 'Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best guardian.' So his mother said: 'O Allah, do not make my son like her.' So the child left off nursing and looked at her, and said: 'O Allah, make me like her.' At that point the two of them exchanged words, and she said: 'May you be bereaved! A handsome man passed by and I said: O Allah, make my son like him, and you said: O Allah, do not make me like him. And they passed by this slave-girl while they were beating her, saying: You committed fornication, you stole, and I said: O Allah, do not make my son like her, and you said: O Allah, make me like her.' He said: 'That man was a tyrant, so I said: O Allah, do not make me like him. And this woman, they say of her: You committed fornication, when she did not fornicate, and you stole, when she did not steal; so I said: O Allah, make me like her.'"
muslim||1199: Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin As-Sabbah and Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaibah - and their wordings were close to one another - narrated to us, they said: Isma'il bin Ibrahim narrated to us, from Hajjaj As-Sawwaf, from Yahya bin Abi Kathir, from Hilal bin Abi Maimunah, from Ata' bin Yasar, from Mu'awiyah bin Al-Hakam As-Sulami who said: While I was praying with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man among the people sneezed, so I said: "May Allah have mercy on you." The people stared at me with their eyes, so I said: "Woe to my mother! What is the matter with you that you are looking at me?" They began striking their hands upon their thighs, and when I saw them silencing me, I fell silent. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished praying - and by my father and mother, I have never seen a teacher before or after him better in teaching than him - by Allah, he did not rebuke me, nor did he strike me, nor did he revile me. He said: "This prayer, nothing of the speech of people is proper in it. It is only glorification of Allah, exalting Him, and recitation of the Qur'an," or words to that effect as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have only recently emerged from ignorance (Jahiliyyah), and Allah has now brought Islam, and among us there are men who go to soothsayers." He said: "Do not go to them." I said: "And among us there are men who take omens (are superstitious about signs)." He said: "That is something they find in their breasts, so let it not deter them." Ibn As-Sabbah said [in his version]: "So let it not deter you." I said: "And among us there are men who draw lines (in divination)." He said: "There was a prophet among the prophets who used to draw lines, so whoever's line matches his, that is it." He said: I had a slave girl who used to tend sheep of mine near Uhud and Al-Jawwaniyyah. One day I looked over and found that a wolf had taken one of her sheep - and I am but a man from the sons of Adam, I feel grief just as they feel grief - but I struck her a blow. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he made that seem a grave matter to me. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not free her?" He said: "Bring her to me." So I brought her to him, and he said to her: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He said: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer."
muslim||4678:
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us. (Another chain:) And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi informed us - both of them from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar. (Another chain:) And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi told us - and this is his wording - Abu 'Ali al-Hanafi 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abd al-Majid informed us: 'Ikrimah, that is, ibn 'Ammar, told us: Iyas ibn Salamah told me: My father told me, he said:

"We came to al-Hudaybiyah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and we were fourteen hundred men, with fifty sheep that could not satisfy [our thirst if we had to rely on water for them alone – i.e. water was scarce]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat at the edge of the well, and either he prayed or he spat into it, and it gushed forth, so we drank and drew water for ourselves.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called us for the pledge of allegiance beneath the tree. I gave him my pledge first among the people, then others pledged one after another, until when he was in the middle of the people he said: 'Give the pledge, O Salamah.' I said: 'I have already pledged to you, O Messenger of Allah, at the very first of the people.' He said: 'Do so again.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw me without any weapon, so he gave me a small round shield or a leather shield. Then he continued taking pledges until, when he was at the end of the people, he said: 'Will you not pledge to me, O Salamah?' I said: 'I have already pledged to you, O Messenger of Allah, at the beginning of the people and in the middle of the people.' He said: 'Do so again,' so I pledged to him a third time.

Then he said to me: 'O Salamah, where is your shield that I gave you?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my uncle 'Amir met me without a weapon, so I gave it to him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and said: 'You are like the one who said: O Allah, grant me a beloved companion who is dearer to me than myself.'

Then the polytheists sent messages to us seeking peace, until some of us mixed with others and we made peace. I was a follower of Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah - I watered his horse, groomed it, served him, and ate from his food - having left my family and wealth, emigrating to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ).

When we and the people of Makkah made peace and mixed with one another, I went to a tree and cleared away its thorns, then lay down at its base. Four polytheists from the people of Makkah came to me and began to speak ill of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I disliked them and moved to another tree. They hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, a caller called out from the bottom of the valley: 'O Muhajirun, Ibn Zunaym has been killed!' So I drew my sword and rushed upon those four while they were sleeping, and I took their weapons and gathered them in a bundle in my hand. Then I said: 'By the One who honored the face of Muhammad, none of you shall raise his head but I will strike the place where his eyes are.' Then I brought them, driving them before me, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

My uncle 'Amir also came with a man from the 'Abalat called Mikraz, leading him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a horse, armored, along with seventy of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at them and said: 'Leave them - let the beginning of the wrongdoing and its repetition be upon them,' and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pardoned them. Then Allah revealed: 'And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within Makkah after He had given you victory over them' (Surah al-Fath, 48:24) - the whole verse.

Then we set out returning to Madinah, and we camped at a place where there was a mountain between us and Banu Lihyan, who were polytheists. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sought forgiveness for whoever would climb this mountain that night, as if he would be a lookout for the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. Salamah said: I climbed it that night twice or three times.

Then we came to Madinah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent the pack animals with Rabah, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I was with him. I went out with him with Talhah's horse, to graze it along with the pack animals. When morning came, 'Abd al-Rahman al-Fazari had raided the pack animals of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), driving them all away and killing the shepherd.

I said: 'O Rabah, take this horse and deliver it to Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, and inform the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that the polytheists have raided his grazing animals.' Then I stood on a hillock, facing Madinah, and called out three times: 'O people, to arms!' Then I went out following the tracks of the group, shooting arrows at them and reciting verses, saying: 'I am the son of al-Akwa', and today is the day of the lowly ones!' I caught up with a man of them and struck him with an arrow in his saddle-pack until the arrowhead reached his shoulder. I said: 'Take this - I am the son of al-Akwa', and today is the day of the lowly ones!'

By Allah, I continued shooting at them and hamstringing their horses. Whenever a horseman turned back toward me, I would go to a tree and sit at its base, then shoot at him and hamstring his mount, until when the mountain pass narrowed and they entered its narrow part, I climbed the mountain and began throwing stones down on them. I continued like that, following them, until Allah left none of the camels of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) pack animals except that I drove it back behind me, and they left it between me and them. Then I continued following them, shooting at them, until they threw down more than thirty cloaks and thirty spears, trying to lighten their load. They did not throw down anything without my placing markers of stones over it, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions would recognize.

Until they came to a narrow mountain pass, where a certain man, Ibn Badr al-Fazari, met them, and they sat down to have their midday meal. I sat on the top of a hill. Al-Fazari said: 'What is this that I see?' They said: 'We have suffered hardship from this man - by Allah, he has not left us since dawn, shooting at us until he has stripped everything from our hands.' He said: 'Let four men of you go up to him.' So four of them climbed up the mountain toward me. When they were within speaking range, I said: 'Do you know me?' They said: 'No, who are you?' I said: 'I am Salamah ibn al-Akwa'. By the One who honored the face of Muhammad (ﷺ), I will not pursue any man of you but I will catch him, and no man of you will pursue me and catch me.' One of them said: 'I think that's true.' So they went back.

I did not move from my place until I saw the horsemen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threading through the trees. The first of them was al-Akhram al-Asadi, followed by Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, followed by al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi. I took hold of al-Akhram's reins as they [the enemy] turned to flee. I said: 'O Akhram, beware of them, lest they cut you off before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions catch up.' He said: 'O Salamah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day, and know that Paradise is true and the Fire is true, do not come between me and martyrdom.' So I let him go, and he met 'Abd al-Rahman. He hamstrung 'Abd al-Rahman's horse, and 'Abd al-Rahman stabbed him and killed him, then turned onto his horse. Abu Qatadah, the horseman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), caught up with 'Abd al-Rahman and stabbed him, killing him.

By the One who honored the face of Muhammad (ﷺ), I followed them running on my own two feet, until I could no longer see any of the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) behind me, nor any dust of theirs, until they turned before sunset toward a mountain pass with water in it called Dhu Qarad, to drink from it, being thirsty. They saw me running behind them, so I drove them away from it, and they did not taste a drop of it. They went out and hurried onward through a mountain pass. I ran and caught up with a man of them and struck him with an arrow in the top of his shoulder. I said: 'Take this - I am the son of al-Akwa', and today is the day of the lowly ones!' He said: 'May his mother be bereaved of him - is this Akwa' at dawn?' I said: 'Yes, O enemy of yourself, this is your Akwa' at dawn.'

They abandoned two horses at a mountain pass, and I brought them, driving them, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). 'Amir caught up with me with a water-skin containing some diluted milk and another water-skin containing water, so I performed ablution and drank. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was at the water from which I had driven them away. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had taken those camels and everything I had recovered from the polytheists, every spear and cloak. Bilal had slaughtered a camel from among those I had recovered from the group, and he was roasting some of its liver and hump for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, let me go and I will select a hundred men from the people and pursue the group, so that not one of them who could report [what happened] will remain but I will kill him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed in the light of the fire, and said: 'O Salamah, do you think you could do that?' I said: 'Yes, by the One who has honored you.'
