He said: 'They are now being given hospitality in the land of Ghatafan.'

Then a man from Ghatafan came and said: 'A certain man slaughtered a camel for them, and when they skinned it, they saw dust [of approaching riders], and said: "The enemy has come upon you!" so they fled.'

When morning came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best of our horsemen today was Abu Qatadah, and the best of our footmen was Salamah.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me two shares - the share of a horseman and the share of a footman - combining them both for me. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had me ride behind him on al-'Adba', returning to Madinah.

While we were traveling, there was a man from the Ansar who could not be outrun in a race. He kept saying: 'Is there anyone to race to Madinah? Is there a racer?' He kept repeating this. When I heard what he said, I said: 'Will you not honor someone honorable, nor fear someone noble?' He said: 'No, unless it is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by my father and mother, let me race the man.' He said: 'If you wish.' I said [to the man]: 'Go on then,' and I bent my legs and leapt up and ran. I paced myself for a stretch or two, conserving my breath, then ran after him, pacing myself for another stretch or two. Then I put on speed until I caught up with him, and I struck him between his shoulders. I said: 'You have been outrun, by Allah!' He said: 'I think so.' So I outran him to Madinah.

By Allah, we had not stayed but three nights when we set out to Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). My uncle 'Amir began reciting verses of poetry to the people: 'By Allah, were it not for Allah, we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed. And we cannot do without Your favor, so make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy], and send down tranquility upon us.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'I am 'Amir.' He said: 'May your Lord forgive you.' And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never sought forgiveness specifically for a person except that he was martyred. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who was on his camel, called out: 'O Prophet of Allah, if only you had let us enjoy 'Amir [longer]!'

When we arrived at Khaybar, their king Marhab came out brandishing his sword and saying: 'Khaybar knows well that I am Marhab, well-armed, a tried and tested hero, when wars come blazing forth.' My uncle 'Amir came forward to face him and said: 'Khaybar knows well that I am 'Amir, well-armed, a daring hero.' They exchanged two strikes, and Marhab's sword struck 'Amir's shield, and 'Amir went to strike low at him, but his sword rebounded upon himself and cut his own artery, and that was the cause of his death.

Salamah said: I went out, and there were some men from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) saying: ''Amir's deed is nullified - he killed himself.' I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) weeping, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, 'Amir's deed is nullified!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever said that has lied. Rather, he has his reward twice over.'

Then he sent me to 'Ali, who had an eye ailment, saying: 'I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, or whom Allah and His Messenger love.' I went and brought 'Ali, leading him by the hand while his eyes were sore, until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who spat in his eyes, and he was cured. He gave him the banner, and Marhab came out and said: 'Khaybar knows well that I am Marhab, well-armed, a tried and tested hero, when wars come blazing forth.' 'Ali said: 'I am the one whom my mother named Haydarah, like a lion of the forests, fearsome in appearance. I will give them full measure with the measure of the sandarah.' Then he struck Marhab's head and killed him, and the conquest was achieved through his hands."

Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told us, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, this hadith in its full length. And Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi al-Sulami told us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad told us, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, similarly.
muslim||7207: Abu Ghassan Al-Mismai, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar ibn Uthman narrated to me - and the wording is that of Abu Ghassan and Ibn al-Muthanna - they said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, from Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, that the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said one day in his sermon: "Indeed, my Lord has commanded me to teach you what you did not know from what He taught me this day of mine. Every wealth I have granted to a servant is lawful. I created My servants all as monotheists (hunafa'), but the devils came to them and turned them away from their religion, and forbade them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me that for which I had sent down no authority. And indeed, Allah looked at the people of the earth and became angry with them, Arabs and non-Arabs alike, except for remnants from the People of the Book." And He said: "I have only sent you to test you and to test [others] through you, and I have sent down to you a Book which water cannot wash away, which you recite while asleep and while awake." And indeed, Allah commanded me to burn the Quraysh, and I said: "My Lord, then they will crush my head and leave it like a loaf of bread!" He said: "Drive them out as they drove you out, and fight them and We will help you fight, and spend and We shall spend on you, and send out an army and We will send five times its like, and fight, with those who obey you, those who disobey you." He said: "The people of Paradise are three: one possessing authority who is just, charitable, and rightly guided; a man who is merciful and tender-hearted towards every relative and every Muslim; and a man who is chaste, self-restraining, and has dependents." He said: "And the people of the Fire are five: the weak one who has no restraint, those who are followers among you, seeking neither family nor wealth; the treacherous one whose greed cannot be concealed, for even in the smallest matter he betrays; a man who does not spend a morning or an evening except that he is scheming to deceive you regarding your family and your wealth" - and he mentioned miserliness or lying - "and the foul-mouthed, obscene person." Abu Ghassan did not mention in his hadith the phrase "and spend and We shall spend on you."
muslim||1563: And Ahmad ibn Sa'eed ibn Sakhr ad-Darimi narrated to me: 'Ubaidullah ibn Abdul-Majid narrated to us: Salm ibn Zarir al-'Utaridi narrated to us, he said: I heard Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, from Imran ibn Husain, who said: "I was with the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey of his. We traveled through the night until, when it was near dawn, we halted and were overcome by sleep until the sun had risen. He said: The first of us to wake up was Abu Bakr, and we would never wake the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from his sleep, if he slept, until he woke up himself. Then Umar woke up and stood by the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and began to say the takbir, raising his voice with it, until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke up. When he raised his head and saw that the sun had risen, he said: 'Move on.' So he traveled on with us until, when the sun had turned white, he stopped and led us in the morning prayer. A man among the people withdrew and did not pray with us. When he finished, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: 'O so-and-so, what kept you from praying with us?' He said: 'O Prophet of Allah, I had a state of major impurity (janabah).' So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered him, and he performed tayammum with the earth (dust), and then prayed. Then he sent me ahead with a group of riders before him in search of water, for we had become extremely thirsty. While we were traveling, we suddenly came upon a woman with her legs dangling between two water-skins. We said to her: 'Where is water?' She said: 'Ayhah, ayhah (i.e., there is none), there is no water for you.' We said: 'How far is it between your family and the water?' She said: 'A day and a night's journey.' We said: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.' She said: 'And who is the Messenger of Allah?' We did not let her have any say in the matter, until we took her with us, and we brought her before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He questioned her, and she told him the same as she had told us, and she informed him that she was a widow with orphan children of her own. So he ordered her water-carrier (camel) to be brought, and it was made to kneel down. He then spat into the two upper water-skins' openings, and sent the water-carrier back. We drank from it, forty thirsty men, until we were satisfied and filled every water-skin and container we had with us, and we washed our companion, but we did not give any water to the camel to drink, while the two water-skins were nearly bursting with water. Then he said: 'Bring whatever you have.' So we collected for her pieces of bread and dates, and tied it up in a bundle for her, and said to her: 'Go and feed your family with this, and know that we have not diminished your water at all.' When she returned to her family, she said: 'I have met the most magical of people, or he is indeed a prophet as he claims. Such and such happened with him.' So Allah guided that group of people through that woman, and she embraced Islam, and they embraced Islam."
muslim||2008: Ishaq b. Ibrahim and Muhammad b. al-Muthanna both narrated it from 'Abd al-A'la - Ibn al-Muthanna said: 'Abd al-A'la, who is Abu Hammam, narrated to me - Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amr b. Sa'id, from Sa'id b. Jubair, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Dimad came to Makkah - he was from Azd Shanu'ah - and he used to recite charms against this affliction (madness). He heard some foolish people among the people of Makkah saying that Muhammad was possessed by jinn (mad), so he said: If I could only see this man, perhaps Allah would grant healing at my hands. He (the narrator) said: So he met him and said: O Muhammad, I recite charms against this affliction, and Allah grants healing through my hands to whomever He wills. So would you like (that I treat you)? The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "Praise be to Allah, we praise Him and seek His help. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Now then..." He (Dimad) said: Repeat these words of yours to me. So the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) repeated them to him three times. He said: I have heard the speech of soothsayers, and the speech of sorcerers, and the speech of poets, but I have never heard anything like these words of yours, and indeed they have reached the depths of the sea. He said: Give me your hand, that I may pledge allegiance to you upon Islam. So he pledged allegiance to him. The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said: "And on behalf of your people (too)." He said: And on behalf of my people. He (the narrator) said: Then the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) sent out a raiding party, and they passed by his people. The leader of the raiding party said to the army: Have you taken anything from these people? A man among the group said: I took a water-vessel from them. He said: Return it, for these are the people of Dimad.
muslim||1930:
Ahmad b. Ja'far al-Ma'qiri narrated to me, Nadr b. Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ikrimah b. 'Ammar narrated to us, Shaddad b. 'Abdullah Abu 'Ammar and Yahya b. Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abu Umamah. 'Ikrimah said: Shaddad met Abu Umamah and Wathilah, and accompanied Anas to Syria, and spoke well of him, praising his excellence and goodness - from Abu Umamah, who said: 'Amr b. 'Abasah al-Sulami said:

While I was still in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance, I used to think that the people were in error and that they had nothing (of true guidance), for they worshipped idols. Then I heard of a man in Makkah who was giving out information (about the truth), so I mounted my riding-beast and went to him. I found that the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) was concealing himself, for his own people were treating him with hostility. I proceeded cautiously until I managed to get to him in Makkah, and I said to him: "What are you?" He said: "I am a Prophet." I said: "What is a Prophet?" He said: "Allah has sent me." I said: "With what has He sent you?" He said: "He has sent me to command the ties of kinship to be honored, idols to be smashed, and that Allah should be affirmed as One, with nothing associated with Him in worship." I said to him: "Who is with you in this?" He said: "A free man and a slave." He said: With him at that time were Abu Bakr and Bilal, among those who had believed in him. I said: "I shall follow you." He said: "You will not be able to do that today. Do you not see my condition and the condition of the people? But go back to your family, and when you hear that I have prevailed, then come to me."

He said: So I went to my family, and the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) went on to Madinah. I remained with my family, seeking out information and asking people about him after he had arrived in Madinah, until there came to me a group from the people of Yathrib, from the people of Madinah, and I said: "What has this man done, the one who came to Madinah?" They said: "The people are flocking to him rapidly, and his own people wanted to kill him but were unable to do so." So I went to Madinah and entered upon him, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you recognize me?" He said: "Yes, you are the one who met me at Makkah." I said: "Indeed I am." Then I said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me about what Allah has taught you that I do not know. Tell me about prayer." He said: "Pray the dawn prayer, then refrain from prayer until the sun rises and clears (the horizon), for it rises between the two horns of Satan, and at that time the disbelievers prostrate themselves to it. Then pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended (by angels), until the shadow of a spear reaches its shortest length. Then refrain from prayer, for at that time Hell is stoked up. Then, when the shade comes forward, pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended (by angels), until you have prayed the afternoon prayer. Then refrain from prayer until the sun sets, for it sets between the two horns of Satan, and at that time the disbelievers prostrate themselves to it."

He said: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me about ablution." He said: "There is not one of you who brings his water for ablution, then rinses his mouth and sniffs water into his nose and blows it out, but the sins of his face and mouth and nostrils fall away. Then when he washes his face as Allah has commanded him, the sins of his face fall away from the tips of his beard along with the water. Then he washes his hands up to the elbows, and the sins of his hands fall away from his fingertips along with the water. Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head fall away from the tips of his hair along with the water. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet fall away from his toes along with the water. Then, if he stands and prays, praising Allah, extolling Him and glorifying Him as He deserves, and empties his heart for Allah, he departs from his sin in a state like the day his mother bore him."

'Amr b. 'Abasah related this hadith to Abu Umamah, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and Abu Umamah said to him: "O 'Amr b. 'Abasah, consider what you are saying: that a man is given all this in a single moment!" 'Amr said: "O Abu Umamah, my age has grown great, my bones have grown frail, and my death has drawn near, and I have no need to lie about Allah or about the Messenger of Allah. Had I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) only once, or twice, or three times - and he counted up to seven times - I would never have related it. But I heard it from him more than that."
muslim||1739: Muhammad bin al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Zurarah, that Sa'd bin Hisham bin 'Amir intended to go on a military expedition in the path of Allah, so he came to Medina and wanted to sell some property he had there, put the proceeds into weapons and horses, and fight the Romans until he died. When he arrived in Medina, he met some people from among the people of Medina who forbade him from doing that, and informed him that a group of six men had intended to do the same thing during the lifetime of the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), but the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade them and said: "Do you not have in me an example to follow?" When they told him this, he took back his wife, whom he had divorced, and had witnesses testify to his taking her back. Then he went to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about the witr of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Ibn 'Abbas said: "Shall I not direct you to the most knowledgeable person on earth regarding the witr of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" He said: "Who?" He said: "'A'ishah. Go to her and ask her, then come back to me and tell me her response." So I went to her, and I came upon Hakim bin Aflah, and I asked him to accompany me to her. He said: "I will not go near her, because I forbade her from saying anything about these two factions, but she insisted on continuing to speak about them." He said: So I swore an oath to him [insisting he come], so he came, and we went to 'A'ishah and asked permission to enter upon her. She gave us permission, and we entered upon her. She said: "Is that Hakim?" - recognizing him. He said: "Yes." She said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Sa'd bin Hisham." She said: "Who is Hisham?" He said: "Ibn 'Amir." She then asked for mercy upon him and spoke well of him. Qatadah said: He had been wounded on the day of Uhud. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes indeed." She said: "The character of the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was the Qur'an." He said: I then thought of getting up and not asking anyone about anything until I died, but then it occurred to me [to ask further], so I said: "Tell me about the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." She said: "Do you not recite: 'O you who wraps himself [in clothing]' (Surah al-Muzzammil, 73:1)?" I said: "Yes indeed." She said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and his companions stood in prayer for a year, and Allah withheld the closing verse of it in heaven for twelve months, until Allah sent down at the end of this surah the relaxation [of the obligation], so the night prayer became voluntary after having been obligatory." He said: I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the witr of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." She said: "We used to prepare for him his tooth-stick and his water for purification, and Allah would wake him at whatever time He willed during the night. He would use the tooth-stick, perform ablution, and pray nine units [rak'ahs], not sitting in any of them except in the eighth. He would remember Allah, praise Him, and supplicate to Him, then rise without giving the greeting of peace [salam]. Then he would stand and pray the ninth, then sit and remember Allah, praise Him, and supplicate to Him, then give the salutation of peace loud enough for us to hear. Then he would pray two units after giving the salutation while sitting. That makes eleven units, my son. When the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) grew older and put on weight, he prayed witr with seven units, and did with the two units the same as he had done before. That makes nine, my son. The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), when he prayed a prayer, loved to maintain it regularly, and when sleep or illness overcame him and prevented him from the night prayer, he would pray twelve units during the day. I do not know of the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ever having recited the entire Qur'an in one night, nor praying an entire night until dawn, nor fasting a complete month other than Ramadan." He said: So I went to Ibn 'Abbas and related to him her account, and he said: "She has spoken the truth. If I were closer to her or could enter upon her, I would go to her so that she could tell me this directly." He said: I said: "Had I known that you would not enter upon her, I would not have related her account to you."
muslim||7511:
Hadhdhab ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said:

"There was a king among those who came before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old, so send me a young boy that I may teach him magic.' So the king sent him a boy to teach him. On his way (to the sorcerer), the boy would pass by a monk, and he sat with him and listened to his speech, and it pleased him. So whenever he went to the sorcerer, he would pass by the monk and sit with him. Then when he came to the sorcerer, the sorcerer would beat him. He complained about this to the monk, who said: 'When you fear the sorcerer, say: My family detained me; and when you fear your family, say: The sorcerer detained me.'

While things were like this, he came upon a huge beast that had blocked the people's way. He said: 'Today I shall know whether the sorcerer or the monk is more excellent.' So he took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the matter of the monk is more pleasing to You than the matter of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so that the people may pass.' He threw the stone at it and killed it, and the people passed by. He then went to the monk and told him what had happened. The monk said to him: 'O my son, today you have become better than me. You have reached a stage which I see, and you will surely be put to trial. If you are put to trial, do not disclose me.'

The boy used to heal the blind and the leper, and treat people for all other diseases. A companion of the king, who had gone blind, heard of him and came to him with many gifts, saying: 'All that is here shall be yours if you cure me.' The boy said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah alone Who cures. If you believe in Allah, I shall pray to Allah and He will cure you.' So he believed in Allah, and Allah cured him. He then went to the king and sat with him as he used to do before. The king said to him: 'Who has restored your sight?' He said: 'My Lord.' The king said: 'Do you have a lord other than me?' He said: 'My Lord and your Lord is Allah.' So the king seized him and continued torturing him until he disclosed the boy.

The boy was brought, and the king said to him: 'O my son, your magic has reached such a level that you cure the blind and the leper and do such and such.' The boy said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah alone Who cures.' So the king seized him and continued torturing him until he disclosed the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him: 'Turn back from your religion.' He refused, so the king called for a saw and placed it in the middle of his head, and split him in two so that both halves fell apart.

Then the king's companion was brought, and it was said to him: 'Turn back from your religion.' He refused, so the saw was placed in the middle of his head, and he was split so that both halves fell apart.

Then the boy was brought, and it was said to him: 'Turn back from your religion.' He refused, so the king handed him over to a group of his men and said: 'Take him to such and such a mountain. Climb the mountain with him, and when you reach its summit, if he turns back from his religion, well and good; otherwise, throw him down.' They took him and climbed the mountain with him. He said: 'O Allah, save me from them by whatever means You wish.' The mountain then shook, and they all fell down, while he came walking back to the king.

The king said to him: 'What happened to your companions?' He said: 'Allah saved me from them.' So the king handed him over to another group of his men and said: 'Take him and carry him in a boat, and take him out to the middle of the sea. If he turns back from his religion, well and good; otherwise, throw him overboard.' They took him, and he said: 'O Allah, save me from them by whatever means You wish.' The boat capsized with them, and they drowned, while he came walking back to the king.

The king said to him: 'What happened to your companions?' He said: 'Allah saved me from them.' Then he said to the king: 'You will not be able to kill me until you do what I command you.' The king said: 'What is that?' He said: 'Gather the people in one open place, and crucify me on a trunk of a tree. Then take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the middle of the bow, and say: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy. Then shoot me. If you do that, you will kill me.'

So the king gathered the people in one open place and crucified him on a trunk of a tree. Then he took an arrow from his quiver and placed it in the middle of the bow, and said: 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.' He then shot him, and the arrow struck him in the temple. The boy placed his hand over the wound in his temple and died.

The people then said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy!'

News was brought to the king, and it was said to him: 'Do you see what you feared? By Allah, what you feared has come upon you—the people have believed!' So he ordered trenches to be dug at the entrances of the roads, and they were dug, and fires were lit in them. He said: 'Whoever does not turn back from his religion, throw him into it,' or it was said, 'cast him into it.' They did this until a woman came with her child. She hesitated to throw herself into the fire, and the child said to her: 'O my mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth.'"
tirmidhi||992:
Ahmad bin Mani' narrated to us, Hushaim narrated to us, Khalid, Mansur, and Hisham informed us - as for Khalid and Hisham, they said: from Muhammad and Hafsah, and Mansur said: from Muhammad, from Umm 'Atiyyah who said: "One of the daughters of the Prophet (ﷺ) died, and he said: 'Wash her an odd number of times, three, or five, or more than that if you see fit, and wash her with water and sidr (lote-tree leaves), and put camphor, or something of camphor, in the last (washing), and when you have finished, inform me.' So when we finished, we informed him, and he threw us his waist-wrapper and said: 'Shroud her in it (as the innermost garment next to her body).'"

Hushaim said: "And in the narration of others - not these narrators - and I do not know, perhaps Hisham was among them - she said: 'And we plaited her hair into three braids.'" Hushaim said: "I think he said: 'And we laid it behind her.'"

Hushaim said: "Khalid, from among the group, narrated to us from Hafsah and Muhammad, from Umm 'Atiyyah, who said: 'And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: "Begin with her right side and the places of wudu."'"

There is also a narration on this topic from Umm Sulaim.

Abu 'Eisa said: The hadith of Umm 'Atiyyah is a hasan sahih hadith. This is what is acted upon according to the people of knowledge. It has been narrated from Ibrahim An-Nakha'i that he said: "The washing of the deceased is like the washing for major ritual impurity (janabah)." Malik bin Anas said: "There is no fixed limit for washing the deceased according to us, and there is no known specific description for it, rather it is (simply) that he be purified." Ash-Shafi'i said: "Malik only said a general statement: 'He is washed and cleaned.' If the deceased is cleaned with plain water or other water, that suffices for his washing, but it is more beloved to me that he be washed three times or more, not less than three, because of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Wash her three times or five.' And if they are cleaned in less than three times, that suffices, and it is not held that the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ) means anything other than achieving cleanliness with three or five, and he did not specify a fixed limit." The jurists have said likewise, and they are more knowledgeable about the meanings of the hadith. Ahmad and Ishaq said: "The washings should be with water and sidr, and in the last one there should be something of camphor."
muslim||7386: Abd al-Warith bin Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith and Hajjaj bin al-Sha'ir narrated to us, from Abd al-Samad - and the wording is that of Abd al-Warith bin Abd al-Samad - my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from al-Husayn bin Dhakwan, Ibn Buraydah narrated to us, Amir bin Sharahil al-Sha'bi of Sha'b Hamdan narrated to me, that he asked Fatimah bint Qays, the sister of al-Dahhak bin Qays, who was one of the earliest migrant women, and said: Tell me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) yourself, without attributing it to anyone else. She said: If you wish, I will indeed do so. He said: Yes, tell me. She said: I was married to Ibn al-Mughirah, who was one of the best young men of Quraysh at that time, and he was killed in the early days of jihad with the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him). When I became a widow, Abd al-Rahman bin Awf proposed to me along with a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), and the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) proposed to me on behalf of his freed slave Usamah bin Zayd. I had been told that the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) had said: "Whoever loves me, let him love Usamah." When the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) spoke to me, I said: My affair is in your hand; marry me to whomever you wish. He said: "Move to the house of Umm Sharik." Umm Sharik was a wealthy woman from among the Ansar who spent generously in the way of Allah, and guests would stay with her. I said: I will do so. He said: "Do not do that. Umm Sharik is a woman who has many guests, and I dislike that your veil might fall off, or your garment might be uncovered from your legs, and the people would see something of you that you dislike. Rather, move to the house of your cousin Abdullah bin Amr ibn Umm Maktum" - he was a man from Banu Fihr, the Fihr of Quraysh, from the same tribe as she was. So I moved to his house. When my waiting period ended, I heard the caller, the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him), calling out: "Prayer, assemble!" So I went out to the mosque and prayed with the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him). I was in the row of women that was directly behind the men. When the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) finished his prayer, he sat on the pulpit, smiling, and said: "Let every person remain in his place of prayer." Then he said: "Do you know why I have gathered you?" They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: "By Allah, I have not gathered you out of desire or fear, but I have gathered you because Tamim al-Dari, who was a Christian man, came and gave his pledge and became a Muslim, and he told me a story that matched what I used to tell you about the Messiah, the Dajjal (Antichrist). He told me that he had sailed on a sea vessel with thirty men from Lakhm and Judham, and the waves tossed them about for a month at sea. Then they put in at an island in the sea, arriving there around sunset, and they sat in the small boats of the ship, then went onto the island. There, a beast with abundant hair met them - so hairy that they could not tell its front from its back due to the amount of hair. They said: Woe to you, what are you? It said: I am al-Jassasah (the Spy). They said: What is al-Jassasah? It said: O people, go to this man in the monastery, for he is longing for news of you. He said: When she named a man to us, we were afraid that she might be a devil. He said: So we set off quickly until we entered the monastery, and there we found the largest man we had ever seen in form, and the most tightly bound - his hands were joined to his neck, and between his knees and his ankles were iron shackles. We said: Woe to you, what are you? He said: You have now managed to find out about me, so tell me, who are you? They said: We are people from the Arabs; we sailed on a sea vessel, and we encountered the sea when it was turbulent, and the waves tossed us about for a month. Then we put in at this island of yours, and we sat in its small boats, then entered the island, and a beast with abundant hair met us - so hairy that its front could not be distinguished from its back due to the amount of hair. We said: Woe to you, what are you? It said: I am al-Jassasah. We said: What is al-Jassasah? It said: Go to this man in the monastery, for he is longing for news of you. So we came to you quickly, and we were frightened by it, and we were not certain that it was not a devil. He said: Tell me about the date-palms of Baysan. We said: About what aspect of them do you inquire? He said: I ask you whether its palms bear fruit. We said to him: Yes. He said: Indeed, it is about to stop bearing fruit. He said: Tell me about the lake of Tiberias. We said: About what aspect of it do you inquire? He said: Does it have water? They said: It has abundant water. He said: Indeed, its water is about to disappear. He said: Tell me about the spring of Zughar. They said: About what aspect of it do you inquire? He said: Is there water in the spring, and do its people cultivate crops with the water of the spring? We said to him: Yes, it has abundant water and its people cultivate crops from its water. He said: Tell me about the Prophet of the unlettered ones (nabi al-ummiyyin) - what has he done? They said: He has come out from Makkah and settled in Yathrib. He said: Did the Arabs fight him? We said: Yes. He said: How did he deal with them? So we told him that he had prevailed over those Arabs near him and they had obeyed him. He said to them: Has that indeed happened? We said: Yes. He said: Indeed, that is better for them, that they obey him. And I inform you about myself: I am the Messiah, and I am about to be given permission to come forth. I will come forth and travel through the land, and I will not leave any town without descending upon it within forty nights, except Makkah and Taybah (Madinah), for both of these are forbidden to me - whenever I intend to enter either one of them, an angel with a drawn sword in his hand confronts me and turns me away from it, and over every mountain pass of it there are angels guarding it." She said: The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him) said, striking the pulpit with his staff: "This is Taybah, this is Taybah, this is Taybah" - meaning Madinah - "Have I not told you this before?" The people said: Yes. "Indeed, the story of Tamim pleased me, for it matched what I used to tell you about him and about Madinah and Makkah. Indeed, he is in the sea of Syria, or the sea of Yemen - no, rather he is from the direction of the east, he is from the direction of the east, he is from the direction of the east" - and he gestured with his hand towards the east. She said: I memorized this from the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him).
tirmidhi||1183:
Hannad narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ash-Sha'bi who said: "Fatimah bint Qais said: 'My husband divorced me with three (divorces) during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no lodging for you and no maintenance."'" Mughirah said: "So I mentioned it to Ibrahim, and he said: 'Umar said: "We will not abandon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of our Prophet (ﷺ) for the statement of a woman - we do not know whether she remembered or forgot." And Umar used to grant her lodging and maintenance.

Ahmad bin Mani' narrated to us, Hushaim narrated to us, Husain, Isma'il and Mujalid informed us - Hushaim said - and Dawud also narrated to us, from Ash-Sha'bi who said: "I went to Fatimah bint Qais and asked her about the ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning her. She said: 'Her husband divorced her irrevocably, so she disputed with him about the lodging and maintenance, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not grant her lodging or maintenance.'" And in the Hadith of Dawud, she said: "And he commanded me to spend my waiting period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktum."

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. And it is the view of some of the people of knowledge, among them Al-Hasan Al-Basri, 'Ata' bin Abi Rabah, and Ash-Sha'bi. Ahmad and Ishaq also hold this view. They say: "There is no lodging or maintenance for the divorced woman if her husband does not have the right to take her back." And some of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them 'Umar and 'Abdullah, said: "The woman who is divorced with three (divorces) has lodging and maintenance." This is the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri and the people of Al-Kufah. And some of the people of knowledge said: "She has lodging but no maintenance." This is the view of Malik bin Anas, Al-Laith bin Sa'd, and Ash-Shafi'i. Ash-Shafi'i said: "We only granted her lodging on the basis of the Book of Allah. Allah Most High said: 'Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they (themselves) leave, unless they commit an open lewdness.'" They said this refers to abusive speech - that she is abusive to her husband's family. And he argued that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not grant Fatimah bint Qais lodging because she used to be abusive to her husband's family. Ash-Shafi'i said: "And she has no maintenance, based on the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the story of Fatimah bint Qais."
tirmidhi||1438:
Narrated Sahl bin Abi Hathmah -Yahya said: "And I think also from Rafi' bin Khadij"- that both of them said: "Abdullah bin Sahl bin Zaid and Muhayyisah bin Mas'ud bin Zaid went out until, when they were at Khaibar, they separated for some purpose there. Then Muhayyisah found Abdullah bin Sahl killed, having been murdered, so he buried him. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Huwayyisah bin Mas'ud and Abdur-Rahman bin Sahl, who was the youngest of the group. Abdur-Rahman went to speak before his two companions, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Let the eldest speak first.' So he kept silent, and his two companions spoke, then he spoke along with them. They mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the killing of Abdullah bin Sahl, and he said to them: 'Will you take fifty oaths and thereby have the right to your companion' - meaning his killer? They said: 'How can we swear when we did not witness it?' He said: 'Then the Jews will clear themselves with fifty oaths.' They said: 'How can we accept the oaths of a disbelieving people?' When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that, he paid the blood-money himself."

[Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Khallal narrated to us], Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, Yahya bin Sa'eed informed us, from Bushair bin Yasar, from Sahl bin Abi Hathmah and Rafi' bin Khadij, a similar report with the same meaning.

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. The people of knowledge act upon this Hadith regarding Al-Qasamah. Some of the jurists of Al-Madinah were of the view that retaliation (Al-Qawad) may be based on Al-Qasamah. Some of the people of knowledge among the people of Al-Kufah and others said that Al-Qasamah does not necessitate retaliation, but it only necessitates the blood-money.

This is the end of the Chapters on Blood Money (Diyat), and praise is due to Allah.
tirmidhi||1361:
Ali bin Khashram narrated to us, Isa bin Yunus informed us, from Sa'eed bin Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from An-Nadr bin Anas, from Bashir bin Nahik, from Abu Hurairah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever frees a share - or he said a portion - of a slave, then his emancipation is to be paid for from his wealth if he has wealth. But if he does not have wealth, then he is to be valued a fair valuation, then he is made to work off (the remaining value) for the portion of the one who did not free (his share), without being overburdened.'"

[Abu Eisa] said: There is also a narration on this topic from 'Abdullah bin 'Amr.

Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya bin Sa'eed narrated to us, from Sa'eed bin Abi Arubah, similarly, and he said: "Shaqisan" (a portion).

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. And likewise, Aban bin Yazid narrated it from Qatadah, similar to the narration of Sa'eed bin Abi Arubah. Shu'bah also narrated this Hadith from Qatadah, but he did not mention in it the matter of working off (the debt).

The people of knowledge differed regarding the working off (the debt). Some of the people of knowledge held the view of allowing the working off (the debt) in this case, and this is the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri and the people of Kufah, and Ishaq holds this view as well.

Some of the people of knowledge said: If a slave is owned jointly by two men, and one of them frees his share, then if he has wealth, he is liable for the share of his partner, and the slave is freed by means of his wealth. But if he does not have wealth, then only what has been freed of the slave is freed, and he is not made to work off (the remainder). They said this based on what has been reported from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ). This is the view of the people of Madinah, and Malik bin Anas, Ash-Shafi'i, and Ahmad hold this view.
tirmidhi||248:
Bundar Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us: Yahya bin Sa'eed and Abdur-Rahman bin Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah bin Kuhail, from Hujr bin 'Anbas, from Wa'il bin Hujr, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite: '(Not of) those who earned Your anger, nor of those who went astray' and he said: 'Ameen,' and he prolonged his voice with it."

He said: There are also narrations on this topic from 'Ali and Abu Hurairah.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Wa'il bin Hujr is a Hasan Hadith. This is what more than one of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), the Followers, and those after them say - they hold that a man raises his voice with the Ta'min and does not conceal it. This is the view of Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.

Shu'bah narrated this Hadith from Salamah bin Kuhail, from Hujr Abu Al-'Anbas, from 'Alqamah bin Wa'il, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "(Not of) those who earned Your anger, nor of those who went astray," and he said: "Ameen," lowering his voice with it.

Abu 'Eisa said: I heard Muhammad (Al-Bukhari) say: The Hadith of Sufyan is more correct than the Hadith of Shu'bah regarding this, and Shu'bah erred in several places in this Hadith. He said "from Hujr Abu Al-'Anbas" when it is actually Hujr bin 'Anbas, whose surname is Abu As-Sakan. And he added in it "from 'Alqamah bin Wa'il," when there is no mention of 'Alqamah in it; rather it is from Hujr bin 'Anbas, from Wa'il bin Hujr. And he said "lowering his voice with it," when it is actually "prolonging his voice with it."

Abu 'Eisa said: I asked Abu Zur'ah about this Hadith, and he said: The Hadith of Sufyan regarding this is more correct than the Hadith of Shu'bah.

He said: Al-'Ala' bin Salih Al-Asadi narrated from Salamah bin Kuhail something similar to the narration of Sufyan.
tirmidhi||1104:
Narrated Aisha: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whatever woman is married without the permission of her guardian, her marriage is void, her marriage is void, her marriage is void. If he has consummated the marriage with her, then she is entitled to a bridal-money for what he enjoyed of her private parts. And if they dispute, then the ruler is the guardian of the one who has no guardian."

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan. Yahya bin Sa'eed Al-Ansari, Yahya bin Ayyub, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, and more than one of the memorizers have narrated something similar to this from Ibn Juraij.

Abu Eisa said: The Hadith of Abu Musa is a Hadith about which there is disagreement. Israel, Shareek bin Abdullah, Abu Awanah, Zuhair bin Mu'awiyah, and Qais bin Ar-Rabi' narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Asbat bin Muhammad and Zaid bin Al-Hubab narrated it from Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Abu Ubaidah Al-Haddad narrated it from Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ) similarly, but he did not mention "from Abu Ishaq" in it. And it has also been narrated from Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Shu'bah and Ath-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no marriage except with a guardian." Some of the companions of Sufyan have mentioned, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa - but this is not correct. The narration of those who narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no marriage except with a guardian" is, in my view, more correct, because their hearing from Abu Ishaq was at different times. And even though Shu'bah and Ath-Thawri are more precise and reliable memorizers than all of those who narrated this Hadith from Abu Ishaq, the narration of these others is, in my view, more likely to be correct, because Shu'bah and Ath-Thawri heard this Hadith from Abu Ishaq in a single sitting. Among what indicates this is what Mahmoud bin Ghailan narrated to us, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah informed us, he said: "I heard Sufyan Ath-Thawri asking Abu Ishaq: 'Did you hear Abu Burdah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no marriage except with a guardian"?' He said: 'Yes.'" This indicates that the hearing of this Hadith by Shu'bah and Ath-Thawri was at one time. And Israel is trustworthy and reliable regarding Abu Ishaq. I heard Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna saying: I heard Abdur-Rahman bin Mahdi saying: "Whatever I missed of the Hadith of Ath-Thawri from Abu Ishaq, I only missed it because I relied on Israel, for he used to bring it more complete."

And the Hadith of Aisha on this topic from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no marriage except with a guardian" is, in my view, a Hasan Hadith. It was narrated by Ibn Juraij, from Sulaiman bin Musa, from Az-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And it was narrated by Al-Hajjaj bin Artah and Ja'far bin Rabi'ah, from Az-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And it was narrated from Hisham bin Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ) similarly. Some of the people of Hadith have criticized the Hadith of Az-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Juraij said: "Then I met Az-Zuhri and asked him about it, and he denied it." So they weakened this Hadith because of this. And it was mentioned from Yahya bin Ma'in that he said: "No one mentioned this wording from Ibn Juraij except Isma'il bin Ibrahim." Yahya bin Ma'in said: "And the hearing of Isma'il bin Ibrahim from Ibn Juraij is not up to that standard; he only verified his books against the books of Abdul-Majid bin Abdul-Aziz bin Abi Rawwad, what he heard from Ibn Juraij." And Yahya weakened the narration of Isma'il bin Ibrahim from Ibn Juraij.

And the practice regarding this topic, according to the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), is based on the Hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no marriage except with a guardian." Among them are Umar bin Al-Khattab, Ali bin Abi Talib, Abdullah bin Abbas, Abu Hurairah, and others. And it has been narrated similarly from some of the jurists among the Followers, that they said: "There is no marriage except with a guardian." Among them are Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Shuraih, Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, Umar bin Abdul-Aziz, and others. And this is the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Al-Awza'i, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, Malik, Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.
tirmidhi||274:
Narrated 'Abdullah bin Al-Aqram Al-Khuza'i: "I was with my father at Al-Qa' of Namirah, and a group of riders passed by, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing performing prayer." He said: "I was looking at the whiteness of his armpits when he prostrated, meaning their whiteness."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are other narrations on this topic from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Buhainah, Jabir, Ahmar bin Jaz', Maimunah, Abu Humaid, Abu Mas'ud, Abu Usaid, Sahl bin Sa'd, Muhammad bin Maslamah, Al-Bara' bin 'Azib, 'Adi bin 'Amirah, and 'Aishah.

Abu 'Eisa said: This Ahmar bin Jaz' is a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he has only one narration.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of 'Abdullah bin Aqram is a Hasan Hadith, we do not know it except from the Hadith of Dawud bin Qais, and we do not know of 'Abdullah bin Aqram Al-Khuza'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), other than this Hadith. This is acted upon according to most of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ).

He said: 'Abdullah bin Aqram Al-Khuza'i only has this Hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ). And 'Abdullah bin Arqam Az-Zuhri is a Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he was the scribe of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq.
tirmidhi||1465:
Narrated Mu'awiyah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever drinks wine, then flog him; if he repeats it a fourth time, then kill him."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are also narrations on this topic from Abu Hurairah, Ash-Sharid, Shurahbil bin Aws, Jarir, Abu Ar-Ramad Al-Balawi, and 'Abdullah bin 'Amr.

Abu 'Eisa said: This is how Ath-Thawri also narrated the Hadith of Mu'awiyah, from 'Asim, from Abu Salih, from Mu'awiyah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Juraij and Ma'mar narrated it from Suhail bin Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

He said: I heard Muhammad [Al-Bukhari] saying: "The Hadith of Abu Salih from Mu'awiyah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), is more authentic in this matter than the Hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ)."

This ruling was only at the beginning of Islam, and it was later abrogated. This is how Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated from Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, from Jabir bin 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever drinks wine, then flog him; if he repeats it a fourth time, then kill him." He said: Then, after that, a man who had drunk wine for the fourth time was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he flogged him but did not kill him. Similarly, Az-Zuhri narrated something similar to this from Qabisah bin Dhu'aib, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

He said: So the killing was lifted, and it had been a concession (that was later withdrawn). This is what is acted upon according to the general body of the people of knowledge; we do not know of any difference of opinion among them regarding this, in the past or present. What further supports this is what has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) through many routes, that he said: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah is not lawful to shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, the married adulterer, and one who abandons his religion."
tirmidhi||304:
Muhammad bin Bashshar and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated to us, they said: Yahya bin Sa'eed Al-Qattan narrated to us, Abdul-Hamid bin Ja'far narrated to us, Muhammad bin Amr bin Ata narrated to us, from Abu Humaid As-Sa'idi who said: "I heard him, while he was among ten of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), one of them being Abu Qatadah bin Rib'i, saying: 'I am the most knowledgeable of you regarding the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' They said: 'You were not the earliest of us in companionship with him, nor the most frequent in coming to him.' He said: 'Yes, I was.' They said: 'Then demonstrate it.' So he said: 'When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood for prayer, he stood up straight and raised his hands until they were level with his shoulders. When he wanted to bow (perform Ruku'), he raised his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then said: "Allahu Akbar," and he bowed. Then he straightened up, not lowering his head nor raising it excessively, and placed his hands on his knees. Then he said: "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah (Allah hears whoever praises Him)," and he raised his hands and stood straight until every bone returned to its place in a straight posture. Then he leaned down to the ground in prostration, and said: "Allahu Akbar." Then he kept his upper arms away from his sides, and spread out his toes. Then he folded his left leg and sat upon it, then straightened up until every bone returned to its place in a straight posture. Then he leaned down in prostration, and said: "Allahu Akbar." Then he folded his leg and sat, and straightened up until every bone returned to its place. Then he rose, and he did the same in the second Rak'ah. When he stood up from the two prostrations, he said "Allahu Akbar" and raised his hands until they were level with his shoulders, just as he had done when he began the prayer. Then he continued to do likewise until, in the Rak'ah in which his prayer was to conclude, he brought his left foot forward and sat on his side in a posture of Tawarruk (sitting with the left side on the ground), then he said the Taslim (concluding salutation).'"

Abu Isa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.

He said: The meaning of his statement "and he raised his hands when he stood up from the two prostrations" means when he stood up from the two Rak'ahs.
tirmidhi||411:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: "The poor came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Indeed the wealthy pray as we pray, and they fast as we fast, and they have wealth with which they free slaves and give charity.' He said: 'So when you pray, say: Allahu Akbar thirty-four times, and Alhamdulillah thirty-three times, and Subhan Allah thirty-three times, and La ilaha illallah ten times. For indeed by it you will catch up to those who preceded you, and none who come after you will catch up to you.'"

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are other narrations on this topic from Ka'b bin 'Ujrah, Anas, 'Abdullah bin 'Amr, Zaid bin Thabit, Abu Ad-Darda, Ibn 'Umar, and Abu Dharr.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] The Hadith of Ibn 'Abbas is a Hasan Gharib Hadith.

There is also something on this topic from Abu Hurairah and Al-Mughirah. And it has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There are two habits which no Muslim man maintains but that he enters Paradise: He glorifies Allah after every prayer ten times, and praises Him ten times, and magnifies Him ten times, and he glorifies Allah when he goes to sleep thirty-three times, and praises Him thirty-three times, and magnifies Him thirty-four times."
tirmidhi||460:
Hannad narrated to us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Harith, from Ali, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to perform Witr with three (Rak'ah), reciting in them nine Surahs from the Mufassal, reciting three Surahs in every Rak'ah, the last of them being (Qul huwa Allahu Ahad)."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are other narrations on this topic from 'Imran bin Husain, 'Aishah, Ibn 'Abbas, and Abu Ayyub. And 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abza narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b, and it is also narrated from 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abza from the Prophet (ﷺ). This is how some of them narrated it, not mentioning in it "from Ubayy," while some of them mentioned it from 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abza from Ubayy.

Abu 'Eisa said: A group of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and others held this view, and they were of the opinion that a man should perform Witr with three (Rak'ah).

Sufyan said: "If you wish, you may perform Witr with five, and if you wish, you may perform Witr with three, and if you wish, you may perform Witr with one Rak'ah." Sufyan said: "What I prefer is to perform Witr with three Rak'ah." And this is the view of Ibn Al-Mubarak and the people of Kufah.

Sa'eed bin Ya'qub At-Talaqani narrated to us, Hammad bin Zaid narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad bin Sireen, who said: "They used to perform Witr with five, and with three, and with one Rak'ah, and they considered all of that good."
tirmidhi||2183:
Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas narrated: I fell ill during the year of the Conquest with an illness that brought me close to death. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to visit me, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a great deal of wealth and no one will inherit from me except my daughter. Shall I bequeath all of my wealth?" He said: "No." I said: "Then two-thirds of my wealth?" He said: "No." I said: "Then half?" He said: "No." I said: "Then a third?" He said: "A third, and a third is a lot. It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor, begging from people. Whatever you spend seeking thereby [the reward of Allah], you will be rewarded for it, even the morsel of food that you lift to your wife's mouth." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will I be left behind after my emigration [i.e., die in Mecca]?" He said: "You will not be left behind after me to do a deed by which you seek the Face of Allah, but that you will increase thereby in rank and standing. Perhaps you will be left long enough that some people will benefit through you and others will be harmed through you. O Allah, complete for my companions their emigration, and do not turn them back on their heels. But the wretched one is Sa'd bin Khawlah" - the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lamented for him because he died in Mecca.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There is also a narration on this topic from Ibn 'Abbas. This is a Hasan Sahih Hadith. This hadith has been narrated through more than one route from Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas. The people of knowledge act upon this, that a man may not bequeath more than a third [of his wealth]. Some of the people of knowledge held it desirable to give less than a third, due to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "And a third is a lot."
tirmidhi||2174:
Sa'id bin 'Abdur-Rahman Al-Makhzumi and more than one other narrator narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Az-Zuhri. (Another chain:) And 'Ali bin Hujr narrated to us, [saying]: Hushaim informed us, from Az-Zuhri, from 'Ali bin Husain, from 'Amr bin 'Uthman, from Usamah bin Zaid, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim." Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, [saying]: Sufyan narrated to us, [saying]: Az-Zuhri narrated to us similarly.

Abu 'Eisa said: There is something on this topic from Jabir and 'Abdullah bin 'Amr. This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. It has been narrated in this manner by Ma'mar and more than one other narrator, from Az-Zuhri, similar to this. Malik narrated from Az-Zuhri, from 'Ali bin Husain, from 'Umar bin 'Uthman, from Usamah bin Zaid, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly. The Hadith of Malik is a mistake; Malik erred in it. Some of them narrated it from Malik saying "from 'Amr bin 'Uthman," and most of the companions of Malik said "from Malik, from 'Umar bin 'Uthman." 'Amr bin 'Uthman bin 'Affan is well known among the children of 'Uthman, while 'Umar bin 'Uthman is not known. The practice is upon this Hadith according to the people of knowledge. Some of the people of knowledge differed regarding the inheritance of the apostate; most of the people of knowledge among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and others granted the wealth to his Muslim heirs. Others said that his Muslim heirs do not inherit from him, and they used as evidence the Hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever." This is the view of Ash-Shafi'i.
tirmidhi||312:
Al-Ansari narrated to us, Ma'n narrated to us, Malik bin Anas narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn Ukaimah Al-Laithi, from Abu Hurairah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished a prayer in which he had recited aloud, and said: 'Did any of you recite along with me just now?' A man said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I said (to myself): Why am I being contested in the Qur'an?'" He said: "So the people refrained from reciting along with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the prayers in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited aloud, once they heard that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are also narrations on this topic from Ibn Mas'ud, 'Imran bin Husain, and Jabir bin 'Abdullah.

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan. Ibn Ukaimah Al-Laithi's name is 'Umarah, and it is also said that it is 'Amr bin Ukaimah. Some of the companions of Az-Zuhri narrated this Hadith and mentioned this wording: Az-Zuhri said: "So the people refrained from reciting when they heard that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

There is nothing in this Hadith that contradicts the view of those who hold that one should recite behind the Imam, because it is Abu Hurairah himself who narrated this Hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Hurairah also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever performs a prayer in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qur'an (Al-Fatihah), it is deficient, it is deficient, incomplete." So the one who conveyed this Hadith said to him: "Sometimes I am behind the Imam." He (Abu Hurairah) said: "Recite it to yourself."

Abu 'Uthman An-Nahdi narrated from Abu Hurairah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded me to announce that there is no prayer without reciting the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah)."

The majority of the people of Hadith have chosen the view that a man should not recite when the Imam recites aloud, and they said: he should follow the pauses of the Imam.

The people of knowledge have differed concerning recitation behind the Imam. The majority of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), the Successors, and those after them held the view of reciting behind the Imam, and this is the view of Malik bin Anas, 'Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. It has been narrated from 'Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak that he said: "I recite behind the Imam, and the people recite, except for a group among the Kufans, and I hold that whoever does not recite, his prayer is still valid."

Some of the people of knowledge were strict concerning the abandonment of the recitation of the Opening of the Book, even if one is behind the Imam, and they said: "No prayer is valid without the recitation of the Opening of the Book, whether one is alone or behind the Imam." They relied upon what 'Ubadah bin As-Samit narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ). 'Ubadah bin As-Samit, after the Prophet (ﷺ), used to recite behind the Imam, and he interpreted the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no prayer without the recitation of the Opening of the Book" accordingly. This is the view held by Ash-Shafi'i, Ishaq, and others besides them.

As for Ahmad bin Hanbal, he said that the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book" applies when one is praying alone. He argued using the Hadith of Jabir bin 'Abdullah, wherein he said: "Whoever performs a Rak'ah in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qur'an has not prayed, unless he is behind the Imam." Ahmad bin Hanbal said: "This is a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who interpreted the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book' to mean when one is praying alone." Despite this, Ahmad still preferred reciting behind the Imam, and that a man should not abandon the Opening of the Book even if he is behind the Imam.
tirmidhi||392:
Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Abdul A'la and Abu Dawud narrated to us, they said: Hisham narrated to us, from Yahya bin Abi Kathir, from Muhammad bin Ibrahim, that Abu Hurairah and As-Sa'ib Al-Qari used to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness before the Taslim.

Abu Isa said: The Hadith of Ibn Buhainah is a Hasan Sahih Hadith. This is acted upon according to some of the people of knowledge, and it is the view of Ash-Shafi'i, who holds that all prostrations of forgetfulness are before the Salam. He says that this abrogates the other Hadiths, and he mentions that the last action of the Prophet (ﷺ) was according to this.

Ahmad and Ishaq said: When a man stands up after two Rak'ah (mistakenly, before completing the prayer), he should perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness before the Salam, based on the Hadith of Ibn Buhainah.

Abdullah Ibn Buhainah is Abdullah bin Malik; he is the son of Buhainah - Malik is his father and Buhainah is his mother. This is how Ishaq bin Mansur informed me, from Ali bin Abdullah Al-Madini.

Abu Isa said: The people of knowledge differed regarding the two prostrations of forgetfulness, as to when a man should perform them - before the Salam or after it. Some of them held the view that they should be performed after the Salam, and this is the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri and the people of Kufah. Others held that they should be performed before the Salam, and this is the view of most of the jurists among the people of Madinah, such as Yahya bin Sa'eed, Rabi'ah, and others, and it is what Ash-Shafi'i says.

Others said: If it is due to an addition in the prayer, then it is after the Salam, and if it is due to a deficiency, then it is before the Salam. This is the view of Malik bin Anas.

Ahmad said: What has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the two prostrations of forgetfulness should each be applied according to its context. He holds that if one stands up after two Rak'ah, then according to the Hadith of Ibn Buhainah, he should perform them before the Salam. And if he prays Zuhr with five Rak'ah, then he should perform them after the Salam. And if he says the Salam after two Rak'ah of Zuhr or Asr, then he should perform them after the Salam. Each is to be applied according to its context. And every case of forgetfulness for which there is no report from the Prophet (ﷺ) - then the two prostrations of forgetfulness are to be performed before the Salam.

Ishaq said something similar to the view of Ahmad in all of this, except that he said: every case of forgetfulness for which there is no report from the Prophet (ﷺ) - if it is due to an addition in the prayer, he performs them after the Salam, and if it is due to a deficiency, he performs them before the Salam.
tirmidhi||2259:
Narrated Abu Sa'eed Al-Khudri: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in the Asr prayer one day while it was still daytime, then he stood up to deliver a sermon, and he did not leave anything that would happen up until the establishment of the Hour without informing us of it. Whoever memorized it, memorized it, and whoever forgot it, forgot it. Among the things he said was: 'Indeed this world is sweet and green (attractive), and Allah is going to place you as successors in it, then He will see how you act. So beware of this world and beware of women.' And among what he said was: 'Indeed, let not the awe of people prevent any man from speaking the truth when he knows it.'" He (the narrator) said: "Abu Sa'eed wept and said: 'By Allah, we have seen things and felt awed.'" And among what he said was: "Indeed a banner will be raised for every treacherous person on the Day of Judgement according to the extent of his treachery, and there is no treachery greater than that of a leader of the common people, whose banner will be planted at his rear." And among what we memorized that day was: "Indeed the children of Adam were created in various different levels: among them is one who is born a believer, lives as a believer, and dies a believer; among them is one who is born a disbeliever, lives as a disbeliever, and dies a disbeliever; among them is one who is born a believer, lives as a believer, and dies a disbeliever; and among them is one who is born a disbeliever, lives as a disbeliever, and dies a believer. Indeed, among them is one who is slow to anger and quick to calm down, and among them is one who is quick to anger and quick to calm down - so that balances out that. Indeed, among them is one who is quick to anger and slow to calm down. Indeed, the best of them is the one who is slow to anger and quick to calm down, and indeed the worst of them is the one who is quick to anger and slow to calm down. Indeed, among them is one who repays well and asks well (of his due), and among them is one who repays badly but asks well, and among them is one who repays well but asks badly - so that balances out that. Indeed, among them is one who repays badly and asks badly. Indeed, the best of them is the one who repays well and asks well, and indeed the worst of them is the one who repays badly and asks badly. Indeed, anger is like a burning coal in the heart of the son of Adam. Have you not seen the redness of his eyes and the swelling of his veins? So whoever feels something of that, let him cling to the ground." He (the narrator) said: "We began looking towards the sun to see how much of it remained." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, what has passed of this world compared to what remains of it is just like what has passed of this day of yours compared to what remains of it."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are narrations on this topic from Hudhaifah, Abu Maryam, Abu Zaid bin Akhtab, and Al-Mughirah bin Shu'bah, and it is mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) informed them of what would happen up until the establishment of the Hour. This Hadith is Hasan.
tirmidhi||2530:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Madduyah At-Tirmidhi narrated to us, Al-Qasim bin Al-Hakam Al-'Urani narrated to us, 'Ubaidullah bin Al-Walid Al-Wassafi narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'eed, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered his place of prayer and saw some people who appeared to be laughing excessively. He said: 'Indeed, if you were to remember much the destroyer of pleasures, it would have kept you occupied from what I see. So remember much the destroyer of pleasures - death - for there does not come a day upon the grave except that it speaks, saying: "I am the house of estrangement, I am the house of solitude, I am the house of dust, I am the house of worms." So when the believing slave is buried, the grave says to him: "Welcome and greetings! Indeed, you were among the most beloved of those who walked upon my back to me. Now that you have been entrusted to me today and have come to me, you will see my treatment of you."' He said: 'Then it expands for him as far as his sight can reach, and a door is opened for him to Paradise.' 'But when the wicked or disbelieving slave is buried, the grave says to him: "No welcome and no greetings! Indeed, you were among the most hated of those who walked upon my back to me. Now that you have been entrusted to me today and have come to me, you will see my treatment of you."' He said: 'Then it closes in on him until it meets together upon him and his ribs are crushed.'" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) interlocked his fingers to demonstrate this, then he said: "And Allah will send seventy dragons for him, such that if one of them were to breathe upon the earth, nothing would grow on it for as long as the world remains. They will bite and claw at him until he is brought to the reckoning." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The grave is nothing but a garden among the gardens of Paradise, or a pit among the pits of the Fire."

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Gharib (rare); we do not know of it except from this route.
tirmidhi||2547:
Hannad narrated to us, Yunus bin Bukair narrated to us, 'Umar bin Dharr narrated to me, Mujahid narrated to us, from Abu Hurairah who said: "The people of As-Suffah were the guests of the people of Islam; they had no families or wealth to depend upon. By Allah besides Whom there is no other god, I would press my liver against the ground due to hunger, and I would tie a stone against my stomach due to hunger. One day I sat along the path which they used to take when they went out, and Abu Bakr passed by me, so I asked him about a verse from the Book of Allah - I only asked him so that he would take me along with him - but he passed by and did not do so. Then 'Umar passed by me, and I asked him about a verse from the Book of Allah - I only asked him so that he would take me along with him - but he passed by and did not do so. Then Abu Al-Qasim (ﷺ) passed by me, and he smiled when he saw me, and said: 'Abu Hurairah?' I said: 'At your service, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Follow me.' And he went on, so I followed him, and he entered his house. I asked permission to enter and he granted me permission. He found a bowl of milk and said: 'Where did this milk come from?' It was said: 'So-and-so gave it to us as a gift.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Abu Hurairah?' I said: 'At your service.' He said: 'Go to the people of As-Suffah and invite them.'" [Abu Hurairah said:] "They were the guests of the people of Islam; they had no families or wealth to depend upon. Whenever any charity came to him, he would send it to them and would not take anything from it himself, and whenever a gift came to him, he would send for them, and take some of it, and share it with them. This upset me, and I said: 'What good will this bowl do among the people of As-Suffah? I am the one being sent to call them, so he will order me to pass it around among them, and what benefit could I hope to get from it? I had hoped to get from it enough to satisfy me, but there was no avoiding obedience to Allah and His Messenger.' So I went to them and called them. When they entered upon him and took their seats, he said: 'Abu Hurairah, take the bowl and give it to them.' So I took the bowl and started giving it to each man, and he would drink until he was satisfied, then he would give it back to me, and I would give it to the next one, until I reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with it, and everyone had drunk their fill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the bowl and put it on his hand, then raised his head and smiled, and said: 'Abu Hurairah, drink.' So I drank, then he said: 'Drink.' I kept on drinking, and he kept on saying: 'Drink,' until I said: 'By the One Who sent you with the truth, I cannot find any more room for it.' So he took the bowl and praised Allah, mentioned His Name, then drank."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.
tirmidhi||2748:
Muslim bin Hatim Al-Ansari Al-Basri narrated to us, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari narrated to us, from his father, from Ali bin Zaid, from Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: Anas bin Malik said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'O my son, if you are able to spend your morning and evening with no deceit in your heart towards anyone, then do so.' Then he said to me: 'O my son, that is part of my Sunnah, and whoever revives my Sunnah has loved me, and whoever loves me will be with me in Paradise.'" And there is a lengthy story connected with this Hadith.

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Ghareeb from this route. Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari is trustworthy, his father is trustworthy, and Ali bin Zaid is truthful, except that he sometimes reports as connected (marfu') something that others report as stopped (mawquf) [at the level of the companion].

He said: And I heard Muhammad bin Bashshar saying: Abu Al-Walid said: Shu'bah said: "Ali bin Zaid narrated to us, and he used to raise reports (i.e., report them as marfu')." And we do not know of any narration from Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab from Anas except this lengthy Hadith. Abbad bin Maisarah Al-Minqari has also narrated this Hadith from Ali bin Zaid from Anas, without mentioning Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab in it.

Abu Eisa said: I discussed it with Muhammad bin Ismail, and he did not know of it, and this Hadith - nor any other - is known to have been narrated by Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab from Anas. Anas bin Malik died in the year ninety-three, and Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab died two years after him, in the year ninety-five.
tirmidhi||2451:
Suwaid bin Nasr narrated to us, [saying]: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak informed us, [saying]: Haiwah bin Shuraih informed us, [saying]: Al-Walid bin Abu Al-Walid Abu Uthman Al-Madani informed me, that Uqbah bin Muslim narrated to him, that Shufayy Al-Asbahi narrated to him, that he entered Al-Madinah, and there he found a man around whom the people had gathered. He said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Hurairah." So I drew near to him until I sat down in front of him while he was narrating to the people. When he fell silent and was alone, I said to him: "I ask you by the right due, and by the right due, that you narrate to me a Hadith which you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which you understood well and knew well." Abu Hurairah said: "I will do so. I shall narrate to you a Hadith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me, which I understood well and knew well." Then Abu Hurairah sobbed once, and remained still for a while, then he recovered and said: "I shall narrate to you a Hadith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me in this house, with none present besides me and him." Then Abu Hurairah sobbed once more, then he recovered and wiped his face, and said: "I shall narrate to you a Hadith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me, while I and he were in this house, with none present besides me and him." Then Abu Hurairah sobbed once more, then he recovered and wiped his face, and said: "I will do so. I shall narrate to you a Hadith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me, while I was with him in this house, with none present with him besides me and him." Then Abu Hurairah sobbed severely, then he leaned over falling upon his face, and I supported him against myself for a long while, then he recovered and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me that Allah, Blessed and Most High, when it is the Day of Judgement, will descend to His servants to judge between them, while every nation is kneeling. The first to be called will be a man who had memorized the Qur'an, a man who was killed fighting in the cause of Allah, and a man of abundant wealth. So Allah will say to the reciter: 'Did I not teach you what I revealed to My Messenger?' He will say: 'Yes indeed, O Lord.' He will say: 'What did you do with what you were taught?' He will say: 'I used to recite it standing throughout the hours of the night and the hours of the day.' Allah will say to him: 'You have lied,' and the angels will say to him: 'You have lied,' and Allah will say to him: 'Rather, you wanted it to be said that so-and-so is a reciter, and that has indeed been said.' Then the man of wealth will be brought, and Allah will say to him: 'Did I not make you affluent, such that I left you in no need of anyone?' He will say: 'Yes indeed, O Lord.' He will say: 'What did you do with what I gave you?' He will say: 'I used to maintain ties of kinship and give in charity.'
