Allah will say to him: 'You have lied,' and the angels will say to him: 'You have lied,' and Allah, Most High, will say: 'Rather, you wanted it to be said that so-and-so is generous, and that has indeed been said.' Then the one who was killed fighting in the cause of Allah will be brought, and Allah will say to him: 'For what were you killed?' He will say: 'I was commanded to fight in Your cause, so I fought until I was killed.' Allah, Most High, will say to him: 'You have lied,' and the angels will say to him: 'You have lied,' and Allah will say: 'Rather, you wanted it to be said that so-and-so is brave, and that has indeed been said.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck my knee and said: "O Abu Hurairah, those three are the first of Allah's creation for whom the Fire shall be kindled on the Day of Judgement."

Al-Walid Abu Uthman said: "Uqbah bin Muslim informed me that it was Shufayy who entered upon Mu'awiyah and informed him of this."

Abu Uthman said: "Al-'Ala bin Abu Hakim narrated to me that he had been a swordsman for Mu'awiyah, and a man entered upon him and informed him of this from Abu Hurairah. Mu'awiyah said: 'This has been done to these people, so what about the rest of the people?' Then Mu'awiyah wept severely, until we thought that he was going to perish, and we said: 'This man has brought us something evil.' Then Mu'awiyah recovered and wiped his face and said: 'Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth: "Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We shall repay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein is rendered worthless, and vain is what they used to do."'"

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Gharib.
tirmidhi||2619:
Muhammad bin Isma'il narrated to us, Hisham bin 'Ammar narrated to us, 'Abdul-Hamid bin Habib bin Abi Al-'Ishrin narrated to us, Al-Awza'i narrated to us, Hassan bin 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab, that he met Abu Hurairah, and Abu Hurairah said: "I ask Allah to bring us together in the marketplace of Paradise." Sa'eed said: "Is there a marketplace in it?" He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed me that the people of Paradise, when they enter it, will settle therein according to the merit of their deeds. Then permission will be granted for a period equal to the day of Jumu'ah among the days of this world, during which they will visit their Lord, and He will display His Throne to them, and He will manifest Himself to them in one of the gardens of Paradise. Pulpits of light will be placed for them, and pulpits of pearl, and pulpits of ruby, and pulpits of chrysolite, and pulpits of gold, and pulpits of silver. And the lowest of them - and none among them is truly lowly - will sit upon hills of musk and camphor, and they will not think that those upon the chairs have a better sitting place than they do." Abu Hurairah said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord?' He said: 'Yes. Do you dispute about seeing the sun and the moon on the night when it is full?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'Just so, you will not dispute about seeing your Lord. And no man will remain in that gathering except that Allah will address him directly, until He says to one of them: "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, do you remember the day when you said such and such?" reminding him of some of his acts of treachery in the world. He will say: "O my Lord, did You not forgive me?" He will say: "Yes indeed, and it is by the vastness of My forgiveness that you have attained this rank of yours." While they are in this state, a cloud will come over them from above and will rain down upon them a fragrance the like of whose scent they have never encountered before. And our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, will say: "Rise up to that which I have prepared for you of honor, and take whatever you desire."' He said: 'So we will go to a marketplace surrounded by the angels, containing what no eyes have seen the like of, nor have ears heard, nor have hearts imagined. Whatever we desire will be brought to us, without any buying or selling therein. And in that marketplace the people of Paradise will meet one another.' He said: 'A man of elevated rank will come forward and meet one who is beneath him - though none among them is truly lowly - and he will be struck with awe at what he sees him wearing. But before he finishes his conversation, he will find himself imagining something even more beautiful than it, for it is not fitting that anyone should feel any sorrow therein. Then we will return to our dwellings, and our spouses will come to meet us, saying: "Welcome, and greetings! You have come, and you possess more beauty than when you parted from us." And we will say: "We sat today with our Lord, the Compeller, and it is only right that we should return as we have returned."'"

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Ghareeb (rare/unfamiliar); we do not know it except through this route. Suwaid bin 'Amr has narrated something of this Hadith from Al-Awza'i.
tirmidhi||2708:
Narrated Qutaibah: Al-Laith narrated to us, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban, from Ibn Muhairiz, from As-Sunabihi, from 'Ubadah bin As-Samit:

That he said: "I entered upon him while he was dying, and I wept. So he said: 'Wait, why are you weeping? By Allah, if I am called upon to testify, I shall surely testify for you, and if intercession is permitted for me, I shall surely intercede for you, and if I am able, I shall surely benefit you.' Then he said: 'By Allah, there is no Hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which contains good for you, but that I have narrated it to you, except for one Hadith, which I shall narrate to you today, since I am now surrounded [by death]. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, Allah will forbid the Fire for him."'"

[He said:] There are also narrations on this topic from Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, Jabir, Ibn 'Umar, and Zaid bin Khalid.

He said: "I heard Ibn Abi 'Umar saying: 'I heard Ibn 'Uyainah saying: Muhammad bin 'Ajlan was trustworthy and reliable in Hadith.'"

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih Gharib from this route, and As-Sunabihi is 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Usailah, Abu 'Abdullah.

It has been reported from Az-Zuhri that he was asked about the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah' will enter Paradise." He said: "This was only [the case] at the beginning of Islam, before the revelation of the obligatory duties and the commands and prohibitions."

Abu 'Eisa said: The explanation of this Hadith, according to some of the people of knowledge, is that the people of monotheism will enter Paradise, and even if they are punished in the Fire for their sins, they will not remain in the Fire forever.

It has been reported from 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Abu Dharr, 'Imran bin Husain, Jabir bin 'Abdullah, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Sa'eed Al-Khudri, and Anas bin Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "A people from among the people of monotheism will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise." This is how it has been reported from Sa'eed bin Jubair, Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, and others among the Successors.

It has also been reported through more than one route from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the explanation of this verse: "Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims" (15:2) - they said: "When the people of monotheism are brought out of the Fire and admitted to Paradise, those who disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims."
tirmidhi||2627:
Narrated Abu Hurairah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will gather the people on the Day of Judgment in one plain, then the Lord of the worlds will look at them and say: 'Should not every person follow what he used to worship?' So the one who worshipped the cross will be presented with his cross, the one who worshipped images will be presented with his images, and the one who worshipped fire will be presented with his fire. So they will follow what they used to worship, and the Muslims will remain. Then the Lord of the worlds will look at them and say: 'Will you not follow the people?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You, we seek refuge in Allah from You. Allah is our Lord, this is our place until we see our Lord.' And He commands them and steadies them. Then He disappears, then He looks at them and says: 'Will you not follow the people?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You, we seek refuge in Allah from You. Allah is our Lord, and this is our place until we see our Lord.' And He commands them and steadies them." They said: "And shall we see Him, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night when it is full?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "So you will have no difficulty in seeing Him at that time. Then He disappears, then He looks at them and makes Himself known to them, then He says: 'I am your Lord, so follow Me.' So the Muslims stand, and the Sirat is placed, and they cross over it like fine, swift horses and riding camels, and their saying upon it is: 'Save, save (us).' And the people of the Fire remain, and a group of them is thrown into it, then it is said: 'Are you full?' And it says: 'Are there more?' Then a group is thrown into it, and it is said: 'Are you full?' And it says: 'Are there more?' Until, when they have been put into it completely, the Most Merciful places His foot upon it, and its parts draw together, then He says: 'Enough, enough.' It says: 'Enough, enough.' Then when Allah admits the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, death is brought, bound by its forelock, and it is placed upon the wall that is between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise!' So they look out, fearful. Then it is said: 'O people of the Fire!' So they look out, delighted, hoping for intercession. Then it is said to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire: 'Do you recognize this?' So they say - both of them - 'Yes, we recognize it. It is death, the one which was assigned to us.' So it is laid down and slaughtered upon the wall that is between Paradise and the Fire. Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death! And O people of the Fire, eternity with no death!'"

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.

There have been narrated many reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) like this one, in which the matter of the Vision is mentioned, that the people will see their Lord, and the mention of the Foot, and other similar matters. The view held on this matter by the people of knowledge among the Imams, such as Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Malik bin Anas, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ibn 'Uyainah, Waki' and others, is that they narrated these things, then they said: "These Hadiths are to be narrated and we believe in them, and it is not to be said 'How?'" This is what the people of Hadith have chosen: that these things are to be narrated as they have come, and belief is to be held in them, and they are not to be interpreted, nor imagined, nor is it to be said "How?" This is the matter of the people of knowledge which they have chosen and adopted. The meaning of his saying in the Hadith: "Then He makes Himself known to them" means: He manifests Himself to them.
tirmidhi||2504:
Suwaid bin Nasr narrated to us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak narrated to us, Abu Hayyan At-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah bin Amr bin Jarir, from Abu Hurairah who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought some meat, and the forearm was raised up to him, and he ate it, for it was something he liked. He took a bite from it, then said: 'I am the leader of the people on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why that is? Allah will gather the first and the last people on one plain, so that the caller will be able to make them hear, and the eye will be able to encompass all of them, and the sun will draw close to them, and the people will experience such distress and hardship that they will not be able to bear or endure it. So the people will say to one another: "Do you not see what has befallen you? Do you not think to look for someone who might intercede for you with your Lord?" So the people will say to one another: "Go to Adam." So they will go to Adam and say: "You are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand, and breathed into you of His spirit, and commanded the angels, and they prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?" Adam will say to them: "Indeed, my Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. He forbade me from the tree, and I disobeyed. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Nuh."

So they will go to Nuh and say: "O Nuh, you are the first of the Messengers sent to the people of the earth, and Allah has named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?" Nuh will say to them: "Indeed, my Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. I had one supplication which I used against my people. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Ibrahim."

So they will go to Ibrahim and say: "O Ibrahim, you are the Prophet of Allah and His close friend among the people of the earth. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in?" He will say: "Indeed, my Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. I told three lies" - and Abu Hayyan mentioned them in the Hadith - "Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Musa."

So they will go to Musa and say: "O Musa, you are the Messenger of Allah, Allah favored you with His message and with His speech over mankind. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in?" He will say: "Indeed, my Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again. I killed a soul that I was not ordered to kill. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Isa."

So they will go to Isa and say: "O Isa, you are the Messenger of Allah, and His word which He cast to Maryam, and a spirit from Him, and you spoke to the people while in the cradle. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in?" Isa will say: "Indeed, my Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and will never be angry with the like of it again" - and he did not mention any sin - "Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me, go to Muhammad."

He said: So they will come to Muhammad and say: "O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, and you have been forgiven for your past and future sins. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in?" So I will go and come beneath the Throne, and fall down in prostration to my Lord. Then Allah will open to me such praises and glorification of Him as He has not opened to anyone before me. Then it will be said: "O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and it shall be given to you, intercede and your intercession will be accepted." So I will raise my head and say: "O my Lord, my nation! O my Lord, my nation! O my Lord, my nation!" Then He will say: "O Muhammad, admit those of your nation who have no reckoning against them through the right gate among the gates of Paradise, and they will share the other gates along with the rest of the people." Then he said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the distance between the two door-panels of the gates of Paradise is like the distance between Makkah and Hajar, or like the distance between Makkah and Busra."

There are narrations on this topic from Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, Anas, Uqbah bin Amir, and Abu Sa'eed.

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. Abu Hayyan At-Taymi's name is Yahya bin Sa'eed bin Hayyan, a Kufan, and he is trustworthy (Thiqah). Abu Zur'ah bin Amr bin Jarir's name is Harim.
tirmidhi||523:
Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Suhail bin Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever among you prays after Jumu'ah, let him pray four (units).'"

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.

Al-Hasan bin Ali narrated to us, Ali bin Al-Madini narrated to us, from Sufyan bin 'Uyainah, who said: "We used to consider Suhail bin Abi Salih to be reliable (thabt) in Hadith."

This is acted upon by some of the people of knowledge.

It has been narrated from Abdullah bin Mas'ud that he used to pray four (units) before Jumu'ah and four after it.

It has also been narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ordered praying two units after Jumu'ah, then four.

Sufyan Ath-Thawri and Ibn Al-Mubarak held the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

Ishaq said: "If one prays in the masjid on Friday, he should pray four; and if he prays in his house, he should pray two." He argued that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray two units after Jumu'ah in his house, and (also cited) the Hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever among you prays after Jumu'ah, let him pray four."

Abu 'Eisa said: It is Ibn Umar who narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to pray two units after Jumu'ah in his house. And Ibn Umar, after the Prophet (ﷺ), used to pray two units in the masjid after Jumu'ah, and after the two units he would pray four.

Ibn Abi Umar narrated that to us, Sufyan bin 'Uyainah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', who said: "I saw Ibn Umar pray two units after Jumu'ah, then after that he prayed four."

Sa'eed bin Abdur-Rahman Al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Sufyan bin 'Uyainah narrated to us, from Amr bin Dinar, who said: "I have not seen anyone more precise in Hadith than Az-Zuhri, and I have not seen anyone for whom dinars and dirhams were more insignificant than for him; dinars and dirhams were, to him, like camel dung."

Abu 'Eisa said: I heard Ibn Abi Umar say: I heard Sufyan bin 'Uyainah say: "Amr bin Dinar was older than Az-Zuhri."
tirmidhi||3071:
Abdullah bin Abdur-Rahman narrated to us, Ubaidullah bin Musa informed us, from Isra'il, from As-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Al-Bara' regarding: "and do not aim at that which is worthless from it to spend" - he said: "It was revealed concerning us, the group of the Ansar. We were owners of date-palms, and a man would bring from his palms according to how much or how little he had. A man would bring a cluster or two clusters and hang it in the Masjid, and the people of As-Suffah had no food, so when one of them became hungry he would come to the cluster and strike it with his stick, and some unripe and ripe dates would fall down, and he would eat. There were some people among those who did not care for good who would bring a cluster containing shriveled, worthless dates and shriveled dried-up dates, and a cluster that had been broken, and hang it up. So Allah, Most High, sent down: 'O you who believe! Spend of the good things which you have earned, and of that which We have produced from the earth for you, and do not aim at that which is worthless from it to spend, when you would not take it yourselves unless you closed your eyes to it.' They said: 'If one of you were given something like what he gave as a gift, he would not take it except with reluctance and shame.'" He said: "So after that, one of us would bring the best of what he had."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Gharib Sahih. Abu Malik is Al-Ghifari, and it is said that his name was Ghazwan. Sufyan has narrated something of this from As-Suddi.
tirmidhi||2991:
Mahmud bin Ghailan narrated to us, he said: Bishr bin As-Sari narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Alqamah bin Marthad, from Abu Abdur-Rahman As-Sulami, from Uthman bin Affan, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best among you - or the most virtuous among you - is he who learns the Qur'an and teaches it.'"

This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. And likewise it was reported by Abdur-Rahman bin Mahdi and more than one other from Sufyan Ath-Thawri, from Alqamah bin Marthad, from Abu Abdur-Rahman, from Uthman, from the Prophet (ﷺ); and Sufyan does not mention "from Sa'd bin Ubaidah" in it.

Yahya bin Sa'eed Al-Qattan reported this Hadith from Sufyan and Shu'bah, from Alqamah bin Marthad, from Sa'd bin Ubaidah, from Abu Abdur-Rahman, from Uthman, from the Prophet (ﷺ). Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated that to us, he said: Yahya bin Sa'eed narrated to us from Sufyan and Shu'bah. Muhammad bin Bashshar said: "This is how Yahya bin Sa'eed mentioned it, from Sufyan and Shu'bah, on more than one occasion, from Alqamah bin Marthad, from Sa'd bin Ubaidah, from Abu Abdur-Rahman, from Uthman, from the Prophet (ﷺ)." Muhammad bin Bashshar said: "But the companions of Sufyan do not mention in it, from Sufyan, from Sa'd bin Ubaidah." Muhammad bin Bashshar said: "And that is more correct."

Abu Eisa said: Shu'bah added "Sa'd bin Ubaidah" in the chain of this Hadith, and it seems that the Hadith of Sufyan is more resembling (of the correct chain).

Ali bin Abdullah said: Yahya bin Sa'eed said: "No one is equal to Shu'bah in my view, but when Sufyan differs with him, I take the view of Sufyan."

Abu Eisa said: I heard Abu Ammar mention from Waki', who said: Shu'bah said: "Sufyan has better memory than me, and Sufyan never narrated to me anything from anyone but that when I asked about it, I found it just as he had narrated it to me."

And in this regard, there are narrations from Ali and Sa'd.
tirmidhi||3165:
Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Umar bin Yunus Al-Yamami narrated to us, Ikrimah bin Ammar narrated to us, Abu Zumail narrated to us, Abdullah bin Abbas narrated to us, Umar bin Al-Khattab narrated to us, he said: "The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the idolators, and they were one thousand, while his companions were three hundred and some odd men. So the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) faced the Qiblah, then he stretched forth his hands, and began beseeching his Lord: 'O Allah! Fulfill for me what You have promised me! O Allah! Grant me what You have promised me! O Allah! If You destroy this group from the people of Islam, You shall not be worshipped upon the earth.' He did not cease beseeching his Lord, hands outstretched, facing the Qiblah, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. So Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak, and put it back on his shoulders. Then he embraced him from behind and said: 'O Prophet of Allah! Your pleading with your Lord is enough for you, for indeed He shall fulfill for you what He has promised you.' So Allah revealed: 'When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will help you with a thousand angels, following one after another."' So Allah aided them with the angels."

[Abu Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih Gharib. We do not know of it from the narration of Umar except from the narration of Ikrimah bin Ammar, from Abu Zumail. Abu Zumail's name is Simak Al-Hanafi. And this was on the Day of Badr.
tirmidhi||3170:
Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya bin Sa'eed, Muhammad bin Ja'far, Ibn Abu Adi, and Sahl bin Yusuf narrated to us, they said: Awf bin Abu Jamilah narrated to us, Yazid Al-Farisi narrated to us, Ibn Abbas narrated to us, he said: "I said to Uthman bin Affan: 'What made you place Al-Anfal, which is one of Al-Mathani, next to Bara'ah, which is one of Al-Mi'in, joining them together without writing the line 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim' between them, and placing them among As-Sab' At-Tiwal (the seven long Surahs)? What made you do that?' Uthman said: 'There were times that came upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when Surahs with a number of verses would be revealed to him, and when something was revealed to him, he would call for one of those who used to write, and say: "Place these verses in the Surah in which such and such is mentioned." And when a verse was revealed to him, he would say: "Place this verse in the Surah in which such and such is mentioned." Al-Anfal was one of the first (Surahs) that was revealed in Al-Madinah, and Bara'ah was one of the last parts of the Qur'an (to be revealed), and its story resembled its story, so I thought that it was part of it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away and he did not make it clear to us that it was part of it. For this reason I joined them together and did not write the line "Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim" between them, and I placed it among As-Sab' At-Tiwal.'"

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan, we do not know it except from the Hadith of Awf, from Yazid Al-Farisi, from Ibn Abbas. Yazid Al-Farisi has narrated more than one Hadith from Ibn Abbas, and it is said that he is Yazid bin Hurmuz. Yazid Ar-Raqashi is Yazid bin Aban Ar-Raqashi, and he did not meet Ibn Abbas; he only narrated from Anas bin Malik. Both of them were from the Tabi'in, from the people of Al-Basrah, and Yazid Al-Farisi is older (in narration) than Yazid Ar-Raqashi.
tirmidhi||3232:
Narrated Abu Sa'eed: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the leader of the children of Adam on the Day of Judgment, and this is no boast. In my hand will be the banner of praise, and this is no boast. There is no Prophet that Day - Adam or anyone else - but he will be under my banner. And I am the first for whom the earth will split open, and this is no boast." He said: "The people will be seized with terror three times, and they will come to Adam and say: 'You are our father Adam, so intercede for us with your Lord.' He will say: 'I committed a sin for which I was brought down to earth, but go to Nuh.' So they will go to Nuh, and he will say: 'I called down a curse upon the people of the earth and they were destroyed, but go to Ibrahim.' So they will go to Ibrahim, and he will say: 'I told three lies.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Not one of them was but he used it to defend the religion of Allah, but go to Musa." So they will go to Musa, and he will say: 'I killed a person, but go to Isa.' So they will go to Isa, and he will say: 'I was worshipped besides Allah, but go to Muhammad.'" He said: "So they will come to me, and I will go along with them."

Ibn Jud'an said: Anas said: "It is as if I can see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "I will take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise and knock it, and it will be said: 'Who is this?' It will be said: 'Muhammad.' So they will open for me and welcome me, saying: 'Welcome.' Then I will fall down in prostration, and Allah will inspire me with praise and glorification. Then it will be said to me: 'Raise your head. Ask and you shall be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted, and speak and you will be heard.' And that is Al-Maqam Al-Mahmud (the praiseworthy station) which Allah mentioned when He said: {It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.}"

Sufyan said: "Nothing was narrated from Anas except this statement: 'I will take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise and knock it.'"

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan. Some of them narrated this Hadith from Abu Nadrah, from Ibn Abbas, in its lengthy form.
tirmidhi||3257:
Yahya bin Musa, Abd bin Humaid, and more than one other narrator - the meaning being the same - narrated to us, they said: Abdur-Razzaq narrated to us, from Yunus bin Sulaim, from Az-Zuhri, from Urwah bin Az-Zubair, from Abdur-Rahman bin Abd Al-Qari who said: "I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: 'When revelation would descend upon the Prophet (ﷺ), a sound like the buzzing of bees would be heard near his face. One day revelation was sent down upon him, and we waited a while, then it was lifted from him, whereupon he faced the Qiblah, raised his hands, and said: "O Allah, increase us and do not decrease us, honor us and do not humiliate us, give to us and do not deprive us, favor us and do not favor others over us, and make us pleased and be pleased with us." Then he (ﷺ) said: "Ten Verses have been revealed to me; whoever upholds them will enter Paradise." Then he recited: "Certainly will the believers succeed" (Qad Aflaha Al-Mu'minun) until he completed ten Verses.'"

Muhammad bin Aban narrated to us, he said: Abdur-Razzaq narrated to us, from Yunus bin Sulaim, from Yunus bin Yazid, from Az-Zuhri, with this chain, similarly, with the same meaning.

Abu Isa said: This is more correct than the first Hadith. I heard Ishaq bin Mansur saying: "Ahmad bin Hanbal, Ali bin Al-Madini, and Ishaq bin Ibrahim narrated this Hadith from Abdur-Razzaq, from Yunus bin Sulaim, from Yunus bin Yazid, from Az-Zuhri."

Abu Isa said: Those who heard from Abdur-Razzaq early on mention in it "from Yunus bin Yazid," while some of them do not mention in it "from Yunus bin Yazid." Whoever mentions Yunus bin Yazid in it, that is more correct. Abdur-Razzaq would sometimes mention Yunus bin Yazid in this Hadith and sometimes not mention him, and if Yunus is not mentioned in it, then it is Mursal (with a broken chain).
tirmidhi||3306:
Abu Kuraib, Abd bin Humaid, and more than one other narrator narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah informed us, from Al-Hasan bin Al-Hakam An-Nakha'i, Abu Sabrah An-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Farwah bin Musaik Al-Muradi who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I not fight those of my people who turned away, along with those who came forward?' So he permitted me to fight them and put me in charge (as commander). When I left his presence, he asked about me: 'What did Al-Ghutaifi do?' He was informed that I had already set out. He said: 'So he sent someone after me and had me brought back.' I came to him while he was among a group of his companions, and he said: 'Call the people, and whoever among them accepts Islam, accept it from him, and whoever does not accept Islam, do not be hasty until I send you further instructions.'"

He said: "And what was revealed concerning Saba' was revealed." So a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Saba' - is it a land or a woman?" He said: "It is neither a land nor a woman, but it is a man who fathered ten (sons) among the Arabs. Six of them went to the right (south/Yemen) and four of them went to the left (north/Sham). As for those who went to the left, they are Lakhm, Judham, Ghassan, and 'Amilah. As for those who went to the right, they are Al-Azd, Al-Ash'ariyyun, Himyar, Madh-hij, Anmar, and Kindah."

Then a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Anmar?" He said: "Those from among them are Khath'am and Bajilah."

This has also been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Gharib.
tirmidhi||3308:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with a group of his companions, a star was shot with light, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What did you used to say about something like this during Jahiliyyah when you saw it?' They said: 'We used to say that a great person had died or a great person had been born.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'It is not shot for the death of anyone, nor for anyone's life, but when our Lord, Mighty and Sublime, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the inhabitants of the heaven who are next to them glorify Him, then those who are next to them, until the glorification reaches the inhabitants of this heaven. Then the inhabitants of the sixth heaven ask the inhabitants of the seventh heaven: What did your Lord say? So they inform them. Then the inhabitants of each heaven seek information from each other, until the information reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. Then the devils snatch the hearing, and they are shot at, and they cast it down to their allies. Whatever they bring in its true form is correct, but they distort it and add to it.'"

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.

This Hadith has been reported from Az-Zuhri, from 'Ali bin Al-Husain, from Ibn 'Abbas, from some men among the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ)..."

Al-Awza'i reported it from Az-Zuhri, from 'Ubaidullah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from some men among the Ansar, who said: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ)..." and he mentioned something similar in meaning. Al-Husain bin Huraith narrated that to us, he said: "Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, he said: 'Al-Awza'i narrated to us.'"
tirmidhi||3302:
Narrated Anas bin Malik (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got married, and he went in to his wife. He said: My mother, Umm Sulaim, prepared Hais (a dish made of dates, clarified butter and dried yogurt) and put it in a bowl, and said: 'O Anas! Take this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and tell him: My mother sends this to you, she sends her greetings of peace to you and says: This is a small gift from us, O Messenger of Allah.'"

He said: "So I took it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'My mother sends her greetings of peace to you and says: This is a small gift from us to you.' He said: 'Put it down.' Then he said: 'Go and call for me so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and whoever you meet' - and he named some men." He said: "So I called those whom he named and whoever I met." He (the narrator) said: "I asked Anas how many they numbered, and he said about three hundred."

He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'O Anas! Bring the bowl.'" He said: "So they entered until the Suffah and the room were full. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let them form circles of ten, and let each man eat from what is in front of him.'" He said: "So they ate until they were full." He said: "Then one group would leave and another group would come in, until they had all eaten." He said: "Then he said to me: 'O Anas! Lift it up.'" He said: "So I lifted it up, and I do not know whether there was more when I put it down or when I lifted it up."

He said: "Some groups of them sat talking in the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting and his wife had her face turned to the wall. They became a burden to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and gave greetings of peace to his wives, then returned. When they saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had returned, they thought they had become burdensome to him." He said: "So they hurried to the door and all of them left. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and let down the curtain and entered, while I was sitting in the room. He did not stay but a little while before he came out to me, and these Ayat were revealed. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out and recited them to the people: 'O you who believe! Enter not the Prophet's houses, except when leave is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its proper time...' to the end of the Ayah."

Al-Ja'd said: "Anas said: 'I am the most recent of the people in terms of learning of these Ayat, and the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were veiled (secluded).'"

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. Al-Ja'd is Ibn 'Uthman, and it is said that he is Ibn Dinar, and he is called Abu 'Uthman, a Basri, and he is trustworthy according to the people of Hadith. Yunus bin 'Ubaid, Shu'bah, and Hammad bin Zaid narrated from him.
tirmidhi||3404:
Abd bin Humaid narrated to us, Abdur-Rahman bin Sa'd narrated to us, from Amr bin Abu Qais, from Simak bin Harb, from Abdullah bin Amirah, from Al-Ahnaf bin Qais, from Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib who said: He claimed that he was sitting in Al-Batha in a group, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting among them, when a cloud passed over them and they looked at it. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what this is called?" They said: "Yes, this is As-Sahab (the cloud)." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And Al-Muzn." They said: "And Al-Muzn." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And Al-'Anan." They said: "And Al-'Anan." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Do you know how far the distance is between the heaven and the earth?" They said: "No, by Allah, we do not know." He said: "Indeed the distance between them is either seventy-one, or seventy-two, or seventy-three years, and the heaven above that is the same," until he counted seven heavens like that. Then he said: "Above the seventh heaven there is a sea, between whose top and bottom is like the distance between one heaven and another, and above that there are eight mountain goats (Awal), between their hooves and their knees is like the distance between one heaven and another, then above their backs is the Throne, between its bottom and its top is like the distance between one heaven and another, and Allah is above that."

Abd bin Humaid said: I heard Yahya bin Ma'in saying: "Would that Abdur-Rahman bin Sa'd not perform Hajj until we hear this Hadith from him."

Abu Isa said: This Hadith is Hasan Gharib. Al-Walid bin Abu Thawr narrated something similar to it from Simak, and he raised it (as a Marfu' report). Sharik narrated part of this Hadith from Simak but he stopped it (as a Mawquf report) and did not raise it (to the Prophet ﷺ). Abdur-Rahman is Ibn Abdullah bin Sa'd Ar-Razi.
tirmidhi||3452:
Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Safwan bin Isa narrated to us, Al-Harith bin Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Dhubab narrated to us, from Sa'eed bin Abi Sa'eed Al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When Allah created Adam and breathed the soul into him, he sneezed, and said: "Al-hamdulillah (praise be to Allah)." So he praised Allah by His permission. His Lord said to him: "May Allah have mercy upon you, O Adam! Go to those angels - to a gathering of them who are sitting - and say: As-salamu alaikum (peace be upon you)." They said: "Wa alaikas-salamu wa rahmatullah (and upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah)." Then he returned to his Lord, and He said: "This is your greeting, and the greeting of your children among themselves." Then Allah said to him, while His two Hands were closed: "Choose whichever of them you wish." He said: "I choose the right hand of my Lord, and both of my Lord's Hands are right and blessed." Then He opened it, and there was Adam and his progeny within it. He said: "O my Lord! What are these?" He said: "These are your progeny." And every person had his lifespan written between his eyes. Among them was a man who was the brightest of them, or among the brightest of them. He said: "O Lord, who is this?" He said: "This is your son Dawud. I have written for him a lifespan of forty years." He said: "O Lord, increase his lifespan." He said: "That is what I have written for him." He said: "O Lord, then I have granted him sixty years from my own lifespan." He said: "You, and that is for you (to decide)."' He said: 'Then he was made to dwell in Paradise for as long as Allah willed, then he was sent down from it. So Adam kept count for himself.' He said: 'Then the Angel of Death came to him, and Adam said to him: "You have hastened - a thousand years have been written for me." He said: "Yes, but you granted sixty years of it to your son Dawud." So he denied it, and his progeny denied it; and he forgot, and his progeny forgot.' He said: 'So from that day, it was commanded that writing and witnesses be used.'"

Abu Isa said: This Hadith is Hasan Gharib from this route. And it has been narrated through other routes from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from the narration of Zaid bin Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).
tirmidhi||3397:
Abd bin Humaid narrated to us, Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from As-Suddi, from Abu Sa'eed Al-Azdi, Zaid bin Arqam narrated to us, he said: "We went out on a military expedition with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there were some people of the Bedouins with us. We used to race to reach the water, and the Bedouins used to reach it before us. One time a Bedouin outraced his companions, reaching there before them, and he filled the trough and placed stones around it and put a leather sheet over it until his companions came. He said: 'Then a man from the Ansar came to a Bedouin and loosened the rein of his she-camel so it could drink, but he refused to let him do so. So he pulled out the stopper of the water, and the Bedouin raised his stick and struck the Ansari on the head, wounding him. So he went to Abdullah bin Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, and told him, for he was one of his companions. Abdullah bin Ubayy became angry, then he said: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse" from around him - meaning the Bedouins, for they used to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the time of food. Abdullah said: "When they disperse from around Muhammad, then bring Muhammad food, so he and those with him may eat." Then he said to his companions: "If you return to Madinah, surely the more honorable will drive out from it the more despicable."'

Zaid said: "I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I heard Abdullah bin Ubayy, so I informed my uncle, who went and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for him, and he swore and denied it." He said: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and disbelieved me." He said: "Then my uncle came to me and said: 'You have done nothing but earn the hatred of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward you, and he has disbelieved you, and so have the Muslims.'" He said: "So I was overcome by worry the like of which no one else had ever been overcome by." He said: "So while I was traveling with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, having nodded off with my head from worry, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and pulled my ear and smiled in my face, and nothing could have pleased me more, not even if I had been granted eternal life in this world.

Then Abu Bakr caught up with me and said: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to you?' I said: 'He did not say anything, except that he pulled my ear and smiled in my face.' He said: 'Rejoice.' Then Umar caught up with me, and I said to him the same as I had said to Abu Bakr. Then when morning came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surat Al-Munafiqun."

[Abu Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.
tirmidhi||3319:
This hadith has been narrated at length from Mu'adh bin Jabal, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I dozed and fell into a heavy sleep, and I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said: 'About what are the highest assembly disputing?'"

Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Mu'adh bin Hani' Abu Hani' Al-Yashkuri narrated to us, Jahdam bin 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Yahya bin Abi Kathir, from Zaid bin Sallam, from Abu Sallam, from 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'A'ish Al-Hadrami, that he narrated to him from Malik bin Yukhamir As-Saksaki, from Mu'adh bin Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was held back from us one morning from the Fajr prayer, until we almost looked at the sun with our own eyes. Then he came out quickly, and the call was given for the prayer. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed and shortened his prayer. When he gave the salutation, he called out loudly, saying to us: 'Stay in your rows as you are.' Then he turned to face us and said: 'Indeed, I shall tell you what kept me from you this morning. I got up during the night and performed ablution and prayed as much as was decreed for me. Then I dozed during my prayer until I fell into a heavy sleep, and there I was with my Lord, Blessed and Exalted, in the most beautiful form. He said: "O Muhammad." I said: "Here I am, at Your service, my Lord." He said: "About what are the highest assembly disputing?" I said: "I do not know." He said this three times. He said: Then I saw Him place His palm between my shoulders, until I felt the coolness of His fingertips between my breasts. Then everything became clear to me and I came to know. He said: "O Muhammad." I said: "Here I am, at Your service, my Lord." He said: "About what are the highest assembly disputing?" I said: "About the expiations." He said: "What are they?" I said: "Walking on foot to the congregational prayers, sitting in the mosques after the prayers, and performing ablution thoroughly in times of dislike (i.e., difficulty)." He said: "Then what else?" I said: "Feeding the hungry, speaking gently, and praying at night while people are sleeping." He said: "Ask." I said: "O Allah, I ask You for the doing of good deeds, the abandonment of forbidden deeds, love of the poor, and that You forgive me and have mercy on me. And when You intend a trial for a people, then take me unto You without being tried. I ask You for Your love, and the love of those who love You, and the love of deeds that draw me closer to Your love."'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is true, so study it, then learn it."

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. I asked Muhammad bin Isma'il about this Hadith, and he said: "This Hadith is Hasan Sahih." And he said: "This is more authentic than the Hadith of Al-Walid bin Muslim, from 'Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir." He said: "Khalid bin Al-Lajlaj narrated to us, 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'A'ish Al-Hadrami narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)..." and he mentioned the Hadith. This is not preserved (i.e., not authentic in this form). This is how Al-Walid mentioned it in his Hadith from 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'A'ish, saying: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Bishr bin Bakr narrated this Hadith from 'Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir with this chain of narration, from 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'A'ish, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is more authentic. And 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'A'ish did not hear (directly) from the Prophet (ﷺ).
tirmidhi||3120:
Al-Hasan bin Ahmad bin Abu Shu'aib Abu Muslim Al-Harrani narrated to us: Muhammad bin Salamah Al-Harrani narrated to us: Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Asim bin 'Umar bin Qatadah, from his father, from his grandfather, Qatadah bin An-Nu'man, who said: "There was a household among us called the Banu Ubairiq: Bishr, Bashir, and Mubashshir. Bashir was a hypocrite who used to compose poetry with which he satirized the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then attribute it to some of the Arabs, saying: 'So-and-so said such-and-such, so-and-so said such-and-such.' When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry they would say: 'By Allah, none but this wicked man could have said this poetry' - or words to that effect - and they would say: 'The son of Ubairiq said it.'

He said: They were a household of need and poverty in both the pre-Islamic era (Jahiliyyah) and in Islam. The people's food in Madinah was only dates and barley, and when a man had some wealth, and a caravan came from Syria bringing fine white flour, a man would buy some of it and set it aside for himself, while the family's food remained dates and barley. A caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah bin Zaid bought a load of fine white flour and put it in an upper room of his, in which there was also weaponry - armor and a sword. Someone came upon it from beneath the house, broke into the upper room, and took the food and the weapons.

When morning came, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: 'O son of my brother, we have been robbed this night - our upper room was broken into and our food and weapons were taken.' He said: So we made inquiries in the neighborhood and asked around, and it was said to us: 'We saw the Banu Ubairiq lighting a fire this night, and we think it can only be over some of your food.'

He said: The Banu Ubairiq said - while we were asking around in the neighborhood - 'By Allah, we think none other than your companion Labid bin Sahl did it' - a man among us of righteousness and Islam. When Labid heard this, he drew his sword and said: 'I steal?! By Allah, this sword shall clash with you, or you shall clarify this theft!' They said: 'Leave it be, O man, for you are not the one responsible for it.' So we asked around in the neighborhood until we had no doubt that they [the Banu Ubairiq] were the culprits.

My uncle said to me: 'O son of my brother, why don't you go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention this to him?'"

Qatadah said: "So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'A household among us, people of harshness, deliberately went after my uncle Rifa'ah bin Zaid, broke into an upper room of his, and took his weapons and food. Let them return our weapons to us; as for the food, we have no need of it.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I shall look into that.'

When the Banu Ubairiq heard of this, they went to a man among them called Usair bin 'Urwah and spoke to him about it. So a group of people from the neighborhood gathered and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Qatadah bin An-Nu'man and his uncle have deliberately gone after a household among us, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without proof or certainty.'"

Qatadah said: "So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: 'You have deliberately gone after a household known for Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without certainty or proof.' So I went back, and I wished that I had given up some of my wealth rather than have spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this.

Then my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: 'O son of my brother, what have you done?' So I informed him of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: 'Allah is the One from whom help is sought.'

It was not long before the Qur'an was revealed: 'Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you, and do not be for the deceitful an advocate' [4:105] - referring to the Banu Ubairiq - 'And seek forgiveness of Allah' [4:106] - meaning for what you said to Qatadah - 'Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like anyone who is a habitually sinful deceiver. They conceal [their evil intentions and deeds] from the people, but they cannot conceal from Allah' [4:107-108] up to His saying '...Forgiving and Merciful' [4:110] - meaning: had they sought Allah's forgiveness, He would have forgiven them - 'And whoever commits a sin only earns it against himself' [4:111] up to His saying '...a manifest sin' [4:112] - referring to their statement about Labid - 'And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy...' [4:113] up to His saying '...We will bestow upon him a great reward' [4:114].

When the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he returned them to Rifa'ah."

Qatadah said: "When I brought the weapons to my uncle - and he was an old man who had grown weak, or [the narrator said] had grown old, during the pre-Islamic era, and I used to think there was some deficiency in his Islam - when I brought him the weapons he said: 'O son of my brother, it is for the sake of Allah,' and I then knew that his Islam had been sound.

When the Qur'an was revealed, Bashir joined the polytheists and stayed with Sulafah bint Sa'd bin Sumayyah. Allah then revealed: 'And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will leave him to what he has chosen and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination. Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly strayed into far error' [4:115-116].

When he stayed with Sulafah, Hassan bin Thabit attacked her with some verses of his poetry, so she took his belongings, placed them upon her head, went out, and threw them down in Al-Abtah, saying: 'You have brought me the poetry of Hassan as a gift - you have brought me nothing good!'"

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Gharib (unusual). We do not know of anyone who narrated it with this chain except Muhammad bin Salamah Al-Harrani. Yunus bin Bukair and others narrated this Hadith from Muhammad bin Ishaq, from 'Asim bin 'Umar bin Qatadah, as a Mursal report, without mentioning "from his father, from his grandfather" in it. Qatadah bin An-Nu'man was the maternal half-brother of Abu Sa'eed Al-Khudri, and Abu Sa'eed Al-Khudri's name was Sa'd bin Malik bin Sinan.
tirmidhi||3619:
Narrated Zirr bin Hubaish: I went to Safwan bin 'Assal Al-Muradi to ask him about wiping over the leather socks (Khuffs). He said: "What has brought you here O Zirr?" I said: "Seeking knowledge." So he said: "Indeed, the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, being pleased with what he seeks." I said: "Wiping over the Khuffs after passing stool and urine has been bothering my chest, and you were a companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), so I have come to ask you if you heard him mention anything about that." He said: "Yes, he used to order us, when we were on a journey or travelers, not to remove our Khuffs for three days and their nights, except due to major impurity (Janabah), but for stool, urine, and sleep (it was permitted)." So I said: "Did you hear him mention anything concerning passion?" He said: "Yes, we were with the Prophet (ﷺ) on a journey, and while we were with him, a Bedouin called out to him with a loud, booming voice: 'O Muhammad!' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) answered him in a similar tone: 'Here I am.' We said to him: 'Woe to you! Lower your voice, for you are in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) and you have been forbidden to do this.' He said: 'By Allah, I will not lower it.' The Bedouin said: 'A man loves a people but has not yet joined them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'A man will be with those whom he loves on the Day of Resurrection.'" He continued narrating to us until he mentioned a gate towards the west, the width of its passage - or a rider would travel across its width - in forty or seventy years. (Sufyan said: towards Ash-Sham) Allah created it on the day He created the heavens and the earth, open - meaning for repentance - and it will not be closed until the sun rises from it.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.
tirmidhi||3506:
Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Khallal narrated to us, Abu Al-Walid At-Tayalisi narrated to us, Abdul-Aziz bin Abi Salamah and Yusuf bin Al-Majishun narrated to us - Abdul-Aziz said: "My paternal uncle narrated to me," and Yusuf said: "My father informed me" - Al-A'raj narrated to me, from Ubaidullah bin Abi Rafi', from Ali bin Abi Talib, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood for prayer he would say: "I have turned my face towards the One Who created the heavens and the earth, as a monotheist (Hanifan) and I am not of the idolaters. Indeed my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my life and my death belong to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds, no partner has He. This is what I have been commanded and I am of the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King, there is no god but You. You are my Lord and I am Your slave. I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me all of my sins, for none forgives sins except You. Guide me to the best of characters, for none guides to the best of them except You, and turn away from me its evil, for none turns away its evil from me except You. Here I am at Your service, granted the good is all in Your Hands, and the evil is not attributed to You. I exist by You and unto You. Blessed and Exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness and I turn in repentance to You." Then when he bowed (in Ruku') he would say: "O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My hearing, my sight, my bones, and my sinews are humbled before You." Then when he raised (from Ruku') he would say: "O Allah our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth, and filling what is between them, and filling whatever else You will." Then when he prostrated (in Sujud) he would say: "O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to the One Who created it and formed it, and split open its hearing and sight. So blessed is Allah, the best of Creators." Then, among the last things he would say between the Tashahhud and the Taslim, he would say: "O Allah, forgive me what I have put forth and what I have left behind, what I have done in secret and what I have done openly, what I have committed in excess, and what You know better of than I. You are the One Who brings forward and You are the One Who puts back. There is no god but You."

[Abu Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.
tirmidhi||3503:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: "I heard the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) saying one night, when he had finished his prayer:

'O Allah, indeed I ask You for mercy from You, by which You guide my heart, and unite my affair, and put together my scattered state, and set right that which is absent from me, and raise that which is present with me, and purify my deeds, and inspire me with right guidance through it, and restore my unity through it, and protect me through it from every evil. O Allah, grant me faith and certainty after which there is no disbelief, and mercy by which I attain the honor of Your generosity in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, indeed I ask You for triumph in the gift - and it is also transmitted 'in the decree' - and the station of the martyrs, and the life of the fortunate, and victory over enemies. O Allah, I bring down to You my need, and even if my opinion falls short and my deed is weak, I am in need of Your mercy. So I ask You, O Decider of matters, O Healer of hearts, just as You give safe passage between the seas, that You grant me safe passage from the punishment of the blazing Fire, and from the call of destruction, and from the trial of the graves. O Allah, whatever my opinion falls short of, and whatever my intention does not reach, and whatever my request does not attain, of good which You have promised to anyone among Your creation, or good which You are going to give to anyone among Your servants, then indeed I desire it from You, and I ask You for it by Your mercy, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, O Possessor of the strong bond and the right command, I ask You for security on the Day of Threat, and Paradise on the Day of Eternity, along with those brought near, the witnesses, those who bow and prostrate, those who fulfill their covenants. Indeed You are Merciful, Loving, and You do what You will. O Allah, make us guides who are rightly guided, not astray nor leading others astray, at peace with Your friends and an enemy to Your enemies. We love, through Your love, whoever loves You, and we show enmity, through enmity to You, towards whoever opposes You. O Allah, this is the supplication, and upon You is the response; this is the effort, and upon You is the reliance. O Allah, place for me light in my grave, and light in my heart, and light before me, and light behind me, and light on my right, and light on my left, and light above me, and light below me, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight, and light in my hair, and light in my skin, and light in my flesh, and light in my blood, and light in my bones. O Allah, increase for me light, and grant me light, and make for me light. Glory be to the One Who wrapped Himself in might and spoke of it; Glory be to the One Who clothed Himself in glory and was generous through it; Glory be to the One for Whom glorification is befitting to none but Him; Glory be to the Possessor of bounty and blessings; Glory be to the Possessor of glory and generosity; Glory be to the Possessor of majesty and honor.'"

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Gharib, we do not know of it except from the Hadith of Ibn Abi Laila, from this route. Shu'bah and Sufyan Ath-Thawri have both narrated from Salamah bin Kuhail, from Kuraib, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) some of this Hadith, but they did not mention it in its lengthy form.
tirmidhi||3799:
Narrated 'Uthman bin 'Abdullah bin Mawhab: That a man from the people of Egypt performed Hajj to the House, and he saw a group of people sitting, so he said: "Who are these?" They said: "Quraish." He said: "Who is this shaikh?" They said: "Ibn 'Umar." So he went to him and said: "I am going to ask you about something, so tell me. I ask you by the sanctity of this House: Do you know that 'Uthman fled on the day of Uhud?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he was absent from the pledge of Ridwan, and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he was absent on the day of Badr, and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Allahu Akbar." So Ibn 'Umar said to him: "Come, let me explain to you what you have asked about. As for his fleeing on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that Allah has pardoned him and forgiven him. As for his absence on the day of Badr, he had - or was married to - the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'You shall have the reward of a man who witnessed Badr, and his share (of the spoils).' And he ordered him to stay behind with her, and she was sick. As for his absence from the pledge of Ridwan, if there had been anyone more honored in the interior of Makkah than 'Uthman, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have sent him in place of 'Uthman. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Uthman to Makkah, and the pledge of Ridwan took place after 'Uthman had gone to Makkah." He said: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said with his right hand: 'This is the hand of 'Uthman,' and he struck it upon his own hand, and said: 'This is for 'Uthman,' may Allah be pleased with him." He said to him: "Now go, take this with you."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih.
tirmidhi||3752:
Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abu Ash-Shawarib narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abdul Malik bin Umair, from Ibn Abu Al-Mu'alla, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon one day and said: "Indeed, a man was given a choice by his Lord between living in this world as long as he wished and eating in this world as much as he wished, and meeting his Lord, and he chose to meet his Lord." He said: So Abu Bakr wept, and the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you not wonder at this old man? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned a righteous man who was given a choice by his Lord between this world and meeting his Lord, and he chose to meet his Lord!" He said: Abu Bakr was the most knowledgeable of them about what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said, so Abu Bakr said: "Rather, we would ransom you with our fathers and our wealth." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one among the people who has been more gracious to us in his companionship and with what he possesses than the son of Abu Quhafah. If I were to take a close friend, I would have taken the son of Abu Quhafah as a close friend, but there is affection and brotherhood of faith, affection and brotherhood of faith" - twice or three times - "and indeed your companion is the close friend of Allah."

This Hadith has also been reported from Abu 'Awanah, from Abdul Malik bin Umair, with a different chain of narration than this one. The meaning of his saying "Amanna ilaina" is "he was gracious to us." There is also a narration on this topic from Abu Sa'eed. This Hadith is Hasan Gharib.
tirmidhi||533:
Narrated An-Nu'man bin Bashir: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the two 'Eids and in Jumu'ah: 'Sabbih Isma Rabbika Al-A'la' and 'Hal Ataka Hadith Al-Ghashiyah,' and sometimes they would fall on the same day, so he would recite them both."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are other narrations on this topic from Abu Waqid, Samurah bin Jundab, and Ibn 'Abbas.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of An-Nu'man bin Bashir is Hasan Sahih. This is how Sufyan Ath-Thawri and Mis'ar reported it from Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Muntashir, similar to the narration of Abu 'Awanah. As for Sufyan bin 'Uyainah, there is a difference in the narration from him; it is reported from him from Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Muntashir, from his father, from Habib bin Salim, from his father, from An-Nu'man bin Bashir. But we do not know of Habib bin Salim narrating from his father. Habib bin Salim was the freed slave of An-Nu'man bin Bashir, and he narrated several Hadiths from An-Nu'man bin Bashir. It has also been reported from Ibn 'Uyainah, from Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Muntashir, in a manner similar to the narration of these (other narrators). It has been reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the prayer of the two 'Eids: "Iqtarabat As-Sa'ah," and this is what Ash-Shafi'i says.
tirmidhi||560:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed during an eclipse, so he recited, then bowed, then recited, then bowed, then recited, then bowed - three times - then he prostrated with two prostrations, and the other (unit) was similar to it.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are narrations on this topic from 'Ali, 'Aishah, 'Abdullah bin 'Amr, An-Nu'man bin Bashir, Al-Mughirah bin Shu'bah, Abu Mas'ud, Abu Bakrah, Samurah, Abu Musa Al-Ashari, Ibn Mas'ud, Asma' bint Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, Ibn 'Umar, Qabisah Al-Hilali, Jabir bin 'Abdullah, 'Abdur-Rahman bin Samurah, and Ubayy bin Ka'b.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Ibn 'Abbas is a Hasan Sahih Hadith. And it has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he prayed during an eclipse with four Rak'ah and four prostrations. This is what Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq say.

He said: The people of knowledge differed regarding the recitation in the eclipse prayer. Some of the people of knowledge held the view that the recitation in it during the day should be silent. Others held the view that the recitation in it should be aloud, similar to the two 'Eid prayers and the Friday prayer, and this is what Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq say - they hold the view that it should be recited aloud. Ash-Shafi'i said: It should not be recited aloud in it.

Both of these two reports have been confirmed as authentic from the Prophet (ﷺ). It has been confirmed from him that he prayed four Rak'ah with four prostrations, and it has also been confirmed from him that he prayed six Rak'ah with four prostrations. This, according to the people of knowledge, is permissible depending on the length of the eclipse: if the eclipse is prolonged, then he prays six Rak'ah with four prostrations, and that is permissible; and if he prays four Rak'ah with four prostrations and lengthens the recitation, that is also permissible. Our companions hold the view that the eclipse prayer should be performed in congregation, for both a solar and a lunar eclipse.
tirmidhi||3654:
Ahmad bin Al-Hasan narrated to us, Sulaiman bin 'Abdur-Rahman Ad-Dimashqi narrated to us, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from 'Ata' bin Abi Rabah and 'Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), 'Ali bin Abi Talib came to him and said: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, this Qur'an has slipped away from my chest, and I do not find myself able to retain it.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'O Abul-Hasan, shall I not teach you words by which Allah will benefit you, and benefit through them whomever you teach them, and which will make firm in your chest what you have learned?' He said: 'Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah, teach me.' He said: 'When the night of Friday comes, if you are able to rise in the last third of the night, then it is a witnessed hour and supplication in it is answered. My brother Ya'qub said to his sons: (I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord) meaning until the night of Friday comes. But if you are not able to do so, then rise in the middle of it, and if you are not able to do so, then rise at the beginning of it, and pray four Rak'ah, reciting in the first Rak'ah the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah) and Surat Ya-Sin, and in the second Rak'ah the Opening of the Book and Ha-Mim, Ad-Dukhan, and in the third Rak'ah the Opening of the Book and Alif-Lam-Mim Tanzil, As-Sajdah, and in the fourth Rak'ah the Opening of the Book and Tabarak, Al-Mufassal. When you finish the Tashahhud, then praise Allah, and extol Allah with excellent praise, and send blessings upon me and do so excellently, and upon all the rest of the Prophets, and ask forgiveness for the believing men and believing women and for your brothers who preceded you in faith. Then say at the end of that: "O Allah, have mercy on me by abandoning sins forever as long as You keep me alive, and have mercy on me by sparing me from burdening myself with what does not concern me, and grant me good insight into what pleases You concerning me. O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Possessor of Majesty and Honor and Might which cannot be resisted, I ask You, O Allah, O Most Merciful, by Your Majesty and the light of Your Face, to make my heart hold fast to the memorization of Your Book as You have taught me, and grant me to recite it in the manner that pleases You concerning me. O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Possessor of Majesty and Honor and Might which cannot be resisted, I ask You, O Allah, O Most Merciful, by Your Majesty and the light of Your Face, to illuminate my sight with Your Book, and to set free my tongue with it, and to relieve my heart through it, and to expand my chest through it, and to cleanse my body through it, for none can help me attain the truth except You, and none can grant it except You, and there is no might and no power except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great." O Abul-Hasan, do this for three Fridays, or five, or seven, and it will be answered by Allah's permission. By the One Who sent me with the truth, it has never failed a believer.'"

'Abdullah bin 'Abbas said: "By Allah, 'Ali did not remain more than five or seven (days) before he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a gathering similar to that one, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, before this I would only take in four verses or so, and when I recited them to myself they would slip away, but today I learn forty verses or so, and when I recite them to myself it is as if the Book of Allah is right before my eyes. And I used to hear a Hadith, and when I repeated it, it would slip away, but today I hear Hadiths, and when I narrate them I do not miss a single letter of them.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said to him: "A believer, by the Lord of the Ka'bah, O Abul-Hasan!"

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Gharib; we do not know it except through the narration of Al-Walid bin Muslim.
tirmidhi||3731:
Narrated by Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Al-Husain bin Abi Halimah from Qasr Al-Ahnaf, and Ahmad bin 'Abdah Ad-Dabbi, and 'Ali bin Hujr - the meaning being the same - they said: "Isa bin Yunus narrated to us, 'Umar bin 'Abdullah, the freed slave of Ghufrah, narrated to us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad, from the descendants of 'Ali bin Abi Talib, narrated to me: 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), when he would describe the Prophet (ﷺ), would say: "He was not tall to the point of excess, nor short and compact. He was of medium stature among people. His hair was neither tightly curled nor completely straight, but wavy and combed. He was not fleshy-faced, nor was his face rounded, but there was roundness in his face. He was white with a reddish tinge, dark-eyed, with long eyelashes, with pronounced joints and shoulder-blades. He had no hair on his body except a fine line (from chest to navel). His palms and feet were thick. When he walked, he walked with vigor, as if walking downhill. When he turned to look at something, he turned with his whole body. Between his shoulders was the seal of prophethood, and he is the seal of the Prophets. He was the most generous of people in giving, the most open-hearted, the most truthful in speech, the gentlest in nature, and the noblest in companionship. Whoever saw him unexpectedly held him in awe, and whoever came to know him closely loved him." The one describing him would say: "I never saw the like of him before or after him."'"

Abu 'Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Gharib (good, strange); its chain of narration is not connected.

Abu Ja'far said: I heard Al-Asma'i say, explaining the description of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Al-Mumaghghat means one who is excessively tall." And I heard a Bedouin say: "Tamaghghata fi nash-shabatin" meaning he stretched it (the arrow) with great force.

As for "Al-Mutaraddid," it refers to one whose limbs seem to fold into each other due to shortness.

As for "Al-Qatat," it means one with extremely tight, curly hair, while "Rajil" refers to one whose hair has slight waviness.

As for "Al-Mutahham," it means one who is fleshy and heavily built.

As for "Al-Mukalthum," it means one with a round face.

As for "Al-Mushrab," it refers to one whose whiteness is mixed with a reddish tinge, and "Al-Adja'" means one with intensely black eyes, and "Al-Ahdab" means one with long eyelashes.

"Al-Katad" refers to the area where the shoulders meet, which is the upper back.

"Al-Masrubah" refers to the fine line of hair that appears like a thin stick extending from the chest to the navel.

"Ash-Shathn" refers to thickness in the fingers of the hands and feet.

"At-Taqallu'" means to walk with strength and vigor, and "As-Sabab" means a downward slope, as one would say: "We descended down a slope (sabub or sabab)."

His saying "Jalil Al-Mushash" refers to the tops of the shoulders.

"Al-'Ashirah" means companionship, and "Al-'Ashir" means companion.

"Al-Badihah" means a sudden encounter, as one says: "Badahtuhu bi amrin," meaning "I confronted him suddenly with a matter."
tirmidhi||561:
Muhammad bin 'Abdul-Malik bin Abi Ash-Shawarib narrated to us, Yazid bin Zurai' narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'Aishah, that she said: "The sun eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led the people in prayer, and he prolonged the recitation, then he performed a prostration (bowing), and he prolonged the bowing, then he raised his head and prolonged the recitation, which was shorter than the first, then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, which was shorter than the first, then he raised his head and prostrated. Then he did the same in the second unit (Rak'ah)."

Abu 'Eisa said: "This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. This is what Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq say; they view the eclipse prayer as four Rak'ahs with four prostrations."

Ash-Shafi'i said: "He recites in the first Rak'ah the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah) and something similar to Surat Al-Baqarah, silently if it is during the day. Then he performs a prolonged bowing similar in length to his recitation. Then he raises his head with the Takbir, and remains standing as he was, and recites again the Opening of the Book and something similar to Surat Al 'Imran. Then he performs a prolonged bowing similar to his recitation. Then he raises his head and says: 'Allah hears the one who praises Him (Sami' Allahu Liman Hamidah).' Then he performs two complete prostrations, remaining in each prostration for a duration similar to what he remained in his bowing. Then he stands and recites the Opening of the Book and something similar to Surat An-Nisa. Then he performs a prolonged bowing similar to his recitation. Then he raises his head with the Takbir and remains standing. Then he recites something similar to Surat Al-Ma'idah. Then he performs a prolonged bowing similar to his recitation. Then he raises and says: 'Allah hears the one who praises Him.' Then he performs two prostrations, then performs the Tashahhud and gives the Salam."
tirmidhi||564:
Narrated Salim: from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) led one of the two groups in prayer for one Rak'ah while the other group faced the enemy. Then they withdrew and took the position of the others, and the others came and he led them in another Rak'ah, then he said the Salam for them. Then these stood and completed their Rak'ah, and those stood and completed their Rak'ah.

Abu Eisa said: This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. Musa bin 'Uqbah has also narrated similarly from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar.

He said: There are narrations on this topic from Jabir, Hudhaifah, Zaid bin Thabit, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Mas'ud, Sahl bin Abu Hathmah, Abu 'Ayyash Az-Zuraqi whose name is Zaid bin Samit, and Abu Bakrah.

Abu Eisa said: Malik bin Anas held the view regarding Salat Al-Khawf according to the Hadith of Sahl bin Abu Hathmah, and this is the view of Ash-Shafi'i. Ahmad said: "The Salat Al-Khawf has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) in various forms, and I do not know of anything in this topic except an authentic Hadith, and I prefer the Hadith of Sahl bin Abu Hathmah." Similarly, Ishaq bin Ibrahim said: "The narrations from the Prophet (ﷺ) about Salat Al-Khawf are established." He held the view that whatever has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding Salat Al-Khawf is permissible, and this depends on the degree of fear. Ishaq said: "We do not prefer the Hadith of Sahl bin Abu Hathmah over the other narrations."
tirmidhi||576:
Yahya bin Musa narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Yazid bin 'Abdullah bin Qusait, from 'Ata' bin Yasar, from Zaid bin Thabit who said: "I recited An-Najm (Surat An-Najm) to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he did not prostrate during it."

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Zaid bin Thabit is a Hasan Sahih Hadith. Some of the people of knowledge have interpreted this Hadith, saying: "The Prophet (ﷺ) only refrained from prostrating because when Zaid bin Thabit recited it and did not prostrate, the Prophet (ﷺ) did not prostrate." They said: "The prostration is obligatory upon whoever hears it," and they did not permit leaving it. They said: "If a man hears it while he is not in a state of purity, then when he performs ablution he should prostrate." This is the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri and the people of Kufa, and it is what Ishaq says.

Some of the people of knowledge said: "The prostration is only required for one who intends to prostrate during it and seeks its merit," and they permitted leaving it if that was one's intention. They cited as evidence the Marfu' Hadith of Zaid bin Thabit, where he said: "I recited An-Najm to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he did not prostrate during it." They said: "If the prostration were obligatory, the Prophet (ﷺ) would not have left Zaid without correcting him, such that Zaid would prostrate and the Prophet (ﷺ) would prostrate."

They also cited as evidence the Hadith of 'Umar, that he recited a verse containing a prostration on the pulpit, so he came down and prostrated. Then he recited it on the following Friday, and the people prepared themselves to prostrate, so he said: "It was not prescribed for us except that we wish (to do it)." So he did not prostrate, and they did not prostrate. Some of the people of knowledge have adopted this view, and it is the view of Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad.
tirmidhi||621:
