Ziyad bin Ayyub Al-Baghdadi, Ibrahim bin 'Abdullah Al-Harawi, and Muhammad bin Kamil Al-Marwazi narrated to us - the meaning being the same - they said: 'Abbad bin Al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan bin Husain, from Az-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote the document of Zakat but did not send it out to his workers until he passed away, and he kept it tied to his sword. When he passed away, Abu Bakr acted according to it until he passed away, and (then) 'Umar (acted according to it) until he passed away. In it was written:

"For every five camels, one sheep (is due); for ten, two sheep; for fifteen, three sheep; for twenty, four sheep; for twenty-five, one Bint Makhad, up to thirty-five. If it increases (beyond that), then a Bint Labun is due, up to forty-five. If it increases, then a Hiqqah is due, up to sixty. If it increases, then a Jadha'ah is due, up to seventy-five. If it increases, then two Bint Labuns are due, up to ninety. If it increases, then two Hiqqahs are due, up to one hundred and twenty. If it increases beyond one hundred and twenty, then for every fifty, a Hiqqah, and for every forty, a Bint Labun.

As for sheep: For every forty sheep, one sheep is due, up to one hundred and twenty. If it increases, then two sheep, up to two hundred. If it increases, then three sheep, up to three hundred sheep. If it increases beyond three hundred sheep, then for every hundred sheep, one sheep. Then there is nothing due (in addition) until it reaches four hundred.

Animals that are separate should not be combined, and animals that are combined should not be separated, out of fear of (increasing) the Zakat. Whatever is jointly owned by two partners, they settle between themselves equally. Neither an old, worn-out animal nor one with a defect should be taken for Zakat."

Az-Zuhri said: "When the Zakat collector comes, he divides the sheep into three parts: a third that are the best, a third that are average, and a third that are the worst, and the collector takes from the average."

Az-Zuhri did not mention cattle.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are other reports on this topic from Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, from Bahz bin Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, and from Abu Dharr and Anas.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Ibn 'Umar is a Hasan Hadith, and it is acted upon according to the majority of the jurists.

Yunus bin Yazid and more than one other narrator reported this Hadith from Az-Zuhri, from Salim, without making it a Marfu' report (i.e., without attributing it directly to the Prophet ﷺ). It was only Sufyan bin Husain who made it Marfu'.
tirmidhi||759:
Narrated Abu Ayyub: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, that is (equivalent to) fasting the entire year."

There are also narrations on this topic from Jabir, Abu Hurairah, and Thawban.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] The Hadith of Abu Ayyub is Hasan Sahih. Some people have recommended fasting six days of Shawwal on the basis of this Hadith. Ibn Al-Mubarak said: "It is Hasan; it is similar to fasting three days from every month." Ibn Al-Mubarak said: "It is reported in some of the Hadith: 'And this fast is joined to Ramadan.'" Ibn Al-Mubarak preferred that the six days be at the beginning of the month. It has been reported from Ibn Al-Mubarak that he said: "If one fasts six days of Shawwal separately (not consecutively), then that is permissible."

He said: 'Abdul-Aziz bin Muhammad reported this from Safwan bin Sulaim and Sa'd bin Sa'eed, from 'Umar bin Thabit, from Abu Ayyub, from the Prophet (ﷺ). Shu'bah reported this Hadith from Warqa' bin 'Umar, from Sa'd bin Sa'eed. Sa'd bin Sa'eed is the brother of Yahya bin Sa'eed Al-Ansari, and some of the people of Hadith have criticized Sa'd bin Sa'eed with regard to his memory.

Narrated Al-Hasan Al-Basri: that when the fasting of six days of Shawwal was mentioned in his presence, he would say: "By Allah, indeed Allah has been pleased to make the fasting of this month equivalent to the fasting of the whole year."
tirmidhi||662:
Narrated Al-Qasim bin Muhammad: "I heard Abu Hurairah saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts charity, and He takes it with His right hand, and He nurtures it for one of you just as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel becomes like the size of (the mountain of) Uhud."'" And the confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Sublime: "And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants" and "takes the charities" and "Allah eliminates usury and nurtures charities."

[Abu Eisa said:] This Hadith is Hasan Sahih. Something similar to this has been reported from 'Aishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

More than one of the people of knowledge have said, concerning this Hadith and what resembles it among the narrations about the Attributes and the descent of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, every night to the lowest heaven: "These narrations are established as valid and are to be believed in. They should not be imagined [in a bodily sense], nor should one ask 'how?'" This has been reported from Malik, Sufyan bin 'Uyainah, and 'Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, who said concerning these Hadiths: "Accept them as they are without asking how." This is likewise the position of the people of knowledge among the people of the Sunnah and the community (Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah).

As for the Jahmiyyah, they rejected these narrations and said: "This is anthropomorphism (Tashbih)." Allah, Mighty and Sublime, mentioned in more than one place in His Book the Hand, the Hearing, and the Sight, but the Jahmiyyah reinterpreted these verses, explaining them differently from how the people of knowledge explained them. They said: "Allah did not create Adam with His Hand," and they said: "The meaning of 'Hand' here is 'Power.'"

Ishaq bin Ibrahim said: "Anthropomorphism only occurs if one says 'a hand like a hand' or 'similar to a hand,' or 'a hearing like a hearing' or 'similar to a hearing.' If one says 'a hearing like a hearing' or 'similar to a hearing,' then this is anthropomorphism. But if one says, as Allah the Exalted said, 'Hand,' 'Hearing,' and 'Sight,' without saying 'how,' and without saying 'similar to a hearing' or 'like a hearing,' then this is not anthropomorphism. This is as Allah the Exalted said in His Book: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.'"
tirmidhi||894:
Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Al-Mas'udi, from Al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent the weak members of his family ahead, and said: "Do not stone the Jamrah until the sun has risen."

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Ibn 'Abbas is a Hasan Sahih Hadith. The practice on this Hadith among the people of knowledge is that they see no harm in the weak going ahead from Muzdalifah at night to reach Mina. And most of the people of knowledge hold, in accordance with the Hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ), that they should not stone (the Jamrah) until the sun has risen. Some of the people of knowledge permitted stoning it at night, but the practice is upon the Hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) that they should not stone (it before sunrise). This is the view of Ath-Thawri and Ash-Shafi'i.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me with the baggage," is a Sahih Hadith, and it has been reported from him through more than one route. Shu'bah reported this Hadith from Mushash, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, from Al-Fadl bin 'Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent the weak members of his family ahead from Jam' at night. This is an erroneous Hadith; Mushash erred in it and added in it "from Al-Fadl bin 'Abbas." Ibn Jurayj and others reported this Hadith from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, and they did not mention in it "from Al-Fadl bin 'Abbas." Mushash was from Basrah, and Shu'bah reported from him.
malik||485: Yahya related to me from Malik from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Sasaa from his father from Abu Said al-Khudri that he heard a man reciting "Say: He is Allah, the One" (Surat al-Ikhlas) repeatedly. When morning came, he went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned this to him, as if the man considered it insufficient. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "By the One in whose hand my soul is, it is indeed equal to a third of the Qur'an."
tirmidhi||889:
Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya bin Sa'eed narrated to us, from Isma'il bin Abi Khalid, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'eed bin Jubair, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, a similar report. Muhammad bin Bashshar said: Yahya said: "And what is correct is the Hadith of Sufyan."

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There are narrations on this topic from 'Ali, Abu Ayyub, 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Jabir, and Usamah bin Zaid.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Ibn 'Umar according to the narration of Sufyan is more accurate than the narration of Isma'il bin Abi Khalid, and the Hadith of Sufyan is a Hasan Sahih Hadith.

Abu 'Eisa said: Isra'il narrated this Hadith from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah and Khalid, the two sons of Malik, from Ibn 'Umar. And the Hadith of Sa'eed bin Jubair from Ibn 'Umar is also a Hasan Sahih Hadith; it was narrated by Salamah bin Kuhail from Sa'eed bin Jubair. As for Abu Ishaq, he narrated it from 'Abdullah and Khalid, the two sons of Malik, from Ibn 'Umar.

And that is what is acted upon according to the people of knowledge, because Maghrib prayer is not to be prayed except at Jam', so when he comes to Jam', which is Muzdalifah, he combines the two prayers with a single Iqamah, and he does not pray any voluntary prayer between them. This is what some of the people of knowledge have chosen and adopted, and it is the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri. Sufyan said: "And if he wishes, he may pray Maghrib, then eat his evening meal and remove his garments, then give the Iqamah and pray 'Isha."

And some of the people of knowledge said: He combines Maghrib and 'Isha at Muzdalifah with one Adhan and two Iqamahs; he calls the Adhan for Maghrib, gives the Iqamah, and prays Maghrib, then gives the Iqamah and prays 'Isha. This is the view of Ash-Shafi'i.

Abu 'Eisa said: Isra'il narrated this Hadith from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah and Khalid, the two sons of Malik, from Ibn 'Umar. And the Hadith of Sa'eed bin Jubair from Ibn 'Umar is also a Hasan Sahih Hadith; it was narrated by Salamah bin Kuhail from Sa'eed bin Jubair. As for Abu Ishaq, he narrated it from 'Abdullah and Khalid, the two sons of Malik, from Ibn 'Umar.
malik||486: And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Ubaydullah ibn Abd ar-Rahman, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, the mawla of the family of Zayd ibn al-Khattab, that he said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: "I came along with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he heard a man reciting (Say, He is Allah, the One), and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'It is obligatory.' I asked him, 'What is, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'The Garden.'" Abu Hurayrah said, "I wanted to go to him and give him the good news, but then I was afraid that I would miss the midday meal with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so I preferred the midday meal with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then I went to the man and found that he had already gone."
malik||671: And he narrated to me, from Malik, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih as-Samman, from Abu Hurairah, that he used to say: "Whoever has wealth and does not pay its zakat, it will be made to appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald serpent with two black spots above its eyes, pursuing him until it overtakes him, saying: 'I am your treasure.'"
tirmidhi||774:
Muhammad bin Yahya, Muhammad bin Rafi' An-Naisaburi, Mahmud bin Ghailan, and Yahya bin Musa narrated to us, they said: Abdur-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Yahya bin Abi Kathir, from Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Qarith, from As-Sa'ib bin Yazid, from Rafi' bin Khadij, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who performs cupping and the one who has cupping performed on him have both broken their fast."

Abu Eisa said: There are narrations on this topic from Ali, Sa'd, Shaddad bin Aws, Thawban, Usamah bin Zaid, Aishah, Ma'qil bin Sinan - and it is also said Ibn Yasar - Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, Abu Musa, and Bilal.

Abu Eisa said: The Hadith of Rafi' bin Khadij is a Hasan Hadith.

It has been mentioned from Ahmad bin Hanbal that he said: "The most authentic thing on this topic is the Hadith of Rafi' bin Khadij."

It has been mentioned from Ali bin Abdullah that he said: "The most authentic thing on this topic is the Hadith of Thawban and Shaddad bin Aws, because Yahya bin Abi Kathir narrated both Hadiths - the Hadith of Thawban and the Hadith of Shaddad bin Aws - from Abu Qilabah."

Some of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and others disliked cupping for the one who is fasting, to the extent that some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) would have themselves cupped at night, among them Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari and Ibn Umar. This is what Ibn Al-Mubarak says.

Abu Eisa said: I heard Ishaq bin Manzur saying: Abdur-Rahman bin Mahdi said: "Whoever has himself cupped while fasting must make up that day."

Ishaq bin Manzur said: This is also what Ahmad bin Hanbal and Ishaq bin Ibrahim said.

Abu Eisa said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Az-Za'farani informed me, saying: Ash-Shafi'i said: "It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he was cupped while he was fasting, and it has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: 'The one who performs cupping and the one who has cupping performed on him have both broken their fast.' I do not know either of these two Hadiths to be firmly established. If a man were to avoid cupping while fasting, that would be more preferable to me. But if a fasting person were to have himself cupped, I would not consider that to break his fast."

Abu Eisa said: This was the view of Ash-Shafi'i in Baghdad. As for in Egypt, he leaned towards the permissibility, and did not see any harm in cupping for the one who is fasting, using as evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) was cupped during the Farewell Pilgrimage while he was in a state of Ihram and fasting.
tirmidhi||907:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) placed two sandals [around the neck of the sacrificial animal as markers] and marked the sacrificial animal with a wound on its right side at Dhul-Hulaifah, and wiped away the blood from it.

[Abu 'Eisa said:] There is also a narration on this topic from Al-Miswar bin Makhramah.

Abu 'Eisa said: The Hadith of Ibn 'Abbas is Hasan Sahih. Abu Hassan Al-A'raj's name is Muslim.

This is acted upon according to the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and others; they hold the view of marking [the sacrificial animal by wounding it]. This is the view of Ath-Thawri, Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.

Abu 'Eisa said: I heard Yusuf bin 'Eisa saying: "I heard Waki' say, when he narrated this Hadith: 'Do not look to the saying of the people of opinion (Ahl Ar-Ra'i) concerning this matter, for marking [the sacrificial animal] is a Sunnah, and their saying is an innovation.'"

He said: And I heard Abu As-Sa'ib saying: "We were with Waki', and he said to a man present with him, one of those who look into opinion (Ra'i): 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marked [his sacrificial animal], yet Abu Hanifah says it is mutilation.'" The man said: "It has indeed been narrated from Ibrahim An-Nakha'i that he said: 'Marking is mutilation.'" He said: "So I saw Waki' become extremely angry, and he said: 'I tell you that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said [such], and you tell me that Ibrahim said [otherwise]! How deserving you are of being imprisoned and not released until you retract this statement of yours!'"
malik||951: Yahya related to me from Malik from Ibn Shihab a similar hadith.
tirmidhi||886:
Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Ahmad Az-Zubairi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdur-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Ayyash bin Abi Rabi'ah, from Zaid bin Ali, from his father, from Ubaidullah bin Abi Rafi', from Ali bin Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) halted at Arafah and said: 'This is Arafah and this is the standing place, and all of Arafah is a standing place.' Then he departed when the sun had set, having mounted Usamah bin Zaid behind him, and he began gesturing with his hand in a manner, while the people were pushing to the right and left. He would turn towards them and say: 'O people, calmness!' Then he came to Jam' (Muzdalifah) and led them in both prayers together. When morning came, he came to Quzah and stood upon it and said: 'This is Quzah, and it is the standing place, and all of Jam' is a standing place.' Then he departed until he reached the valley of Muhassir, and he struck his she-camel so it trotted quickly until it crossed the valley. Then he stopped, having mounted Al-Fadl behind him. Then he went to the Jamrah and stoned it. Then he came to the place of sacrifice and said: 'This is the place of sacrifice, and all of Mina is a place of sacrifice.' A young girl from Khath'am sought his ruling, saying: 'My father is a very old man, and the obligation of Allah regarding Hajj has become due upon him - would it suffice for me to perform Hajj on his behalf?' He said: 'Perform Hajj on behalf of your father.'" He said: "And he turned the neck of Al-Fadl (away). So Al-Abbas said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why did you turn the neck of your cousin?' He said: 'I saw a young man and a young woman, and I did not feel safe from Satan regarding them.'" He said: "Then a man came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I departed (from Mina to Makkah for Tawaf) before shaving.' He said: 'Shave, or trim, and there is no harm.'" He said: "Then another came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed before stoning.' He said: 'Stone, and there is no harm.'" He said: "Then he came to the House and performed Tawaf around it. Then he came to Zamzam and said: 'O children of Abdul-Muttalib, were it not that the people would overpower you regarding it, I would draw water (from it myself).'"

[Abu Isa said:] There is also a narration on this topic from Jabir.

Abu Isa said: The Hadith of Ali is a Hasan Sahih Hadith. We do not know of it from the Hadith of Ali except through this route, from the Hadith of Abdur-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Ayyash. It has been reported by more than one narrator from Ath-Thawri, similar to this.

The practice according to the people of knowledge is upon this - they hold that Zuhr and Asr are to be combined at Arafah during the time of Zuhr. Some of the people of knowledge said: If a man prays in his tent, and does not attend the prayer with the Imam, then if he wishes, he may combine the two prayers just as the Imam did.

He said: And Zaid bin Ali is the son of Husain bin Ali bin Abi Talib, peace be upon him.
malik||927: Yahya related to me from Malik from Abd ar-Rahman ibn al-Qasim from his father that A'isha said, "I came to Makka while I was menstruating, and I did not do tawaf around the Kabah, nor between as-Safa and al-Marwa. I complained about that to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said, 'Do as the pilgrims do, except that you should not do tawaf around the Kabah, nor between as-Safa and al-Marwa, until you are pure.'"
malik||1176: Yahya related to me from Malik from Ibn Shihab, from Talha ibn Abdullah ibn Awf - and he said that he was the most knowledgeable of them about that - and from Abu Salama ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, that Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf divorced his wife irrevocably while he was ill, and Uthman ibn Affan gave her a share of inheritance from him after her waiting period had finished.
malik||1191: Yahya related to me from Malik from Nafi that Abdullah ibn Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating, during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about that, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Command him to take her back, then keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then is pure again. Then, if he wishes, he may keep her after that, or if he wishes, he may divorce her before he touches her. That is the waiting period which Allah has commanded women to be divorced for."
malik||1203: And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Nafi': that Abdullah ibn Umar divorced a wife of his who was living in the residence of Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. That residence was on his way to the mosque, but he used to take another route, from behind the houses, because he disliked having to ask permission to enter upon her, until he took her back.
malik||672: Yahya related to me from Malik that he read the letter of Umar ibn al-Khattab concerning zakat. He said, "I found in it: In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. The book of zakat: For twenty-four camels or fewer, sheep are due, one sheep for every five camels. When they reach twenty-five up to thirty-five, a female yearling camel (bint makhad) is due; if a bint makhad is not available, then a male two-year-old camel (ibn labun) is due. When they reach thirty-six up to forty-five, a female two-year-old camel (bint labun) is due. When they reach forty-six up to sixty, a three-year-old female camel (hiqqa) fit for breeding is due. When they reach sixty-one up to seventy-five, a four-year-old female camel (jadha) is due. When they reach seventy-six up to ninety, two female two-year-old camels (bint labun) are due. When they reach ninety-one up to one hundred and twenty, two three-year-old female camels (hiqqa) fit for breeding are due. If the number of camels increases beyond that, for every forty, a bint labun is due, and for every fifty, a hiqqa is due. As for sheep that graze freely, when they reach forty up to one hundred and twenty, one sheep is due. When they exceed that up to two hundred, two sheep are due. When they exceed that up to three hundred, three sheep are due. If they increase beyond that, then for every hundred, one sheep is due. No male goat, decrepit animal, or defective animal is to be taken for zakat, except what the zakat collector wishes to take. Animals belonging to different owners are not to be combined, nor are animals belonging to one owner to be separated, out of fear of the zakat obligation. Whatever is jointly owned by two partners, they are to settle between themselves equally. As for silver, when it reaches five uqiyas, a quarter of a tenth (2.5%) is due."
malik||1171: Yahya related to me from Malik that he had heard that Urwa bin az-Zubayr used to say about the child of a woman whose husband had made a mutual oath of condemnation against her (li'an), and about the child of fornication: that when he died, his mother inherited her due share as prescribed in the Book of Allah, Most High, and his brothers by his mother inherited their due shares, and the rest was inherited by the mawali of his mother, if she was a freed slave woman. If she was an Arab woman, she inherited her due share, and his brothers by his mother inherited their due shares, and what remained belonged to the Muslims.
malik||1338: And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: "There is no riba except in gold or silver, or in that which is measured or weighed of what is eaten or drunk."
malik||1748: It reached A'isha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that a household living in her house had a backgammon set in their possession, so she sent word to them, "If you do not remove it, I will remove you from my house," and she disapproved of that.
sunan-darimi||2584: Abu al-Walid informed us, [saying]: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, with his chain of transmission, similar to it.
sunan-darimi||2427: (Report with a stopped chain) Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, from Al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: A group of us, companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sat together and discussed among ourselves, saying: If only we knew which of deeds was most beloved to Allah, the Exalted, we would perform it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise" (Surah Al-Hashr, verse 1) until He completed it. Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, then recited it to us until he completed it. Abu Salamah said: Ibn Salam recited it to us. Yahya said: Abu Salamah recited it to us, and Yahya recited it to us, and Al-Awza'i recited it to us, and Muhammad recited it to us.
sunan-darimi||2503: Yahya ibn Hammad informed us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Mujahid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, from Abu Dharr: that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I have been given five things which no prophet before me was given: I was sent to the red and the black, the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, the spoils of war were made lawful for me, and they were not made lawful for anyone before me, I was granted victory through terror for a distance of a month's journey, the enemy being terrified of me for a month's journey. And it was said to me: 'Ask, and you shall be given.' So I withheld my supplication as intercession for my nation, and it will reach you, if Allah Almighty wills, whoever does not associate anything with Allah."
sunan-darimi||2718: Abu al-Walid informed us, Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib saying: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded a man that when he takes to his bed, he should say: "O Allah, I have submitted myself to You, and I have turned my face towards You, and I have entrusted my affair to You, and I have taken refuge with You, out of desire for You and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed, and in Your Prophet whom You have sent." For if he dies, he dies upon the natural disposition (al-fitrah).
sunan-al-daraqutni||4237: He said: and 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, [saying]: Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Sabrah al-Qurashi narrated to me, from Husayn ibn 'Abdullah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah gave birth to Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Her child has set her free."
sunan-al-daraqutni||4008: He said: Hisham said: Yahya wrote to me, from Ya'la ibn Hakim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to say: "Declaring [something] forbidden is an oath which must be atoned for." And Ibn 'Abbas said: "Indeed you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example: the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had declared his slave-girl forbidden to himself, so Allah said: 'Why do you forbid that which Allah has made lawful for you' (Surat al-Tahrim, verse 1), up to His saying: 'Allah has already ordained for you [Muslims] the dissolution of your oaths' (Surat al-Tahrim, verse 2). So he atoned for his oath and made the prohibition an oath."
sunan-darimi||1514:
Ishaq bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Mu'adh bin Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Zurarah bin Awfa, from Sa'd bin Hisham: that he divorced his wife and came to Medina to sell his property in order to put it into weapons and horses [for jihad]. He met a group of the Ansar, and they said: "Six of us intended to do that during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, but he forbade them and said: 'Do you not have an example in me?'"

Then he came to Basra, and he narrated to us that he met Abdullah bin Abbas and asked him about the Witr prayer. Ibn Abbas said: "Shall I not tell you about the most knowledgeable person regarding the Witr of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?" I said: "Yes indeed." He said: "The Mother of the Believers, Aishah. Go to her and ask her, then come back to me and tell me what she tells you."

So I went to Hakim bin Aflah and said to him: "Come with me to the Mother of the Believers, Aishah." He said: "I do not go to her; I have forbidden [myself from] these two factions." But I insisted on going. I said: "I implore you by oath to come with me." So we went, and we greeted her, and she recognized Hakim's voice and said: "Who is this?" I said: "Sa'd bin Hisham." She said: "Who is Hisham?" I said: "Hisham bin Amir." She said: "What a good man he was; he was killed on the day of Uhud."

I said: "Tell us about the character of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes indeed." She said: "Indeed, it [the Qur'an] was the character of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."

I wanted to get up and not ask anyone about anything until I meet Allah, but the matter of [nightly] standing [in prayer] occurred to me. So I said: "Tell us about the standing [in prayer] of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said: "Do you not recite: 'O you wrapped in garments (Al-Muzzammil)'?" I said: "Yes indeed." She said: "That was the standing [in prayer] of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The beginning of the surah was revealed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions stood [in prayer] until their feet became swollen. The last part of it was withheld in heaven for sixteen months, then it was revealed, so the night prayer became voluntary after having been obligatory."

I wanted to get up and not ask anyone about anything until I meet Allah, but the matter of the Witr prayer occurred to me. So I said: "Tell us about the Witr prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he slept, would place his tooth-stick near me. Then Allah would wake him whenever He willed to wake him, and he would pray nine cycles of prayer, not sitting except in the eighth. He would praise Allah and call upon his Lord, then he would stand without giving the greeting of peace. Then he would sit in the ninth, praising Allah and calling upon his Lord, and he would give one greeting of peace loud enough for us to hear. Then he would pray two more cycles while sitting. That makes eleven cycles, my son.

When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, grew old and put on weight, he prayed seven cycles, not sitting except in the sixth. He would praise Allah and call upon his Lord, then he would stand without giving the greeting of peace. Then he would sit in the seventh, praising Allah and calling upon his Lord, then he would give one greeting of peace. Then he would pray two more cycles while sitting. That makes nine, my son.

When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was overcome by sleep or illness, he would pray twelve cycles during the day. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he adopted a practice, loved to maintain it consistently. The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never stood in prayer for an entire night until morning, nor did he ever recite the entire Qur'an in one night, nor did he ever fast a complete month other than Ramadan."

Then I went to Ibn Abbas and told him [what she had said]. He said: "She has told you the truth. Indeed, if I were to visit her, I would speak to her face to face." I said: "Had I known that you do not visit her, I would not have told you [what she said]."
sunan-al-daraqutni||4481: Yahya bin Muhammad bin Sa'id told us, Muhammad bin Zunbur al-Makki told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim told us, from Yazid bin al-Had, from Muhammad bin Ibrahim, from Busr bin Sa'id, from Abu Qais the freed slave of Amr bin al-'As, from Amr bin al-'As, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When a judge passes judgment, exerting his effort (in ijtihad), and errs, he has a reward; then if he passes judgment and is correct, he has two rewards." Yazid bin al-Had said: I then narrated this hadith to Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm, and Abu Bakr said: This is how Abu Salamah narrated to me, from Abu Hurairah. Ibn Sa'id told us, Muhammad bin Abi Abdur Rahman al-Muqri told us, my father told us - and also - Ibn Sa'id told us, Ahmad bin Mansur told us, Abu Abdur Rahman al-Muqri told us, Haywah bin Shuraih told us, Yazid bin al-Had narrated to me, with both chains of transmission, similar to the wording of al-Qawariri.
abudawud||2107:
Narrated Umm Habibah: She was married to 'Ubaidullah ibn Jahsh, and he died in the land of Abyssinia. An-Najashi married her to the Prophet (ﷺ) and paid on his behalf a dower of four thousand (dirhams), and sent her to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Shurahbil ibn Hasanah.

Abu Dawud said: Hasanah was his mother.
nasai||3936: It was narrated from Ali bin Hujr who said: Shareek narrated to us, from Tariq, from Sa'eed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: "There is nothing wrong with leasing bare land for gold or silver."
abudawud||569: Narrated 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman: that 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen what innovations the women have introduced, he would have forbidden them the mosque as the women of the Children of Israel were forbidden it. Yahya said: I asked 'Amrah: Were the women of the Children of Israel forbidden it? She said: Yes.
sunan-al-daraqutni||3365:
The judge narrated it to us - the judge al-Mahamili narrated it to us, Al-'Abbas ibn Yazid narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abdullah, who said: "The blood-money for manslaughter is in fifths," then he explained it exactly as Abu 'Ubaydah and 'Alqamah explained it on his authority. This report, even though it contains an interruption (irsal), Ibrahim al-Nakha'i is the person most knowledgeable about 'Abdullah, his opinion, and his rulings, having taken this from his maternal uncles 'Alqamah, al-Aswad, and 'Abd al-Rahman - the two sons of Yazid - and others among the senior companions of 'Abdullah. He is the one who said: "When I say to you, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said,' it is from a group of his companions on his authority, but when I hear it from a single man, I name him to you."

And another point: the elevated (marfu') report which mentions "sons of makhad" - we do not know of anyone who narrated it except Khishf ibn Malik, from Ibn Mas'ud, and he is an unknown man. No one narrated it from him except Zayd ibn Jubayr ibn Harmal al-Jushami. The people of knowledge in hadith do not accept as proof a report narrated solely by a man who is not well-known; rather, knowledge is established for them by a report only when its narrators are either a well-known trustworthy person, or a man from whom the designation of "unknown" has been lifted. The lifting of the designation of "unknown" from him occurs when two or more men narrate from him. When this is his description, the designation of "unknown" is lifted from him and he then becomes known. But as for one from whom only a single man has narrated, being the sole narrator of a report, it is obligatory to withhold judgment regarding that report of his until someone else corroborates him. And Allah knows best.

And another point: regarding the report of Khishf ibn Malik, we do not know that anyone narrated it from Zayd ibn Jubayr on his authority except Hajjaj ibn Artah, and Hajjaj is a man well-known for tadlis (concealment in transmission) and for narrating from those he never met and from those he never heard from. Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir said: Hajjaj said to me, "Let no one ask me about the report" - meaning: when I narrate something to you, do not ask me who informed you of it. And Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah said: I was with Hajjaj ibn Artah one day, and he ordered the door to be closed, then said: "I did not hear anything from al-Zuhri, and I did not hear from Ibrahim, nor from al-Sha'bi except one hadith, nor from so-and-so, nor from so-and-so" - until he counted seventeen or more than ten, all of whom Hajjaj had narrated from. Then, after narrating from them, he claimed that he had never met them nor heard from them. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, and 'Isa ibn Yunus abandoned narrating from him after having sat with him and come to know him - and that they did so is sufficient proof of their knowledge and excellence regarding men. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "I visited Hajjaj ibn Artah and heard his speech, and he mentioned something I found objectionable, so I did not carry anything from him." Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan said: "I saw Hajjaj ibn Artah in Makkah, and I did not carry anything from him, nor did I carry anything from a man who narrated from him, whom I considered unreliable (mudtarib)." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "Hajjaj ibn Artah's hadith is not to be relied upon." 'Abdullah ibn Idris said: "I heard Hajjaj say, 'A man does not attain nobility until he abandons the congregational prayer.'" 'Isa ibn Yunus said: "I heard Hajjaj say, 'I go out to prayer and the porters and greengrocers jostle me.'" Jarir said: "I heard Hajjaj say, 'Love of wealth and status has destroyed me.'"

And another point: a group of trustworthy narrators transmitted this hadith from Hajjaj ibn Artah, but they differed among themselves regarding it. 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated it from Hajjaj with the wording we have mentioned from him, and 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad agreed with him on that. But Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi - who is among the trustworthy - differed from both of them, narrating it from Hajjaj, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khishf ibn Malik, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled concerning manslaughter that it be in fifths: twenty four-year-old she-camels, twenty five-year-old she-camels giving milk, twenty three-year-old male camels giving milk, twenty two-year-old she-camels, and twenty two-year-old male camels" - placing, in place of the four-year-old camels (hiqaq), the three-year-old male camels giving milk (bani labun).
sunan-al-daraqutni||772:
Al-Husayn ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ali ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us: I heard Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi say: I heard Imran ibn Husayn say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, traveled with us one night, then we stopped to rest, and we did not wake up until the heat of the sun. Six of us woke up - I have forgotten their names - then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, woke up and began to prevent them from waking the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: "Perhaps Allah has detained him for a purpose of His." So Abu Bakr began to say the takbir loudly, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, woke up. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, our prayer has passed!" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Your prayer has not passed. Move on from this place." So he moved on and traveled a short distance, then dismounted and prayed, and said: "Indeed, Allah has completed your prayer for you." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so did not pray with us." He said to him: "What prevented you from praying?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had a state of major impurity (janabah)." He said: "Then perform tayammum with the earth and pray with it, and when you are able to find water, then perform ghusl."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Ali to search for water. Each of us had a small water container, like the ears of a rabbit, between his skin and his garment - whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, became thirsty, we would hasten to give him water. He went until the day grew high and he did not find water. Then he spotted a figure. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Stay where you are until we see what this is." He said: There was a woman between two water-skins. It was said to her: "O servant of Allah, where is water?" She said: "There is no water for you, by Allah! I drew water yesterday, and I have traveled all day and all night, and we have reached this hour." They said to her: "Go to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said: "And who is the Messenger of Allah?" They said: "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said: "The madman of Quraysh?" They said: "He is not a madman, but he is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said: "O you people, leave me alone! By Allah, I have left behind young children of mine with the flock, and I fear I will not reach them before some of them die of thirst." But they gave her no choice in the matter until they brought her to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

He ordered the camel to be made to kneel, then he untied the water-skin from its top, then called for a large vessel and filled it with water, then handed it to the man in a state of major impurity, and said: "Go and perform ghusl." They said: "By Allah, we did not leave a single water container, water-skin, or vessel without filling it with water, while she watched." Then he tied up the water-skin from its top and sent the camel back, and said: "O woman, here is your water. By Allah, if Allah had not added to it, what has decreased from your water would not be even a single drop." He called for a cloak for her and it was spread out, then he said to us: "Whoever has something with him, let him bring it." So a man would come with a worn-out sandal, a worn-out garment, a handful of barley, a handful of dates, or a piece of bread, until they had gathered that for her. Then he tied it up for her and asked her about her people, and she told him.

He said: So she went until she came to her people. They said: "What kept you?" She said: "The madman of Quraysh took hold of me. By Allah, he is one of two things: either he is the greatest sorcerer between this - meaning the sky - and this - meaning the earth - or he is truly the Messenger of Allah." He said: The cavalry of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began raiding those around them while they remained safe. He said: So the woman said to her people: "O my people, by Allah, I see that this man has been grateful to you for what he took of your water. Do you not see that those around you are being raided while you remain safe, not being raided? Do you want something good?" They said: "What is it?" She said: "We go to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and we submit (become Muslims)." He said: So she came leading thirty households until they gave their allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and they became Muslims.
sunan-darimi||670:
(A truncated/discontinued-chain report) Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad ibn Umar ibn al-Kumayt narrated to us, Ali ibn Wahb al-Hamdani narrated to us, ad-Dahhak ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik passed through Medina on his way to Mecca, and he stayed there for some days. He said, "Is there anyone in Medina who met any of the Companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?" They said to him, "Abu Hazim, O Commander of the Believers." So he sent for him.

When Abu Hazim entered upon him, Sulayman said to him, "O Abu Hazim, what is this rudeness?" Abu Hazim said, "O Commander of the Believers, what rudeness have you seen from me?" He said, "The notable people of Medina came to me, but you did not come to me." Abu Hazim said, "O Commander of the Believers, I seek refuge for you with Allah from saying what was not so - you did not know me before this day, nor had I seen you." Sulayman then turned to Muhammad ibn Shihab az-Zuhri and said, "The old man was right, and I was wrong."

Sulayman said, "O Abu Hazim, why do we dislike death?" He said, "Because you have ruined the Hereafter and built up this world, so you dislike moving from what is built up to what is ruined." He said, "You are right, O Abu Hazim. So how will be the arrival tomorrow before Allah?" He said, "As for the doer of good, it is like an absent person arriving to his family, and as for the doer of evil, it is like a runaway slave arriving before his master." Sulayman wept and said, "I wish I knew what awaits us with Allah." He said, "Compare your deeds to the Book of Allah." He said, "And where would I find that?" He said, "'Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in the Hellfire' (Surat al-Infitar 82:13-14)."

Sulayman said, "Then where is the mercy of Allah, O Abu Hazim?" Abu Hazim said, "The mercy of Allah is near to those who do good." Sulayman said to him, "O Abu Hazim, which of Allah's servants is most noble?" He said, "Those possessing manly virtue and sound judgment." Sulayman said to him, "O Abu Hazim, which deeds are most excellent?" Abu Hazim said, "Performing the obligatory duties while avoiding the forbidden things." Sulayman said, "Which supplication is most heard?" Abu Hazim said, "The supplication of one who has been done good, for the one who did good to him." He said, "Which charity is most excellent?" He said, "That given to the needy beggar, and the utmost effort of one who has little, given without any reminder of the favor or any injury." He said, "Which speech is most just?" He said, "Speaking the truth before one you fear or one you hope for something from." He said, "Which believer is most clever?" He said, "A man who acts in obedience to Allah and guides people to it." He said, "Which believer is most foolish?" He said, "A man who lowers himself to follow the desire of his brother while that brother is being unjust, thereby selling his Hereafter for the worldly benefit of someone else."

Sulayman said to him, "You are right. So what do you say about the position we are in?" He said, "O Commander of the Believers, will you excuse me from this?" Sulayman said to him, "No, but give me some sincere advice." He said, "O Commander of the Believers, your forefathers subdued the people by the sword and took this dominion by force, without any consultation with the Muslims, and without their consent, to the point that they killed a great many of them. They have now departed from this world - would that you knew what they said and what was said to them!"

A man among those sitting with him said to him, "What an evil thing you have said, O Abu Hazim!" Abu Hazim said, "You have lied. Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from the scholars that they must make things clear to the people and not conceal it."

Sulayman said to him, "Then how can we set things right?" He said, "You should abandon arrogant boasting, hold fast to manly virtue, and distribute wealth equitably." Sulayman said to him, "How should we go about acquiring it?" Abu Hazim said, "Take it from its lawful sources, and place it with those entitled to it."

Sulayman said to him, "O Abu Hazim, would you be willing to accompany us, so that you might benefit from us and we might benefit from you?" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah from that." Sulayman said to him, "Why is that?" He said, "I fear that if I incline toward you even a little, Allah would make me taste a double portion of punishment in this life and a double portion in the next."

Sulayman said to him, "Present your needs to us." He said, "That you save me from the Fire and admit me into Paradise." Sulayman said, "That is not within my power." Abu Hazim said, "Then I have no need from you besides that." He said, "Then pray for me." Abu Hazim said, "O Allah, if Sulayman is Your close friend, then make easy for him the good of this world and the Hereafter; but if he is Your enemy, then seize him by the forelock toward what You love and are pleased with."

Sulayman said to him, "Enough!" Abu Hazim said, "I have been brief, yet I have said much, if you are among its people; but if you are not among its people, what benefit is there for me in shooting an arrow from a bow that has no string?"

Sulayman said to him, "Advise me." He said, "I shall advise you, and be brief: magnify your Lord, and hold Him too exalted that He should see you where He has forbidden you, or find you absent from where He has commanded you."

When Abu Hazim left his presence, Sulayman sent him one hundred dinars, and wrote to him: "Spend this, and you have with me much more than its like." He said: Abu Hazim returned it to him and wrote to him: "O Commander of the Believers, I seek refuge for you with Allah from your request to me being frivolous, or my returning it to you being mere generosity. I would not be pleased with it for you, so how could I be pleased with it for myself?"

And he wrote to him: "When Musa ibn Imran arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it shepherds watering their flocks, and found apart from them two young women holding back their flocks. He asked them [what was wrong], and they said, 'We cannot water our flocks until the shepherds finish, and our father is a very old man' (Surat al-Qasas 28:23). So he watered their flocks for them; then he withdrew to the shade and said, 'My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need' (Surat al-Qasas 28:24).

"That was because he was hungry and afraid, having no security. He asked his Lord and did not ask the people. The shepherds did not notice, but the two young women did notice. When they returned to their father, they told him the story and what he had said. Their father, who was Shu'ayb, said, 'This is a hungry man.' He said to one of them, 'Go and call him.' When she came to him, she showed him respect and covered her face, and said, 'Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us' (Surat al-Qasas 28:25). This was difficult for Musa when she mentioned 'reward you for having watered for us,' but he had no choice but to follow her, for he was among the mountains, hungry and fearful.

"When he followed her, the wind blew and began flapping her garments against her back, revealing to him the outline of her hips, for she had ample hips, and Musa would look away at one moment, then lower his gaze at another. When his patience was exhausted, he called out to her, 'O maidservant of Allah, walk behind me, and direct me by your words which way to go.'

"When he entered upon Shu'ayb, he found the evening meal prepared, and Shu'ayb said to him, 'Sit, young man, and eat.' Musa said to him, 'I seek refuge in Allah.' Shu'ayb said to him, 'Why? Are you not hungry?' He said, 'Yes, but I fear that this might be in exchange for what I did in watering for them, and we are from a household that would not sell any part of our religion for the earth's fill of gold.' Shu'ayb said to him, 'No, young man, but this is my custom and the custom of my forefathers - we offer hospitality to guests and feed people.' So Musa sat and ate."

[Abu Hazim continued]: "So if these hundred dinars are in exchange for what I have related, then carrion, blood, and swine's flesh in a state of necessity are more lawful than this; and if it is on account of some right of mine in the treasury, then I have equals in it - so if you treat us equally, well and good; otherwise, I have no need of it."
sunan-darimi||672:
(A discontinued/maqtu' hadith) Abdul Malik ibn Sulayman Abu Abdur-Rahman al-Antaki informed us, from Abbad ibn Abbad al-Khawwas ash-Shami, Abu Utbah, who said:

To proceed: Use reason, for reason is a blessing. Yet many a person of reason has had his heart occupied with excessive delving into matters that harm him, distracting him from benefiting from what he actually needs, until he has become heedless of that. It is part of the excellence of a person's reason to refrain from looking into matters in which there is no benefit in looking, so that the excess of his reason does not become a burden upon him in abandoning competition with those who fall short of him in righteous deeds. Or take the case of a man whose heart has been occupied by an innovation, in which he has made his religion dependent on men other than the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, or has contented himself with his own opinion regarding matters in which he sees guidance only through it, and sees misguidance only in abandoning it—claiming that he derived it from the Qur'an, while in fact he is calling people to depart from the Qur'an. Did the Qur'an not have bearers before him and before his companions, who acted upon its clear verses and believed in its ambiguous ones? They were, through it, a beacon lighting up the clear path. The Qur'an was the guide (imam) of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him; the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was the guide of his Companions; and his Companions were guides for those who came after them—men well-known and identified by name in the various lands, united in refuting the people of desires despite whatever differences existed among themselves. Meanwhile, the people of desires stumbled about, following their own opinions, along divergent paths that swerved from the right course and departed from the straight path. Their guides led them astray into confusing wastelands, and they plunged ever deeper, wandering blindly in their bewilderment. Whenever Satan introduced for them a new innovation in their misguidance, they moved on from it to another, because they did not seek the traces of those who came before them, nor did they follow the example of the Emigrants (al-Muhajirin).

It has been mentioned that Umar said to Ziyad: "Do you know what destroys Islam? The slip of a scholar, the disputation of a hypocrite using the Qur'an, and misguided leaders." Fear Allah, and beware of what has arisen among your Qur'an-reciters and the people of your mosques—backbiting, tale-carrying, and going about among people with two faces and two tongues. It has been mentioned that whoever has two faces in this world will have two faces in the Fire. The backbiter meets you and speaks ill, in your presence, of someone he thinks you would like to hear slandered, then he turns against you to your companion and brings him the same about you. So he achieves his purpose with each of you, while each of you remains unaware of what he has brought to the other about you. His presence, when he is with someone, is like the presence of a brother; but his absence, when away from someone, is like the absence of an enemy. Whoever is present with him receives his favor, and whoever is absent has no sanctity in his eyes. He deceives the one present with praise, and slanders the one absent through backbiting. O servants of Allah! Is there not among the people any right-minded person, any reformer, who would suppress this man's scheming and restrain him from violating the honor of his Muslim brother? Rather, he has come to know their inclinations through what he carries to them, so he has gained power over them, and they have granted him what he seeks, so he consumes his own religion along with theirs. So fear Allah, fear Allah! Defend the honor of those who are absent, and restrain your tongues from them except in good. Give sincere counsel to Allah regarding your community, since you are the bearers of the Book and the Sunnah. Indeed, the Book does not speak until it is spoken through, and the Sunnah is not acted upon until it is put into practice. So when will the ignorant learn, if the scholar remains silent, neither denouncing what has become manifest nor commanding what has been abandoned? Allah has taken a covenant from those given the Book: "You shall make it clear to mankind and not conceal it." Fear Allah, for you are living in an age in which piety has become thin, humility has become scarce, and knowledge has been carried by those who corrupt it. They love to be known for carrying it, and hate to be known for wasting it, so they speak about it according to their desires because of the error they have introduced into it, and they distort words away from the truth they have abandoned toward the falsehood they practice. Their sins are sins for which no forgiveness is sought, and their shortcomings are shortcomings that are not acknowledged. How can the seeker of guidance find guidance if the very guide is himself bewildered? They loved this world...

and disliked the standing of its people—so they shared with them in worldly life while distancing themselves from them in speech, defending themselves through speech from being associated with their own deeds. Thus they did not truly disavow what they claimed to disavow, nor did they truly enter into what they claimed to belong to—because the one who acts upon the truth is speaking even if he is silent. It has been mentioned that Allah, exalted is He, says: "I do not accept every speech of the wise man, but I look to his intention and his desire. If his intention and desire are for Me, I make his silence praise and reverence directed to Me, even if he does not speak." And Allah, exalted is He, said: "The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah, then did not carry it, is as the likeness of a donkey who carries volumes [of books]" (Surah al-Jumu'ah 62:5) — that is, books. And He said: "Take what We have given you with strength" (Surah al-Baqarah 2:63) — meaning: act upon what is in it. Do not content yourselves with the Sunnah by merely claiming it verbally without acting upon it, for claiming the Sunnah without acting upon it is a lie in speech coupled with the neglect of deed. And do not criticize innovations merely to adorn yourselves by pointing out their faults, for the corruption of the people of innovation does not add to your own righteousness. Nor should you criticize them out of transgression against their people, for transgression itself is corruption of your own souls. It is not fitting for a physician to treat the sick with what would cure them but would make him sick, for if he becomes sick, he becomes occupied with his own illness instead of treating them. Rather, he should seek health for himself so that he may be strong enough to treat the sick. So let your affair, in what you disapprove of concerning your brothers, be a matter of self-reflection for your own souls, sincere counsel to your Lord, and compassion toward your brothers. And let it be, along with that, that you are more concerned with your own faults than with the faults of others, that you wean one another toward sincere counsel, and that whoever offers it to you and whoever accepts it from you should be held in high regard by you.

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "May Allah have mercy on whoever presents me with my faults." You like to speak, and to have it tolerated from you, yet if the same were said to you as you say, you would become angry. You hold against people what you disapprove of in their affairs, yet you commit the very same—do you not wish, then, that the same standard be applied to you? Suspect your own opinion and the opinion of the people of your time. Establish certainty before you speak, and learn before you act, for a time will come in which truth and falsehood will become confused, in which what is good will be seen as evil, and what is evil will be seen as good. How many are those who seek nearness to Allah through what actually distances them from Him, and who seek His love through what actually earns His anger! Allah, exalted is He, said: "Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming to him so that he sees it as good...?" (Surah Fatir 35:8). So you must stop at doubtful matters until the clear truth becomes evident to you through clear proof, for whoever enters into what he does not know, without knowledge, is sinful. And whoever looks out for Allah's sake, Allah looks out for him. Hold fast to the Qur'an, follow it as your guide, and be led by it. And seek out the traces of those who came before you regarding it.

Had the rabbis and monks not feared the loss of their positions and the ruin of their standing by upholding the Book through their deeds and clarifying what they had distorted or concealed—but rather, when they contravened the Book through their deeds, they sought to deceive their people about what they had done, fearing that their positions would be ruined and that their corruption would become clear to the people—so they distorted the Book through [false] interpretation, and what they could not distort, they concealed. They kept silent about their own conduct in order to preserve their positions, and they kept silent about what their people did, in collusion with them. Yet Allah had taken a covenant from those given the Book: "You shall make it clear to mankind and not conceal it." Instead, they colluded regarding it and made things easy for their people concerning it.
sunan-darimi||1888:
(Marfu' Hadith) Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us: Hatim ibn Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them. Abu Ja'far said: We entered upon Jabir ibn Abdullah, and he asked about the people (present) until he reached me. I said: I am Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali. He then reached out with his hand to my upper button and my lower button, then placed his mouth between my breasts - and I was a young boy at that time - and said: "Welcome, O son of my brother, ask whatever you wish." So I asked him, and he was blind. The time for prayer came, so he stood up wrapped in a woolen cloak (sajah), and whenever he placed it on his shoulders, its edge would come back to him because of its smallness, while his outer garment was beside him on a clothes-rack. He then prayed. I said: Tell me about the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He gestured with his hand, counting nine, and said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, remained for nine years without performing Hajj. Then in the tenth year it was announced to the people that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was going to perform Hajj. So a great many people came to Madinah, all seeking to follow the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and to do as he did. We set out with him until we reached Dhul-Hulayfah, where Asma bint Umays gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them. She sent to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, asking: What should I do? He said: "Take a bath, tie a cloth around yourself (to stop the bleeding), and enter into the state of ihram." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, then prayed in the mosque, then mounted al-Qaswa, and when his camel stood with him on al-Bayda, I looked as far as my eyes could see, before him were riders and walkers, and to his right the same, and to his left the same, and behind him the same. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was among us, and the Qur'an was being revealed to him, and he knew its interpretation. He then raised his voice in the declaration of the oneness of Allah (tawhid): "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak." The people raised their voices with the same declaration they used to make, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did not object to any of it. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, continued his ttalbiyah until we came to the House with him.

Jabir said: We intended nothing but Hajj; we did not know about Umrah. When we came to the House with him, he touched the Corner (Black Stone), then he ran (performed ramal) for three circuits and walked for four. Then he went forward to the Station of Ibrahim and prayed, reciting: "And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer" (Surat al-Baqarah 2:125). He placed the Station between himself and the House. His father used to say - though I do not know if he attributed this to Jabir from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him - that he used to recite in the two rak'ahs: "Say, He is Allah, the One" and "Say, O disbelievers." Then he returned to the Corner and touched it. Then he went out through the gate to al-Safa. When he reached al-Safa, he recited: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah" (Surat al-Baqarah 2:158), [saying] "I begin with what Allah began with." So he began with al-Safa, ascending it until he could see the House. He then declared Allah's oneness and magnified Him, saying: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things capable. There is no god but Allah alone, He has fulfilled His promise, and given victory to His servant, and He alone defeated the confederates." Then he supplicated in between, saying this three times. Then he descended to al-Marwah, and when his feet reached the bottom of the valley -

Abdullah ibn Abdur-Rahman ad-Darimi said: meaning, he ran - until when we ascended he walked, until we reached al-Marwah. He did upon al-Marwah as he had done upon al-Safa. When it was the last circuit upon al-Marwah, he said: "If I had known beforehand what I know now, I would not have brought sacrificial animals, and I would have made it an Umrah. So whoever among you does not have a sacrificial animal with him, let him exit the state of ihram and make it an Umrah." Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, is this for this year only or forever? The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, interlaced his fingers together and said twice: "Umrah has entered into Hajj" - like this - "No, rather it is forever, forever."

Ali came bringing sacrificial camels from Yemen for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he found Fatimah, may Allah's pleasure be upon her, among those who had exited the state of ihram; she had put on dyed clothing and applied kohl. Ali objected to this on her part, but she said: My father commanded me to do so. Ali used to say: I went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to complain to him about Fatimah regarding what she had done, seeking a ruling from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning what she mentioned, for I had objected to it. He said: "She has spoken the truth. What did you say when you decided to enter Hajj?" I said: I said: O Allah, I intend what Your Messenger intends. He said: "Then I have the sacrificial animal with me, so do not exit ihram." Ali said: The total number of sacrificial animals that Ali brought from Yemen and that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, brought was one hundred camels. All the people exited ihram and cut their hair short, except the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and those who had sacrificial animals with them.

When it was the day of Tarwiyah, he set out for Mina, and we entered the state of ihram for Hajj. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, rode and prayed at Mina the Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr prayers. Then he waited a little while until the sun rose, and he ordered a tent of hair to be pitched for him at Namirah. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, rode, and he proceeded such that Quraysh had no doubt that he would stop at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, as Quraysh used to do in the pre-Islamic period at Muzdalifah. But the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, continued on until he reached Arafah, where he found the tent had been pitched at Namirah, and he stayed there until, when the sun had passed its zenith, he ordered al-Qaswa to be saddled for him. He then came to the bottom of the valley and addressed the people, saying: "Indeed your blood and your property are as sacred to you as the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. Indeed, everything from the affairs of the pre-Islamic period is abolished, placed beneath my feet. The blood of the pre-Islamic period is abolished, and the first blood I abolish among our own blood is the blood of Ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith, who was nursed among the Banu Sa'd and was killed by Hudhayl. And the usury of the pre-Islamic period is abolished, and the first usury I abolish is the usury of Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib, for it is all abolished. So fear Allah regarding women, for you have taken them as a trust from Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful for yourselves by the word of Allah. You have a right over them that they not allow anyone you dislike to tread your marriage beds; if they do that, then beat them with a beating that does not cause severe injury. And they have a right over you that you provide for them and clothe them in an appropriate manner. And you will be asked about me, so what will you say?" They said: We bear witness that you have conveyed the message, fulfilled your duty, and given sincere advice. He then raised his index finger to the sky and pointed it toward the people, saying: "O Allah, bear witness, O Allah, bear witness, O Allah, bear witness."

Then Bilal called the adhan once and the iqamah, and he prayed Zuhr. Then he called the iqamah again and prayed Asr, without praying anything between them. Then he rode until he stopped, positioning the belly of his camel al-Qaswa toward the rocky hillocks - Isma'il said: toward the small trees - and placing the path of the walkers before him. Then he faced the Qiblah and remained standing until the sun set and the yellow glow disappeared, until the disk of the sun had vanished. He then had Usamah ride behind him, then he set off, having tightened the rein of al-Qaswa such that her head would touch the front of his saddle, and he was saying with his right hand: "Calmness, calmness." Whenever he came to a rugged path, he would loosen it slightly for her until she ascended, until he reached Muzdalifah, where he prayed Maghrib and Isha with one adhan and two iqamahs. Then he lay down until, when dawn broke, he prayed Fajr with an adhan and an iqamah. Then he rode al-Qaswa until he stopped at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and faced the Qiblah, supplicating to Allah, magnifying Him, declaring His oneness and His singularity, until it became quite bright. Then he set off before the sun rose, having al-Fadl ibn Abbas ride behind him - and he was a man with beautiful hair, fair-skinned, and handsome. When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, set off, he passed by some women riding in litters, and al-Fadl began looking at them. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, took his hand and placed it over al-Fadl's face. Al-Fadl turned his head to the other side, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, placed his hand on the other side. When he reached Muhassir, he moved quickly for a short distance, then took the middle road that leads out to the largest Jamrah, until he reached the Jamrah near which there is a tree. He threw seven pebbles, saying "Allahu Akbar" with each pebble - pebbles the size for flicking - throwing from the bottom of the valley. Then he went to the place of sacrifice and slaughtered sixty-three camels with his own hand. Then he gave the rest to Ali, who slaughtered what remained, and he shared with him in his sacrificial animals. Then he ordered that a piece from each camel be taken and put into a pot and cooked, and they both ate from its meat and drank from its broth. Then he rode and proceeded to the House, coming to it and praying Zuhr in Makkah. He then went to the Banu Abdul-Muttalib, who were drawing water from Zamzam, and said: "Draw water, O Banu Abdul-Muttalib, for were it not that the people would overwhelm you regarding your right to provide water, I would draw water with you." So they handed him a bucket, and he drank.
